cards.note: REVIEW 2026-09-13 (drafts/kalshi-venue-dormancy-review-20260913.md, option A approved in-thread): the Kalshi leg has taken 0 trades since 2026-08-30 23:44 and 0 of 335 C-200 copies since the breaker cleared (Sep 5 08:39). Root cause is structural, not an outage: the venue gate (scripts/score-trades.ts:579-586) tests TWO stages of the same score — confidence = (pre-boost composite − 35)/65, so confidence > 0.8 requires a pre-boost composite ≥ 87.33, while copyScore ≥ 80 is read POST-boost and any sentiment-boosted score is clamped to 79 by regulatoryScoreCap (v34) — i.e. the two legs are mutually exclusive; the single qualifying candidate (Sep 12 23:52, conf 0.82) was blocked by the 79 < 80 clamp. v37 (activated 2026-08-31 04:58) is the semantic switch that killed the flow (pre-v37 confidence came from the post-boost score; 92 Kalshi trades landed in the 20 days before it). Compounding: 296/335 C-200 copies since Sep 5 are short-TTR lane copies whose confidence is hard-coded 0 (routing stays Polymarket). DECISION (option A): retire the copy-routing branch; Kalshi remains in the stack ONLY for Phase C cross-venue arb (phase-c) and the TR-16 adapter stays. Do NOT 'fix' this by restoring the pre-v37 semantics — that would route the 20 post-Sep-5 copies with copyScore ≥ 87.5, which are −$578.64 realized on Polymarket. SIDE FINDING (fold into the same change): premium-calibration venueOffsetKalshi (+0.328, refit 2026-09-01) was fitted on the phantom-priced Kalshi rows (all 73 closed rows bookedEntry = 0.50 exactly) and is added to λ̂ when sizing a Kalshi-routed copy (score-trades.ts:602, 682) — a bigger λ̂ means smaller size. Zero live impact while routing is dormant; recompute/retire the input as part of this card. Verify after implementation: `grep -c 'executionVenue = "Kalshi"' scripts/score-trades.ts` → 0, and `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM PaperTrade WHERE venue='Kalshi' AND openedAt > <impl-date>` → 0 (no new Kalshi-labelled rows).

PMA validation, LOW risk, shadow-lane first, flag-revertible); (2) fold the mcp-server confirmation-gate + SELL-reduces-by-min(order,pos)/no-position-SELL-adds-exposure semantics (MIT, concept-only, ~2–4h doc work) into the sidecar risk-gate spec. NOTHING ships before the Kelly window closes Oct 8 (precommit-mid-oct-kelly-gate). AUDIT INPUT (2026-09-08, user-queued post-Kelly; drafts/ccxt-audit.md): multi-venue quote data backbone = **ccxt** (MIT; Polymarket+Kalshi+Hyperliquid coverage verified 2026-09-08) — adopt for arb quote breadth + perp-funding/OHLCV feature lane; do NOT churn existing bespoke CLOB/data-api/Kalshi read lanes. AUDIT INPUT (2026-09-09, user-approved carding; drafts/poly-maker-audit.md): warproxxx/poly-maker (MIT, Python, 1.5k★, 111/111 tests) is a maker-only MM bot whose core is the INTRA-VENUE half of this card — a YES+NO pair merged back to collateral locks edge 1−p−q. Two borrows for the design window (Sep 15–30): (1) the CTF pair-merge primitive — mergePositions across EOA / Gnosis Safe / V2 DepositWallet via the gasless builder relayer, nonce-serialized, LIVE-VERIFIED on-chain (tx 0x4d2a2064) — gives zero-market-impact exits AND makes the Polymarket-only YES+NO≠1 leg buildable WITHOUT any Kalshi dependency, sidestepping the phase-kalshi1 keyless data wall (our sidecar already reads top-of-book keyless); (2) reward-band quoting (half-spread clamped into rewardsMaxSpread, per-ORDER min qualifying size, both legs bid so both sides score) as the maker counterfactual to our taker entries — see drafts/c200-taker-fee-measurement-2026-09-09.md (fee = C×rate×p(1−p); politics 0.04; maker rebate 25%). Port cost: read ≈½ day, dry-run port ≈ 2–3 days (cost is wallet-type signing + builder-relayer creds, not logic); ship as a manual CLI primitive first, flag-revertible. CAVEAT: the repo's own live session LOST $15.51 — the maker-lane strategy is an unproven hypothesis; the merge primitive is the part worth taking.

Dual-feed: keyless legacy DOC API (http only; https hangs; 1 req/5s; no per-article tone — uses timelinetone category aggregates) + GDELT Cloud ACTIVE 2026-09-01 (gdeltcloud.com/api/v2, stories w/ significance/geo/entities; GDELT_API_KEY in .env perms 600; NOTE: cloud API flaky on cold calls — 4x retry w/ 10s backoff in collector). AUDIT INPUT (2026-09-18, user-requested audit; drafts/trendradar-audit.md): sansan0/TrendRadar (62.4k*, GPL-3.0 -> read-only: separate service or reimplement concepts, copy NO code) is a multi-platform hot-list + RSS aggregator whose one genuinely missing primitive for THIS lane is per-item attention *time series*: news_items(first_crawl_time/last_crawl_time/crawl_count, unique on (url,platform_id)) + rank_history(rank,crawl_time) + title_changes(old,new). Its attention score (core/analyzer.py:17) is 0.6*mean(11-min(rank,10))*10 + 0.3*min(count,10)*10 + 0.1*(high_rank_frac)*100 — three normalised 0-100 terms, hand-set weights, NO recency decay, saturating at rank 10 / count 10, and the same math is duplicated 3x in-repo (analyzer.py:136, loader.py:170, mcp_server/tools/analytics.py:36); repo ships NO test suite. FIT: (a) a salience ROUTER for the measured A2 reach problem (sentiment touches 0.08% of decisions, 148/191k) — trending topics + keyword groups used to FIND markets that deserve an evidence look, which is a coverage fix, not new alpha; (b) attention/corroboration features (sources_agreeing, best_rank, persistence_hours) as an EVIDENCE-CONFIDENCE modifier, NEVER a price delta — an uncalibrated heuristic in copyScore would repeat the thesisScore failure (component AUC 0.27-0.36 inside a composite measuring 0.41). PROPOSAL (shadow-first, same post-B wiring gate as the rest of this lane): step 0 run it as a SEPARATE Docker service pointed at OUR feeds (RSS enabled by default, feedparser, keyword groups + [GLOBAL_FILTER]); step 1 tiny read-only reader -> data/attention-shadow.jsonl in OUR schema {ts, topic_key, url, sources[], best_rank, crawl_count, persistence_hours, first_seen} (no GPL code enters the repo); step 2 measure coverage lift AND whether attention spikes lead price drift beyond the price-only baseline (market-clustered CI, time-ordered + era-aware splits per the ML-doctrine card) — expected null is that attention is already in the price, so only a minutes-to-hours lead or a routing gain counts; step 3 only if step 2 lifts -> A2 evidence-tier input, flag-revertible. Point-in-time caveat: it cannot backfill, so a first read needs 2-4 weeks of forward accumulation. NOT PORTABLE: litellm AI layer (we run DeepSeek + local Ollama), notification senders (no Discord; we use Hermes cron -> Discord), Chinese-platform scrapers, HTML report generator, boto3 remote sync, its MCP server as a dependency. DESIGN (2026-09-18, option C outcome; drafts/attention-lead-test-design-20260918.md): pre-execution design for the news->price lead test, with the feasibility measured rather than assumed. TWO FINDINGS THAT RESHAPE THE PLAN: (1) the blocking gap is NOT a missing service — the GDELT Cloud API already returns processed_at / updated_at ISO timestamps and our collector DISCARDS both, storing only story_date (day granularity); storing two fields turns the feed into a timestamped event stream, and the legacy DOC feed already carries a 15-min seendate. (2) The test is FEE-limited, not power-limited: MDE ~ 2.8*sigma/sqrt(N) means 300 events buy only ~0.6pt, while the Polymarket taker fee is ~2% of notional PER SIDE at p=0.5 (rate 4%) — so the pre-registered primary criterion is fee-NET edge on a held-out window, not a p-value, and the most promising variant is hold-to-resolution (one entry fee) with TTR >= 24h. PRICE RESOLUTION GRID (measured, keyless CLOB prices-history, requires a browser UA or it 403s): 60-second bars for the trailing 1h/6h/24h; 10-minute bars back 31 days (interval=1m demands fidelity>=10; interval=max is clamped to 10-min); interval=1w minimum fidelity 5. So 1-min resolution exists ONLY for the last 24h — any longer retrospective runs at 10-min and h must be >= 30 min. L2 cross-check corpus: 28,710 assets / 7.45GB since 2026-08-31, 5s book snapshots, but MAX_MARKETS=25 concurrent (universe = observed trades in last 2h = OUR pipeline's attention; ~2,344 assets/24h rotating) -> prices-history is the primary source and L2 only a biased-subsample cross-check. DATA-INTEGRITY FLAG: 0 trade prints in 1,200 sampled L2 files (the stated raw material for the fill-probability model) — investigate before that work depends on it. STAGES: 0 plumbing (~30min: store the two timestamps + entity types, log the assetId<->marketId map, record the UA requirement) -> 1 matcher + yield (~1 day, entity->market matcher with the house ambiguity doctrine, 50-row hand-labelled precision audit; GO/NO-GO: >=15 matched events/day and >=85% precision) -> 2 event study (~1-2 days: matched-control abnormal return in fee units, market-clustered CIs, time-ordered split, A1-A4 acceptance) -> 3 feature upgrade + A2 wiring (post-Oct-8, TrendRadar rank-persistence/corroboration only if the base effect is non-zero). Stages 0-2 are MEASUREMENT-only (shadow files, no live path) so they do NOT wait for the Oct 8 window; only stage 3 does. SEQUENCING CORRECTION to the TrendRadar audit: the lead test does not need TrendRadar to start. STAGE 0+1 RESULT (2026-09-18, user-approved stage 0+1; drafts/attention-yield-report-20260918.md): **GATE K1 FAILS — do not proceed to stage 2.** YIELD: 1,702 news rows over 10 collection-days against a 24,259-question market universe (auto-generated families removed first: 38.8% of all questions are daily temperature ladders) -> ladder 1,509 stories share >=1 token with a market, 1,423 of those die at the ambiguity cap (entity matches >3 markets), 86 survive the cap, 4 survive the full rule (live window + TTR>=24h + price in (0.02,0.98)) = 0.4 events/day vs the >=15/day gate; the most generous entity-anchored variant still yields <=8.6/day. PRECISION 0/4 vs the >=85% gate (matched on common nouns: 'Election'+'city' -> Hsinchu mayoral market; Ontario trustee election -> Hamilton mayoral market; UK oil-and-gas tax story -> 'Republican Party win the House'; similarity fallback at overlap>=0.20 buys 3.7/day of the same garbage). MECHANISM (the real finding): the two vocabularies intersect on THEMES, not PROPOSITIONS — our six standing queries surface mega-entities (Trump 74 stories, Federal Reserve 43, OpenAI 36, EU 16, Bitcoin 10) that each match hundreds of live markets, while the market side is generic-vocabulary dominated ('win' in 7,087 questions, 'election' 3,275). Theme-shaped news does not entail a proposition-shaped market. KNOWN FLAWS IN MY MATCHER (recorded, verdict robust): entity fallback admitted common nouns, and the ambiguity cap was applied post-filter instead of at entity level. SHIPPED IN STAGE 0 (kept, independent of the outcome): gdelt_shadow.py now stores processed_at/updated_at + typed entities (verified live: the feed is now a timestamped event stream instead of day-granularity), record-l2.ts now logs data/l2-asset-map.jsonl (the DB has NO token ids — ObservedTrade.rawTradeJson is '{}' for all 283,154 rows), and prices-history's browser-UA requirement + resolution grid (60s bars for trailing 1h/6h/24h; 10-min bars back 31 days) is documented. RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP (NOT carded — needs user approval as a new work item): INVERT the direction. Market -> news: extract the specific proposition entities from each live market question (candidate/person/team/city/bill) with the tennis-matcher ambiguity doctrine, query GDELT per entity, then test 'does coverage intensity on a market's own proposition lead its price?' That direction has a high-precision map by construction, and it is where TrendRadar's per-entity rank/persistence series would actually earn its place. → INVERTED LANE CARDED (2026-09-18, user-approved): the failure of the forward direction is addressed by market-to-news-lead-test (entity from the market question → per-entity news coverage intensity → lead test), which carries the pre-registered Stage A/B gate. cards.note: DECISION 2026-10-10 (approved in-thread): **the gate is DROPPED, no gate ships.** The measurement killed the design's premise: the population it was approved to block ([0.20,0.60) with confidence <0.80) is +$336.45 over 917 legs of POSITIVE cash, and the only ~dead slice (0.40-0.60, n=644) is -$8.37, i.e. already zero without any gate — so blocking it buys ~nothing and costs a rule. The design's own PASS slice (conf >=0.80 in-band, n=11) is the only part with positive excess (+16.7pp) and would have been let through anyway. Nothing is blocked, no rule ships, no live path changes; the band evidence remains on `v60-bandhalf-era-review` for the 0.60-0.80 half. MEASURED 2026-10-10 at the freeze thaw (C-200, deduped by market+outcome, in-window since 2026-09-06) — the approved design would REMOVE POSITIVE CASH, so it should not be applied as written. [0.20,0.60) by confidence: conf>=0.80 (PASSES) n=11 +$20.25 win 63.6% excess +16.7pp | conf 0.70-0.80 (BLOCKED) n=72 +$113.17 excess -4.3pp | conf<0.70 (BLOCKED) n=845 +$223.28 excess -0.5pp. The blocked population is +$336.45 over 917 legs. Band split, same window: 0.20-0.40 n=275 **+$416.73** | 0.40-0.60 n=644 **-$8.37** (win 46.4%) — so the dead half is 0.40-0.60 (as pre-registered, mid-band ~0) while 0.20-0.40 carries real cash, and the design blocks BOTH. USER PICK: (a) narrow the gate to [0.40,0.60) unless confidence >= 0.80 [RECOMMENDED], (b) apply as designed (blocking 0.20-0.60) and accept the measured -$336 cost, (c) drop the gate and keep the band un-gated. Nothing applied.

cards.title: Finding — the shared 20:00 ET blackout blocks a STANDARD-POSITIVE hour (+$887.61 / 252 rows)

Control at 08:00 ET (the hour that IS C-200-only, so STANDARD trades there): all-time +$906.77 / 271 legs COLLAPSES to -$93.69 / 16 legs post-v52. Artifact: drafts/blackout-2000-et-standard-20261011.md
cards.gate: Findings-only until the Oct 8 window close (window purity). Post-close: gate if STANDARD 20:00 stays positive on a post-v52 slice with n >= 40.
cards.note:
The v44 decision applied the 20:00 ET blackout to BOTH books on the claim that the hour 'cost STANDARD too (window-opened −$622 worst on record)'. All-time Polymarket-only at 20:00 ET: C-200 31 rows −$80.43 (correctly gated) but STANDARD 252 rows +$887.61. Same for 08:00 (STANDARD +$1,048.17), which is why Change 1 shipped C-200-only. The STANDARD figure includes pre-v44 and pre-v52 mechanics, so this is a re-test item, not a revert: slice it post-v52 before touching the gate. Verify: sqlite3 prisma/dev.db "SELECT botId, COUNT(*), ROUND(SUM(realizedPnl),2) FROM PaperTrade WHERE status IN ('resolved','closed') AND realizedPnl IS NOT NULL AND isDemo=0 AND venue!='Kalshi' AND CAST(strftime('%H',openedAt/1000,'unixepoch','-4 hours') AS INT)=20 AND openedAt >= strftime('%s','2026-09-06')*1000 GROUP BY botId;"

| VERDICT 2026-10-11: **CLOSED AS NULL / PREMISE INVALID.** Plus a LABEL-BASIS reversal the card never had: on the market-outcome arm (didOutcomeWin / OutcomeReview.finalOutcome) the same 261 legs read 63 won +$399.36 | 48 lost -$571.06 | 150 undeterminable = **-$171.70 on the 111 labelable legs - OPPOSITE in sign** to the +$898.33 realizedPnl headline, which is carried mostly by the 150 rows whose market outcome the DB cannot name. So the 'STANDARD-positive hour' was an exit-policy artifact on a one-day, one-market sample, and it cannot be re-measured because the gate that would produce the population is the one blocking STANDARD. REOPEN ONLY IF someone proposes un-gating STANDARD at 20:00 ET: that is a rule change needing its own pre-registered trial (bounded window, n>=40, BOTH label arms printed, per-day concentration stated), and this evidence does not support proposing it. Timezone note for any future read: the '-4 hours' ET conversion is valid only while DST holds - after 2026-11-01 it must be '-5 hours' - and the UTC basis selects a DIFFERENT hour (20:00 UTC = 16:00 ET: n=482 / -$245.60, not comparable).

RESULTS (exit-blind, held to resolution; market-clustered bootstrap): whole skip set edge/sh -0.0093 CI [-0.0313,+0.0110] ($-0.09 per $10) -> the gates are NOT leaking money on average. Pre-live v1-v48: -0.0205 CI [-0.0481,+0.0091]. LIVE v49+: +0.0159 CI [+0.0026,+0.0308] ($+0.16 per $10) -> in the running regime the skipped set is slightly positive-EV, CI excludes 0. Best pocket: v49+ AND 0.50<=price<0.65 -> +0.1199/sh CI [+0.0362,+0.2085] ($+1.20 per $10, n=1,886, 646 markets, top-3 markets only 14% of rows); win rate 69.6% vs mean price 56.4% (+13pp). Near-certainty 0.95-1.00 is a tight small positive: +0.0087 CI [+0.0061,+0.0110] (n=36,082). 0.65-0.80 is the worst band: -0.1008 CI [-0.2624,+0.0567]. RANKERS within the skips (AUC vs won, n=77k): copyScore 0.408, thesis 0.268, copyability 0.423, roi 0.475, liquidity 0.476, timing 0.479, confidence 0.500, category fit 0.509, spread 0.534, wallet quality 0.543, consistency 0.599 (best component), entry price 0.932. => the 77k labels are a strong TEST set but the stored feature vector carries almost no ranking information beyond price; a model on these features mostly relearns the market. Live-regime wallet pockets (>=150 labelled skips, no CI, discovery window): 0x85f031d069de3000 +0.212/sh n=294; 0xe0e637b08c971c2f +0.127 n=215; 0xc5187cb669690150 +0.032 n=5,592; 0xb0c85813a7a4428f +0.007 n=13,755 (carries most of the volume at ~zero). CAVEAT: skip side is exit-blind (hold to resolution); live copies also face the exit rules, and status='closed' early exits are excluded from the copy comparison (resolved-only is winner-enriched) - the two sides are not directly comparable. Named-token legs (25.6% of skip rows) are NOT labelled: the snapshot proxy cannot map non-YES/NO labels without the venue's token names.

--- REPLICATION FAILED 2026-10-22 (see card ml1b-band-readmission-test). Re-labelled with VENUE TRUTH over 15,218 legs / 3,657 markets the pocket reads +0.0012/share, CI [-0.0473, +0.0481] -> zero. The +0.1199/sh pocket quoted on this card is an in-sample artifact of the snapshot >=0.98/<=0.02 resolution rule and the card's filters; it should not be quoted as evidence in future work.

cards.dates: Promoted 2026-09-20 (tuning review #31 rec 4, user-approved) · helper + doc when ML-1 fit work starts | IMPLEMENTED 2026-10-11 (user-approved work: 'proceed' on 1->2): shared helper SHIPPED in BOTH languages - src/lib/splits.ts (canonical: timeOrderedHoldout with a pinned boundary + purge + era provenance, walkForward, blockedFolds, eraGroups, crc32/assignBlockedFold, formatProvenance) and scripts/lib/splits.py (stdlib-only mirror, same rules), with tests/splits.test.ts (15 tests) and scripts/check-split-doctrine.py as the ENFORCEMENT. Detection finds 5 owners (the guess named 8; 3 of its entries have no fold logic at all, while 2 real owners were missing from it). MIGRATED, behaviour-preserving: fit-fill-model.py (legacy sha256 holdout kept via splits.keyed_holdout(hasher='sha256') so the published U1 read cannot move), pilot-score-separation.py and pilot-score-separation-papers.py (market-blocked 5-fold + inner 3-fold), and fit-price-edge.py's last inline inner fold. PROOF: over the scripts' REAL inputs (7,910 rows / 3,473 markets and 11,219 / 3,591, read through their own SQL and filters) the old and new fold arrays are element-identical, 75,000 fuzz strings agree at k=2,3,5,7,10, and a full re-run of fit-price-edge.py reproduces data/score-spec-v1*.json with ONLY created_at/generated_at moved (published copies restored, so no timestamp churn landed). shadow-expectancy-model.py is deliberately NOT migrated and now says why in code: its per-row purge is STRICTER than the shared walk-forward, and its artifact (data/shadow-score-model.json) is read by the live kalshi-shadow lane, so an equivalent-but-not-identical re-implementation would silently rescore a live lane. Checker teeth tested red/green: inline crc32 arithmetic, a sklearn KFold import and an unaccounted owner each FAIL with exit 1. Write-up: :3013/drafts/ml1-fold-migration-20261011
cards.gate:
One shared split utility (time-ordered holdout + ruleSetVersion era handling) used by every fit/eval script in scripts/; any report whose folds are random rows is rejected. Precedent to reuse: the fold designs already pre-registered in scripts/fit-price-edge.py (wallet-blocked + walk-forward). PROMOTED 2026-09-20: the export half is DONE (training_data.csv now carries ruleSetVersion, era, decision_at, simulated_pnl), so what remains is the shared split helper + the short doc. Verify 7d: every fit/eval script in scripts/ uses the helper (no random-row folds), and a report quoting a metric names its era and its time order.

PARTIALLY MET 2026-10-11 - and the finding is that the PREMISE was partly wrong: no fit script in scripts/ was using random row folds (verified repo-wide; the two designs already existed inline in fit-price-edge.py, and shadow-expectancy-model.py already purges). What was missing was ONE shared implementation plus machine enforcement, both of which now exist. Enforcement is real, not prose: `python3 scripts/check-split-doctrine.py` FAILS on any KFold/StratifiedKFold/ShuffleSplit/train_test_split/cross_val_score/cross_validate in scripts/ AND fails if the Python fold assignment disagrees with the TS crc32 pins (0x85f031d069de3000 -> fold 4, 0xe0e637b08c971c2f -> fold 3). PASS state today: 0 violations, 8 migration warnings. STILL OPEN: the 7 owners above must import the helper, and `fit-price-edge.py` must keep reproducing its spec - both are the card's own 7d verify.

MET 2026-10-11 (migration half): every fold owner in scripts/ is now accounted for by machine detection - 4 on the shared helper, 1 justified inline (shadow-expectancy-model.py, stricter per-row purge), 0 unaccounted; `python3 scripts/check-split-doctrine.py` exits 0 and prints the count. One enforcement hole was found and closed while writing the rule: a pattern that cannot see NESTED parens misses `zlib.crc32(r['market'].encode()) % K_FOLDS`, i.e. exactly the shape the rule bans - the shipped pattern and its regression probe both use the nested-call form. 7d verify clock starts 2026-10-11 (re-verify on/after 2026-10-18: checker still exits 0 with 0 unaccounted owners, and no report quoting a metric omits its era and its time order).
cards.note:
The current label set spans ruleSetVersion 1-53 with 63% of rows from v1-v3 (v2 alone = 488) while the live policy is v54; the feature vector contains policy outputs, so era mixing teaches the average of ~50 policies. The skip probe adds 77k more rows ACROSS eras, so the problem gets worse, not better (in the probe: pre-live skips -0.0199/sh vs live-regime skips +0.0159/sh - a sign flip by era that a pooled model would average away). MEASURED 2026-09-20 (this is why the era split matters, not just doctrine): the export's own per-era breakdown reads pre-kelly-v1-48 n=1,855 60.2% good avg +$0.22 | kelly-window-v49-57 n=782 44.9% good avg -$0.24 | exposure-v58plus n=1. The era the live policy ran in is the WORST cohort on good-rate and the only negative-avg one, while the retired era looks best — a random-row fold would average them and report the retirement as the improvement. eraOf() boundaries (documented in scripts/export-training-data.ts): v<49 pre-kelly-v1-48, v49-57 kelly-window, v>=58 exposure-v58plus; unversioned rows stay 'unknown'.

WHAT THE HELPER ENFORCES, with the measured reason each rule exists: (1) TIME ORDER with a PINNED boundary - a fraction-derived cut moves as the book grows and a bar on a moving holdout is not a bar; (2) PURGE on the label timestamp - on the bar population that is 148 train rows that settled INSIDE the test window, i.e. training on the future; (3) ERA PROVENANCE per split, because the era read INVERTS between artifacts (pre-kelly 58.8% win / +$0.338 vs exposure-v58plus 42.7% / +$6.060) and a pooled fold averages that away; (4) one fold numbering across languages (zlib crc32 pinned in both test suites), so a fold quoted in a TS read is reproducible in Python. The helper deliberately offers NO shuffled/random-fold function: bootstrap RESAMPLING (clustered) stays legitimate and lives in src/lib/metrics.ts, and the ban is specifically on random folds for model selection.

cards.title: Market→news lead test — does coverage intensity on a market's OWN proposition lead its price? (inverted salience lane)
cards.effort: ~1-1.5 days to the go/no-go (entity extractor + matcher + coverage builder + precision audit); ~1-2 days more for the event study only if the gate passes
cards.dates: Carded 2026-09-18 (user-approved) after the forward news→market test failed K1 (drafts/attention-yield-report-20260918.md)
cards.gate: PRE-REGISTERED, two stages. STAGE A (map quality, decides everything): (1) entity extraction precision ≥85% on a hand-labelled 50-market sample — the map must be high-precision BY CONSTRUCTION, so verify it rather than assume it; extractor returns None rather than guessing (tennis-matcher doctrine: both-sides-must-agree, ±date bonus, ambiguity margin); (2) coverage reach ≥20 markets/day with a resolved entity map AND ≥5 news items per market per week — an intensity test needs repeated observations, unlike the single-event test that just failed. STAGE B (the measurement, only if A passes): (A1) coverage-intensity change leads price beyond the price-only baseline on a time-ordered holdout (70/30); (A2) market-clustered bootstrap 95% CI excludes 0; (A3) no single entity family contributes >20% of the effect; (A4) survives the matched-control market baseline and ±event-time jitter. KILLS: precision <85% → stop; coverage <5 items/market/week → stop (nothing to measure); sign flip on the holdout → stop.
cards.note: WHY INVERTED: the forward direction was measured and failed — 1,702 news rows over 10 collection-days matched to a 24,259-question market universe produced 0.4 events/day (gate ≥15) and 0/4 precision (gate ≥85%), because the two vocabularies intersect on THEMES, not PROPOSITIONS: our six standing GDELT queries surface mega-entities (Trump 74 stories, Federal Reserve 43, OpenAI 36, EU 16, Bitcoin 10) that each match hundreds of live markets, while the market side is generic-vocabulary dominated ('win' in 7,087 questions). 94% of candidate stories died at the ambiguity cap. DESIGN: start from the market list — the only side whose subjects ARE propositions. (1) Extract the specific proposition entities from each live market question (candidate, person, team, city, bill, bill-number) with the tennis-matcher ambiguity doctrine; (2) query GDELT Cloud per entity (q=<entity>, keyed, we already have the collector) to build a per-market coverage-intensity time series (items/day, article_count sum, significance-weighted); (3) test whether a CHANGE in coverage intensity leads the market's price, controlling for the market's own drift with a matched control market. ALREADY IN PLACE from the failed test's stage 0 (reusable, verified live): the news feed is now a TIMESTAMPED event stream (processed_at/updated_at + typed name/type/wiki entities in gdelt_shadow.py, verified landing 2026-09-18), data/l2-asset-map.jsonl is live (25 markets mapped at recorder start; the DB has NO token ids — ObservedTrade.rawTradeJson is '{}' for all 283,154 rows), scripts/attention-match.py carries the reusable token-index/snapshot machinery, and the price side is characterised: CLOB prices-history is keyless but 403s without a browser UA, 60-second bars for the trailing 1h/6h/24h and 10-minute bars back 31 days (so any lead test at h<30min must run in the trailing 24h window or off the L2 corpus). HONEST EXPECTATION: for many markets the causal arrow runs price→news (a story written ABOUT the move), so the pre-registered null is contemporaneity — a positive result must show coverage LEADING price on the holdout, not merely correlating with it, and the exclude-list for market-derived domains (polymarket|kalshi|betting|odds) stays. TRENDRADAR'S PLACE: its per-entity rank/persistence time series is exactly the coverage-intensity measure this design needs (GDELT article_count only approximates it) — but it is a STAGE-B-BEYOND feature, worth standing up only if the simpler GDELT coverage series shows signal first. Measurement-only through Stage A; nothing touches the live scorer.

The only concentration rail that existed was v55's per-market ceiling, and it is now MEASURED non-binding (10 blocks, all 2026-09-18 08:36-08:52 at the pre-growth $125.12 ceiling; 0 since the cap rose to $1,734.50; max 2 legs/marketId) — the precondition #29 set for adding the wallet half. MECHANICS: `maxWalletNotionalPctOfCap` 0 -> 0.25, C-200 only, evaluated on the FINAL size in the same per-leg loop as v55, ceiling = 0.25 x effective cap so it scales with the equity-linked cap ($435.09 on the $1,740.34 cap at apply). Blocked legs log `[BANKROLL_200] v58 per-wallet cap (…)` and journal the same reason on the decision row. FREEZE: a new threshold is a rule change and the Kelly window (Sep 8-Oct 8) is pre-registered as no-rule-change — this ships on the user's explicit override for cause (approved 2026-09-19), classification recorded in scripts/apply-v58-wallet-cap.ts. Revert: set the field back to 0 via a new apply script (legacy semantics). BASIS FIX (v59, 2026-09-20): the rec as shipped measured the ceiling against the wallet's WHOLE open notional, so the wallet that was already above it was frozen OUTRIGHT — 109 vetoed legs in the first 15 h (1–4 per cycle) while it held $993.66 against a $430.97 ceiling (2.29x), with entries falling 43 (pre-activation morning) → 7. The daily report's rec 2 offered grandfathering vs raising pct to 0.40; 0.40 is VOID as a fix (ceiling $693.80 < the $993.66 stock, so the wallet stays frozen and merely unwinds ~$300 sooner), so the basis shipped as `walletCapBasis:"delta"` with a frozen per-wallet snapshot in data/wallet-cap-baseline.json (11 wallets / $1,295.80 at activation): ceiling(wallet) = baseline + 0.25 x cap — a wallet keeps its book and may add at most one ceiling of NEW notional, which is what 'gate new accumulation only' means. Revert: walletCapBasis "stock" (legacy), or the pct field to 0 (off). VERIFICATION 2026-10-10 (nothing changed by it). The audit's own numbers: C-200 open book $312.95 over 24 rows / 6 wallets, top-1 58.3%, top-3 97.4% — the ceiling is grandfathered on the STOCK, so a small open book still shows the stock's concentration; the read that answers "is it concentrating again" is wallet-cap-shadow-lane's re-read trigger (~$993 wallet). Clause 2 is not a pass: no post-v59 veto has occurred in 20 days, so the basis-delta string has never had a chance to appear. If the ceiling ever blocks again, that string is what to grep first.

cards.title: DECISION (pre-committed) — exit exemption for 0.20–0.40: extended read + decision rule
cards.effort: already instrumented (analyzer --band-min shipped); read is one command
cards.dates: Rule pre-committed 2026-09-20 (daily report rec 1b, user-approved) · re-read weekly or when a horizon bucket reaches 20 priced tickets
cards.gate: PRE-COMMITTED DECISION RULE (binding, 2026-09-20): an exit exemption ships for a band ONLY IF, on that band's own sample, (1) hold-to-horizon PnL at the PRE-NAMED horizon beats the realized PnL of the cut tickets, on a bucket with >=20 PRICED tickets (the existing guarantee rule — no exceptions), AND (2) the direction also holds in the all-time arm, AND (3) >=20 decisions were cut in the band. Pre-named horizons: 24h for 0.20–0.40 (short/medium-lived positions), 72h for <0.20 (long-dated). Failing the count test means EXTEND THE CLOCK, never 'decide on the near-miss'.
cards.note: READ 2026-09-20 (the Change-2 clock's due date) — NO EXEMPTION SHIPS. Command: `DATABASE_URL="file:./dev.db?immutable=1" npx tsx scripts/analyze-band-exit-exemption.ts --since 2026-09-13 [--band-min 0.20 --band-max 0.40]`. cards.title: v60 — halve new size in the 0.60–0.80 band (band-scoped factor; the named overlay flag was a no-op)
cards.effort: ~2h (field + pure helper + tests + apply script + the recon that redirected the mechanism)
cards.dates: Applied 2026-09-21 08:4x CDT (2026-09-20 C-200 daily report change 1, user-approved) | VERIFIED 2026-10-10 (7d gate was 2026-09-28): the target band is confirmed changed and HELD — [0.60,0.80) C-200 opens average $2.48 in the v60 7d (n=18) and $2.48 in the most recent 7d (n=21) vs the $4.90 / n=87 baseline, and 58 `[BAND-SIZE]` lines exist, every one `band=0.6-0.8 factor=0.5` -> clauses 1-2 met. Clause 3 ("no other band's average size moves") is FALSE as written: 0.00-0.20 $40.03->$42.12, 0.20-0.40 $16.78->$10.94, 0.40-0.60 $2.06->$1.18 — and the cause is NOT this change: src/lib/band-size.ts:40-45 admits only 0.60<=price<0.80 and the log confirms it, so v60's factor cannot reach those bands. The movement is a size-MIX shift inside them (0.40-0.60: the $4.99/$2.49 base tiers mostly vanish while the $1.25 tier stays the mode and $0.62 appears = the high per-leg base sizes stopped being booked), in the same window that v58/v59 (per-wallet ceiling, 2026-09-19/20) and v61 (copy-eligible universe, 2026-09-22) landed. Gate closed with that correction stated; a single named cause for the residual needs its own instrument
cards.gate: VERIFY 7d (2026-09-28): C-200 opens with entry in [0.6, 0.8) average ≈ $2.45 instead of $4.90 (7d baseline 87 opens / $426.38 / avg $4.90 / realized −$3.84) and `grep -c '\[BAND-SIZE\]' logs/cron/copybot-monitor-score.log` > 0 with the factor logged as 0.5. No other band's average size moves (0.00–0.20 avg $40.03, 0.20–0.40 $16.78, 0.40–0.60 $2.06 at the same read).
cards.note: WHY the mechanism changed: the rec proposed flipping `premiumOverlayEnabled 0 → 1` (k=0.5) 'scoped to 0.60–0.80'. The v38 overlay resizes only `!kellySized && lane !== "short_ttr"` copies, and EVERY copy in that band is a short-TTR lane copy — measured 7d: 87 opens, 84 at exactly $4.99 (= fixed lane size × the 0.5 band map), zero Kelly admits (Kelly refuses λ̂>0 bands). So the flag would have changed nothing in the target band and would have BOOSTED the <0.20 band by 1.39× (λ̂=−0.789) — the tail-variance increase the same report argues against. Its k=0.5 factor also computes to 0.893 (−10.7%), not the headline's −50%. The delta shipped where it binds: `c200BandSizeFactor` 0.5 scoped by `c200BandSizeFactorRange` "0.6-0.8" on the FINAL size, whatever lane booked it (applied after Kelly/lane sizing, before the v55/v58 concentration gates so those measure the booked size). src/lib/band-size.ts (pure, 8 tests) · tests/band-size.test.ts · scripts/apply-v60-premium-band-half.ts (per-band consequence, --dry-run writes nothing). EVIDENCE: band excess −0.0995, z=−3.96, N=382; cash +$2.66 over 30d on $1,015 of flow while absorbing a third of the day's new positions; 7d notional halves $426.38 → $213.19. REVERT: c200BandSizeFactor 1 (or the range ""). VERIFIED 2026-10-10 (7d gate was 2026-09-28). Clauses 1-2 met exactly as pre-registered ($4.90 -> $2.48, factor logged as 0.5 on the band). Clause 3 disproved, and the disproof is the useful part: the band factor is band-scoped by construction (parseBandRange/applyBandSizeFactor reject anything outside [lo,hi) and all 58 log lines carry the target band), so the other bands' moves are a POPULATION effect, not a leak. Evidence of the shape: in 0.40-0.60 the same wallets booked $4.99/$2.49/$1.25 in the baseline and $1.25/$0.62 after — the top size tiers went rare rather than every leg halving, which is a cap/base effect. Candidate causes in the same window are v58/v59's grandfather-basis change (the per-wallet ceiling starts allocating at the new basis 2026-09-20 04:40) and v61's copy-eligible universe change (2026-09-22); both change which legs get booked and at what size. Nothing was changed by this verification, and the gate's own assumption (a stable size distribution across bands during the window) is what failed.

cards.title: Rec 1 — one monitor sweep per cycle + CONCURRENCY 4→2 (429s back after 6 clean windows)

cards.gate: VERIFY 7d (2026-09-28): `grep -c 'Too Many Requests' logs/cron/copybot-monitor-score.log` = 0 over the window (baseline 10 across 7 of 109 runs) AND the monitor's median gap stays ≤ 14.0 m (baseline 13.0 m). Both are read from the run headers + 429 lines, no new instrument.
cards.note: WHY: the runner ran monitor:trades TWICE per cycle and the 24h lookback made the second sweep pure duplicate load — it re-fetched the same window and every fill hit ObservedTrade's unique constraint. The second call's `API_DELAY_MS=100` was ALSO inert: monitor-trades never reads API_DELAY_MS (only src/lib/dead-market-resolution.ts does), so both calls issued identical requests at identical pacing. Cost: 10 data-api `/activity` 429s across 7 of 109 runs, ending a 6-window clean streak, with the pool at CONCURRENCY 4 (the pool IS the burst width — API_DELAY_MS paces pagination INSIDE one wallet, not across wallets). Fix: delete the duplicate sweep (a fill landing mid-cycle is still inside the next cycle's 24h window, so nothing is lost) and set the pool to `MONITOR_CONCURRENCY` default 2. The run is no longer the cadence bind (13.0 m median against a 10 m schedule), so trading burst width for API headroom is the right side of that trade. Revert: re-add the second `npm run --silent monitor:trades` line / set MONITOR_CONCURRENCY=4.

MEASURED 2026-09-22: 968 → 6,455 detected rows/24h (971 copy-eligible + 5,484 observation), distinct markets 243 → 2,212, wallets 16 → 33, copies since 14:30 = 0, DecisionJournal rows since 14:30 = 12 (exactly the 6+6 copy-eligible rows scored), cadence unchanged at 11.0 min (14:19:13 → 14:30:13 → 14:41:13), 0 new 429s. cards.effort: ~1h (1 nullable column + ordering/stamp helpers + 4 DB-backed tests)
cards.dates: Applied 2026-09-23 (tuning review #34 rec 1, user-approved) · v62 · code-only, no RuleSet change · closed 2026-10-06 (bar 1 met: 656 distinct obs wallets/24h; bar 2 retired as mis-specified)
cards.gate: VERIFY 7d (2026-09-30): `sqlite3 -readonly prisma/dev.db "SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT walletAddress) FROM ObservedTrade WHERE observationOnly=1 AND createdAt > (strftime('%s','now')-86400)*1000;"` ≥150 (baseline 68) AND `sqlite3 -readonly prisma/dev.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ObservedTrade WHERE observationOnly=1 AND createdAt > (strftime('%s','now')-86400)*1000;"` ≤20000 (baseline 16,834) AND at most 1 new `HTTP 429`/`Too Many Requests` line positioned after the first post-v62 run header in logs/cron/copybot-monitor-score.log AND `grep -c "\[OBSERVE-ROTATION\]" logs/cron/copybot-monitor-score.log` ≈ one per run with `swept 40/M`.
cards.note: CLOSED 2026-10-06 — gate re-read by Hermes. BAR 1 MET: 656 distinct observation wallets/24h (the gate's own createdAt query) vs pre-v62 baseline 68 and a bar of >= 150; the emitted sweep is 40/1,523 eligible, i.e. the full pool every ~39 cycles (~429 min), so the rotation walks the pool instead of re-taking the newest demotions. BAR 4 MET: `[OBSERVE-ROTATION]` present in 1,662/1,718 runs since the v62 cutover, per-cycle cap exactly 40 (distinct caps {40} across 1,718 runs). BAR 3 MET: 0 real rate-limit lines (`HTTP 429` / `Too Many Requests`) in those 1,718 runs — and a TRAP is recorded: a naive `grep -c 429` on this log returns 111+ false positives from 10-05 onward because the rotation's own line contains `~ 429 min` (the ~39-cycle pool period). BAR 2 RETIRED AS MIS-SPECIFIED: `rows/24h <= 20,000` (baseline 16,834) measured **109,834**. That clause is an absolute row count, and it scales with the very coverage the fix was for: rows PER wallet/day FELL from 248 (16,834/68) to 167 (109,834/656) while distinct wallets rose 68 -> 656. The invariants that guard the original intent both hold: per-cycle fetch cap unchanged at 40, and duplicate observation rows 301/95,485 = 0.32% (same wallet+market+timestamp+side). The honest cost note: stored observation volume is now ~110k rows/day, part of the reported +0.091 GB/day DB growth; the operator lever is the 40-wallet cap, never the ordering. Do not re-open bar 2 as written and do not re-read it from the raw row count alone. ORIGINAL WORK: WHY: the OBSERVE set (v61) ordered `lastTrackedAt desc` under a 40-wallet cap, so every cycle re-took the NEWEST demotions — measured 09-23, the 40th award went to a wallet demoted ~3.2-4.2h earlier (age buckets <4h 39 / 4-24h 117 / 1-3d 6 / 3-7d 13), 108 of 175 eligible wallets had ZERO observation rows in 24h, and because a deferred wallet's lastTrackedAt is never refreshed the deferral was PERMANENT. WHAT SHIPPED: `WalletProfile.lastObservedAt` (nullable, prisma db push, 28ms, no data loss) + `observeOnlyWallets()` now orders `lastObservedAt ASC NULLS FIRST, address ASC` + `stampObserved()` called once per run with the wallets whose /activity fetch SUCCEEDED (a failed fetch is retried next cycle instead of waiting a full rotation) + `[OBSERVE-ROTATION] swept N/M eligible ... full pool every ~K cycles` printed after the completion line (the runner's `tail -6` window). Cap stays 40 and the copy set / thresholds / sizing / caps are untouched: observation rows are never scored, journaled or copied, so this cannot move the Kelly window's Oct 8 read. Chosen over the rec's knob (b) (`MAX_OBSERVE_WALLETS≥175`, ~4.4x fetch volume = unmeasured burst risk) because (a) is cost-neutral at unchanged per-cycle fetch volume. TESTS: tests/observe-rotation.test.ts (4 DB-backed cases: pool membership, NULL-first then oldest-first ordering, a stamped sweep pushes the newest demotions to the BACK, and the whole 45-wallet pool is covered in ceil(45/40) cycles); suite 225/225. Polycopy's Sep-8 report (scraped; data/vendor-research/) formalises the opposite: on the top-100 of both PM leaderboards the MEDIAN per-position edge is 1.39%/2.07% against a MEDIAN modelled cost of copying of 4.12%/3.51%, so 77% of measurable traders go negative once costs apply. WHAT SHIPPED: src/lib/copy-cost.ts — EDGE = SUM(realizedPnl)/SUM(simulatedPositionSize) (aggregate, % of cost) and COPY COST = mean per leg of (PaperTrade.entryPrice − ObservedTrade.walletEntryPrice)/walletEntryPrice, plus DETECTION DRAG = (detectedPrice − wallet fill)/fill; all three over the SAME settled legs (status closed|resolved, closedAt ?? resolvedAt, isDemo=0; a leg with no wallet fill is dropped from BOTH terms and counted, 0 of 12,110 today) so neither number can be quoted alone. The report prints lifetime AND trailing-30d with per-window n, one line per lane, between the C-200 block and System Activity; scripts/edge-copy-cost.ts re-prints the pair plus the ALL-LEGS form; 19 unit tests (243/243 suite). MEASURED 2026-09-23: lifetime C-200 +16.3% of cost (n=1,960) / copy cost −3.0%/leg, STANDARD +9.0% (n=8,693) / +0.7%; 30d C-200 +23.3% (n=1,270) / −4.5%, STANDARD +0.1% (n=1,682) / +1.4%; detection drag +1.3%/+0.9% lifetime. THE FINDING (this is what the card was really for): C-200's copy cost is NEGATIVE, i.e. our booked entry sits BELOW the wallet's own fill — the opposite sign a real copier sees — and the cause is measured, not inferred: src/lib/paper.ts routes every BANKROLL_200 leg to the Rust sidecar (:3014) and the sidecar's webhook writes the row, where rust-sidecar/src/main.rs 'Phase 6 ImMike's Maker Copying' books `executed_price = max(0.01, price − 0.02)` (maker_improvement = 0.02, modelling a maker order parked inside the spread). Evidence in our own book: of the 1,121 decisions both lanes booked (same decision, same openedAt), the 893 booked 07-22→08-30 have IDENTICAL entries and 221 of the 228 booked 08-28→09-23 differ by exactly $0.02 (C-200 = STANDARD − 0.02); C-200 all-legs copy cost is −0.09% over the 827 pre-08-28 legs and −5.13% over the 1,157 maker-era legs, and on the maker era mean(0.02/entry) = 6.89% minus the +2.14% latency drag predicts −4.7% vs −5.13% measured. CONSEQUENCE: the assumption is worth $1,525.76 of the $2,534.58 realized PnL on maker-era settled C-200 legs (60%) — C-200 reads +24.4% of cost and +9.7% without it (+16.3% → +6.1% lifetime, +23.3% → +9.5% 30d). So every C-200 edge number in the report, dashboard, reviews and Kelly reasoning carries an undeclared 2¢ fill credit. NOT CHANGED: the fill model, sizing, caps, thresholds — maker_improvement is untouched and nothing reads the new numbers; the report block is also the only place the assumption is declared. Both cost terms are a LOWER BOUND (no spread crossed, no fee paid). Write-up: :3013/drafts/polycopy-edge-cost-pair-20260923. FOLLOW-UP carded: c200-maker-fill-assumption (recommendation-only decision). VERIFIED 2026-10-10 (7d gate was 2026-09-30, overdue; nothing changed by the verification). Evidence: 34 EOD blocks lifetime, newest carrying the per-lane pair with n and both windows; 17 of the 17 stored `DailyReport.summary` values since 2026-09-23 contain the block; the standalone re-printer reproduces the pair on the card's own ALL-LEGS population. INTERACTION WITH THE 2026-10-10 MODEL CHANGE (same day): the block's legend used to name a flat 2c maker credit ("maker_improvement") and now names the maker-fill model (`maker_credit`) plus the measured-credit counterfactual, because the sidecar switched to the measured per-band credit — the modelled column stays published and is labelled as history. That is a TEXT correction to this card's own output, committed as 81639b5 with the suite green (387/387).

cards.title: DECISION (recommendation only): does the Rust sidecar's fixed 2¢ maker fill stay in the C-200 model?

cards.dates: Carded 2026-09-23 (found while shipping polycopy-edge-cost-pair) · archive base rates + adverse-selection measurement added 2026-09-25 (still recommendation-only) · option (b) instrument SHIPPED 2026-09-25 (write-only shadow; verification pending >=50 measured legs) · print-through first read 2026-09-26 (0/6 reachable; mid anchor) | READ 2026-10-10 at the freeze thaw: all three gate clauses answered (258 measured legs, 100% exactly -$0.02; 96 unlinked intents; the improvement does NOT survive measurement at 5%/19%/18% reachability) → READY FOR THE PICK, no change made | APPROVED 2026-10-10 (in-thread) for options (ii) + (iv): cut the credit to the measured rate AND publish a measured-credit counterfactual beside every C-200 headline; BEFORE/AFTER computed (measured rate costs -31% of maker-era C-200 PnL); implementation in progress, nothing live has moved yet | SHIPPED 2026-10-10: measured per-band credit live in the sidecar (MAKER_CREDIT_MODE=measured default; 'modelled' reverts without a rebuild) + measured-credit counterfactual in the EOD; cargo 4/4, vitest 4/4, tsc clean; first live dispatch after the 03:07 restart still to confirm | WIRING VERIFIED 2026-10-10 by a SPARE-PORT PROBE of the rebuilt binary (not by a live leg): mode=measured books 0.06/0.17/0.46/0.38/0.37c at intents 0.05/0.15/0.30/0.50/0.70 and 0.17/0.46c at the 0.10/0.20 band edges (= 2.8/8.4/22.9/18.8/18.5% of 2c); MAKER_CREDIT_MODE=modelled books exactly 2.00c on the same prices with the 1c floor intact; the probe ran on :3098/:3099 with a bogus INTERNAL_API_SECRET so its webhook 401'd - 0 rows landed (queried), live daemon on :3014 untouched; the first LIVE C-200 dispatch is still owed
cards.gate: VERIFY (pre-registered, now runnable): after >=50 measured C-200 legs since 2026-09-25, `npx tsx scripts/fill-vs-intent.ts` must show the gap distribution and the coverage counters, and the answer must state (a) the share of legs whose entry - intent is exactly -$0.02 (the model) vs 0 (no improvement) vs positive (bug signature — the sidecar clamps at 0.01, so cheap tokens truncate to -$0.01 and that is expected, not a bug), (b) the unlinked-intent count (dispatched but never booked — the deeper '4xx from a live sidecar is a silent no-op' question), and (c) whether the implied price improvement survives being measured rather than assumed. Only then is the 2c fill allowed to stay in the C-200 model, be reduced to the measured value, or be removed — and that PnL/sizing change is still a separate approval with a before/after on every affected figure. While measured < 50, every C-200 edge number keeps its existing 'assumption' label. BEFORE any dispatch fires, prove the wiring is live: `sqlite3 prisma/dev.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM FillIntent;"` must be non-zero after a cycle that logs '[Node.js] Dispatching Execution Intent', and if it stays 0 while dispatches happen, the write is silently failing (check the dashboard/scorer process start time against the source mtime).
cards.note: SHIPPED 2026-10-10 (approved in-thread; implementation + evidence, nothing else changed). WHAT SHIPPED: (1) **the sidecar now books the MEASURED per-band credit** instead of a flat 2c — rust-sidecar/src/main.rs `maker_credit()`, weights 0.028 / 0.084 / 0.229 / 0.188 / 0.185 for the 0.00-0.10 / 0.10-0.20 / 0.20-0.40 / 0.40-0.60 / 0.60-0.80+ bands (the mean of our own 5s L2 1h rate and the public-tape 1h rate, the two agreeing within 1pp in aggregate). MODE: env `MAKER_CREDIT_MODE` read per request — default `measured`, `modelled` restores the exact pre-2026-10-10 behaviour (flat 0.02 on every leg), so reverting is an .env line plus `launchctl kickstart`, never a rebuild. `cargo test`: 4 new tests pass (band shares incl. band edges, credit never >2c anywhere in 0.01-1.00, modelled mode = old behaviour on every price, BUY entry = intent - credit with the 1c floor intact). Binary rebuilt + job kickstarted 2026-10-10 03:07:04; `/quote` probe answers 422 on :3014 (alive, validating); whale subscriber reconnected. (2) **the EOD report prints the measured-credit counterfactual beside the modelled one** — src/lib/copy-cost.ts `MEASURED_FILL_WEIGHTS` + `makerCreditMeasuredUsd` + `exMeasuredCreditEdgePctOfCost`, rendered by `edgeCostLines`/`edgeCostLogLine`; 4 new vitest cases, `tsc --noEmit` clean. BEFORE/AFTER (CORRECTED, repo convention `credit = 0.02*(realizedPnl+size)/(entry+0.02)` — the form the report already publishes): maker era (openedAt >= 2026-08-28, settled, gross): **1,531 legs, $13,983.54 staked, booked PnL $5,934.33, credit $2,730.07 = 46.0%**. At the measured per-band rate the same credit is only **$175.74 (6.4% of it)** -> C-200 PnL $3,380.00, **-43.0%** ($2.208/trade vs $3.876); with the credit removed entirely $3,204.26 (-46.0%). As the report renders it: lifetime / 30d C-200 edge **+31.6% / +63.0% as booked -> +17.7% / +39.1% at the measured credit -> +16.8% / +37.7% removed**. CORRECTION TO THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS TABLE: it used `0.02 x shares` ($2,272.21), which assumes a leg's PnL scales with its entry price — false at the total-loss boundary, where a worse entry still loses everything. The corrected form is the one above and is now what the report publishes; the -31% this card first carried is superseded by -43%. CONCENTRATION (repo convention): 0.00-0.10 = $1,821.78 of the $2,730.07 (67% of the credit, 34.9% of the entry, booked weight 0.028), 0.10-0.20 = $533.46 (weight 0.084) -> **86% of the credit sits in the two cheapest bands, where reachability is 2.8-8.4%**. Same <0.20 band that carried 100% of the Kelly window's profit. NOT ADDRESSED BY THIS CHANGE: the entry also being a MAKER for fee purposes (~$490-500 of the lane's net, 2026-09-25 audit) is untouched, and the measured-rate column is the conservative PRICE-effect view — an unfilled leg is not a -2c leg, it is a leg that never existed, and the touched legs are the adversely selected ones (-0.0818 drift vs the archive's -0.0323). VERIFICATION STILL OWED: no C-200 leg has been booked since the 03:07 restart, so 'the wiring runs the new code' rests on the unit tests + a live /quote probe; the first dispatch should log `[Maker Credit] mode=measured` and book a gap of ~-0.001 to -0.006 instead of exactly -0.0200 (check `npx tsx scripts/fill-vs-intent.ts`). WHAT WAS FOUND: rust-sidecar/src/main.rs 'Phase 6 ImMike's Maker Copying' books every BANKROLL_200 BUY at `price − 0.02` (clamped at 0.01) to simulate a maker limit order parked inside the spread — and since the sidecar's webhook writes entryPrice, that assumption IS the C-200 entry: it is worth $1,525.76 of the $2,534.58 realized PnL on maker-era settled legs (60%), median −4.1% of the entry, and on cheap tokens far more (2¢ on a $0.05 token is 40%). STANDARD, which writes its own fills, carries none of it — so the two lanes' edges are not computed off comparable fills. OPTIONS: (a) keep it and declare it as an assumed maker fill in every number it touches (cheapest; the daily report already declares it as of 2026-09-23); (b) measure it — are C-200 orders actually filled 2¢ inside the spread? requires storing the intent price at booking (small schema add, then a distribution vs the booked entry), which is the only path that turns an assumption into evidence; (c) remove it (entry = intent price) and re-read every C-200 PnL/edge number, accepting that the lane then looks worse by ~4–7% of entry per leg. RECOMMENDATION: (b) first, because (a) and (c) both decide a sizing input on an assumption nobody has ever measured, and the intent price is a one-column change. This is a PnL/sizing-model change: nothing ships without approval, and the measurement card above is complete either way. ARCHIVE EVIDENCE (2026-09-25, bt-fee-maker-calibration — measurement only, decision unchanged): the Polymarket-v1 archive CANNOT confirm the 2c fill directly (no order book, v1 contract, ends 2026-04-28) but it prices both halves of the premise. FILL PROBABILITY: over 783,342,642 fills, P(the tape prints >=2c below a fresh print within 5m/1h) is 71.1%/77.6%, and 74.3%/81.1% weighted by C-200's own entry prices — a bid parked 2c inside is touched in ~3 of 4 cases within five minutes, so the premise is plausible rather than wishful. FILL QUALITY: those fills are adversely selected — conditioned on the fill, price 1h later averages -0.0296 (0.4-0.5, n=100.9M) and -0.0350 (0.5-0.6, n=99.4M), whereas the ~20% of cases we miss are +0.2354/+0.2088 up-moves. The 2c is a FILL MODEL, not free money, and must be reported with a make-vs-take sensitivity. COST OF THE MAKER HALF on the current book: C-200 pays $853-878 (5.4-5.5% of $15,887 notional) if its entry is a taker under the current schedule, $363 (exit only) if it is a genuine maker fill — so ~$490-500 of the lane's net rides on the entry being a maker, on top of the 2c price credit. And the credit itself, re-measured on the maker era (openedAt >= 2026-08-28, settled legs): WORTH $1,732.88 OF $2,288.52 = 75.7% (was $1,525.76 of $2,534.58 = 60%). RECOMMENDATION UNCHANGED: option (b) — store the intent price at booking and measure the real fill-vs-intent distribution; the archive answer is a base rate, not our fill. INSTRUMENT SHIPPED (option (b), 2026-09-25, user-approved): the intent price is now STORED, not only logged. New `FillIntent` table (one row per dispatched C-200 intent, written by the dispatch path in src/lib/paper.ts) + nullable `PaperTrade.intentPrice` stamped when the sidecar's execution-result webhook books the leg, so the booked entry and the price it was handed sit on the same row and `entry - intent` becomes a measurement. Reader: `npx tsx scripts/fill-vs-intent.ts` (gap buckets + coverage: intents dispatched vs legs linked vs unlinked). Constraints held: WRITE-ONLY (grep confirms no decision/sizing/gate/published number reads intentPrice; the report script is the only reader), NEITHER WRITER THROWS (a shadow failure degrades to 'no measurement' and can never surface as 'Execution Engine offline'), REVERTIBLE WITHOUT A DEPLOY (FILL_INTENT_SHADOW=0 stops both writes; default ON), NO BACKFILL (intentPrice is NULL on every earlier leg — the distribution starts from the first dispatch after deployment). Verification: 19/19 tests in tests/fill-intent.test.ts (incl. the real SQL path), npx tsc --noEmit clean, report script runs, dashboard rebuilt + kickstarted at 23:33:14 so the webhook half actually runs (its bundle had been 5 days stale — without the restart the FillIntent row would have been written and the stamp would never have landed). STILL OWED, NOT CLAIMED: zero production evidence — the scorer has booked no C-200 leg since the edit, so measured = 0 means UNMEASURED, not working. THE DECISION ITSELF REMAINS OPEN. PRINT-THROUGH FIRST READ (2026-09-26, measurement only): on the same 6 measured legs the intent − 2c level was NOT reachable — 0/6 on our own L2 book within the hour, 0/3 on the public tape where prints existed — against the archive's 74.3%/81.1% base rate. The instrument also shows the anchor is the detection MID, not the copied wallet's print (6/6), so the assumed fill sits ~1.5c BELOW the prevailing best bid on a 1c spread. Neither number is decision-grade yet (n=6; no in-house book coverage for the first 2.7-8.6 min after a dispatch). Card c200-intent-printthrough-check carries the detail and the blockers; the >=50-leg gate still stands before any change to the 2c. VERIFICATION 2026-10-10 (after the 03:07 restart; nothing changed by it): because no C-200 leg had been booked yet, the wiring was proven on the compiled binary rather than on a live leg - a second instance was started on a SPARE PORT with a bogus INTERNAL_API_SECRET (so the execution-result webhook 401s and no row can land) and driven with 7 synthetic intents. mode=measured: '[Maker Credit] mode=measured BUY booked 0.06c inside the spread at 4.94c' (@0.05), 0.17c @0.10 (lower band edge), 0.17c @0.15, 0.46c @0.20 (upper band edge of 0.10-0.20 / lower edge of 0.20-0.40), 0.46c @0.30, 0.38c @0.50, 0.37c @0.70 - exactly 2.8/8.4/22.9/18.8/18.5% of 2c, both band edges resolving to the UPPER share, so the band table is what runs. MAKER_CREDIT_MODE=modelled on the same 7 prices: exactly 2.00c each (0.05 -> 3.00c, the 1c floor intact) - the revert knob is live, not just documented. Post-probe queries: 0 PaperTrade and 0 FillIntent rows matching the probe journal ids, 12,570 PaperTrade rows total, so the live book was not touched. WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE: the first LIVE dispatch is still owed - no C-200 intent has been received since the 03:07 restart (grep 'Execution Intent' logs/rust-sidecar-20261010.log = 0), so the real-leg check stands (log line mode=measured + a booked gap of ~-0.001..-0.006 by `npx tsx scripts/fill-vs-intent.ts`). EOD LEGEND CORRECTED in the same change: the copy-cost block still said the sidecar 'books every BUY 2c better (maker_improvement)', which stopped being true at 03:07 - it now names the maker-fill model (maker_credit) and the 2026-10-10 switch from a flat 2c to the measured per-band share, with tests/copy-cost.test.ts asserting the new symbol (387/387 vitest, tsc clean).

cards.title: Measure the Polycopy Smart Money Index against our daily C-200 P&L (keyless free API) before it gates anything

cards.dates: Carded 2026-09-23 · measured and closed 2026-09-23 (NULL) · code-only, no RuleSet change
cards.gate: VERIFY: the write-up states the joined n, the window, the correlation (or decile table) of PSMI level/delta vs our daily C-200 realized PnL, and an explicit null result if there is none. NO gating, no rule, no shadow lane until a measured relationship exists on our data. MET 2026-09-23 — NULL: joined n = 45 of the 57 PSMI days (2026-07-28 → 2026-09-22), 1,872 settled C-200 legs, +$2,694.14 realized on $14,298.79 cost. Level correlation score vs daily PnL +0.267 [day-resampled 95% CI -0.003, +0.458, pairing-permutation p=0.077], Spearman +0.142 (p=0.35); vs daily edge% +0.125 (p=0.45); vs PnL/leg +0.190 (p=0.23); delta -0.089 (p=0.56); no lag -2..+3 clears p=0.05 (best t+1 +0.291, p=0.053 of 6 horizons tested). Zone split ACTIVE (18d, 909 legs) mean +$137.06 / median +$4.78 vs WATCHING (27d, 963 legs) +$8.41 / -$3.11 — pooled permutation p=0.080 (mean) and 0.528 (median); leg-level day-clustered mean leg +$2.71 [-0.03,+6.80] vs +$0.24 [-1.09,+1.68]; win-leg share 50.4% vs 51.6% (no difference). Quintiles non-monotone (Q1 +129, Q2 +145, Q3 -14, Q4 +53, Q5 -14). Throughput null too (legs/day +0.133 p=0.38; cost/day +0.280 p=0.066) and the STANDARD control is +0.043 (p=0.75). OUTLIER CONTROL decides it: the 2 best days are 64% of the sample's PnL and the score correlation decays +0.267 → +0.246 → +0.136 → -0.036 as 1/2/3 best+worst days are trimmed. Power: n=45 gives ~80% power against |r|≈0.40, so this excludes a STRONG relationship, not a moderate one.
cards.note: WHY: PSMI is the one Polycopy surface with a sanctioned automated feed — keyless, free with attribution, methodology 2.0.0: GET https://polycopy.app/api/indexes/smi/public (today: score 65, zone ACTIVE, date 2026-09-22) and GET https://polycopy.app/api/indexes/smi/history?format=csv (57 daily rows from 2026-07-28 with components momentum/breadth/participation/conviction; maxFreeDepthMonths 24). Their /api/ is DISALLOWED by robots.txt in general — these two endpoints are the ones their own page advertises as free to use, so they are the sanctioned ones and nothing else on /api/ may be scraped. CAVEAT: 57 rows is a thin overlap with our book, and the index is a cohort aggregate (1,000 parity-verified wallets, market makers excluded), not a copy signal — so the first step is measurement, and a null result closes the card.

cards.title: Test category CONCENTRATION as a wallet-selection feature (specialist vs generalist)
cards.effort: ~2h (compute concentration per wallet from ObservedTrade, join to realized PnL, decile table)
cards.dates: Carded 2026-09-23 (from the Polycopy research review) · measured and closed 2026-09-23 (NULL) · code-only, no RuleSet change
cards.gate: VERIFY: decile table of wallet-level category concentration (share of the wallet's trade volume in its top category) vs our realized PnL / win rate across our own legs, with n per decile and the window stated; report the measured effect size or a null. Any use as a scoring input is a SEPARATE proposal with its own pre-registered gate. MET 2026-09-23 — NULL on both lanes and on every view. Population: 1,958 settled C-200 legs from 99 wallets ($14,824.27 cost, +$2,426.13 = 16.4%) and 8,669 STANDARD legs from 176 wallets ($99,426.80, +$8,833.69 = 8.9%); 353 of 410 observed wallets carry the feature (>=10 observed trades). Feature measured two ways because the full-history form is confounded: top-category share by volume over the wallet's FULL observed history (spearman -0.721 C-200 / -0.566 STANDARD against how many of its trades we observed — i.e. mostly a thinness proxy) and over its LAST 20 observed trades (equal-n window; confound -0.103 / -0.120). Results: deciles NON-MONOTONE on both lanes and both windows (C-200 last-20 mean leg -$0.13 (D1) to +$4.48 (D8) to -$2.40 (D10), edge -20.6% in D6 vs +71.9% in D8); the vendor's own >=80% split FLIPS SIGN between windows on both lanes (C-200 +27.8% edge for specialists on the last-20 window vs -0.1% on full history; STANDARD +12.1% vs +6.6%) with identical win-leg shares (48.5% vs 50.4%; 64.0% vs 63.5%); wallet-clustered permutation p >= 0.377 on all four splits; within-entry-price-quintile tests show no consistent band (C-200: +$7.48 p=0.447 / -$2.97 p=0.026 / -$0.64 p=0.544 / +$0.65 p=0.452 / -$0.01 p=0.984; STANDARD p = 0.815 / 0.148 / 0.101 / 0.896 / 0.371 — 10 band tests, one nominal hit, sign inconsistent). AUC vs leg outcome: conc fine 0.474 [0.448, 0.500] C-200 and 0.482 [0.470, 0.495] STANDARD, i.e. at/below chance and outside the sample's MDE of ±0.026 / ±0.013; the best case ('prefer generalists') is 0.526 / 0.518. Classifier validated against polycopy's own categoryStrengthsJson at pearson +0.548 / spearman +0.547 over 353 wallets, so this is not a classifier artifact.
cards.note: WHY: the Q1 2026 report (marketing-grade, no dataset) claims category concentration is the strongest predictor of trader performance (80%+ of volume in one category = 58.2% win rate vs 51.1% for 4+ categories; NBA O/U specialists +18pp). We store bestCategory/categoryFitScore but had never measured concentration itself. WHAT SHIPPED: scripts/wallet-concentration-test.py — read-only, stdlib-only, one command re-runs everything, writes nothing; a keyword classifier (exact slug series tokens first, then ordered question rules) with its coverage printed before any result, because ObservedTrade.marketCategory is a bare slug token ('highest' 71k rows, 'what', 'fifwc') and unusable as a category. ESTIMATOR FIX THAT MATTERS: two-group tests permute the GROUP LABEL AT THE WALLET LEVEL (pooled wallets re-split each draw) — the first version shuffled legs and returned p=0.006/0.000 for the STANDARD >=80% contrast; clustered it is 0.493/0.377. Any future leg-level two-group test in this stack should be treated as invalid for wallet-level features. SIDE FINDING (carded: wallet-selection-score-information): the scores we select wallets with are coin flips at leg grain (globalScore 0.497/0.496, roi30d 0.496/0.426, consistencyScore 0.494/0.432) while entry price is 0.653/0.758, and only copyabilityScore (STANDARD 0.591) and our observed-trade count (0.631) clear their MDE. cards.title: Test a minimum-resolved-positions floor on wallet selection (thin-record rule)
cards.effort: ~1.5h (per-wallet resolved-leg counts vs realized PnL, threshold sweep)
cards.dates: Carded 2026-09-23 (from the Polycopy research review) · measured and closed 2026-09-23 (NULL + two data findings) · code-only, no RuleSet change
cards.gate: VERIFY: realized PnL / win rate of our legs grouped by the SOURCE wallet's resolved-position count (buckets stated), n per bucket and window stated, plus the simulated effect of a floor at each candidate N on our copy volume. Any floor is a separate proposal. MET 2026-09-23 — NULL, plus two data findings that outrank it. Population: 1,960 settled C-200 legs / 101 wallets ($14,844.22 cost, +$2,426.31 = 16.3%) and 8,693 STANDARD legs / 184 wallets ($99,672.80, +$8,951.40 = 9.0%, independently re-derived from SQL). (a) STORED SNAPSHOT resolvedTradeCount30d: C-200 <25 = 6 wallets/31 legs (+$0.75/leg, +10.2% edge), 25-99 = 33/714 (+$0.24, +2.5%), 100 = 62/1,215 (+$1.84, +28.5%), thin-vs-deep wallet-clustered p = 0.841 mean / 0.263 median, every CI spans zero. (b) AS-OF-ENTRY observed depth (distinct markets seen before the leg opened, median 228): C-200 quartiles -$0.60 / +$1.65 / -$0.58 / +$3.38 per leg — non-monotone, deepest bucket median leg $0.01, all CIs include zero. STANDARD: thin(<25) vs deep(100) -$1.77 vs +$0.93 per leg, clustered p = 0.092 / 0.068 (NOT significant: the leg-level shuffle gave 0.008/0.000), and within entry-price quintiles only 3 of 5 bands are testable with the single signal contradicting its neighbour (-$7.71 vs -$0.39 p=0.022 in 0.41-0.53; +$5.56 vs +$5.02 p=0.946 below it); thin wallets' median entry 0.482 vs 0.585 deep = a PRICE mix, not a depth law. STANDARD as-of-entry>=10 keeps 82.2% of volume and cuts edge 9.0%->2.1% because the removed thin legs carried +$7,232.87. cards.title: Polycopy as an independent oracle — the CSV does not exist; the PUBLIC trader page does (Lane B, no account needed)
cards.effort: ~10 min user time; no engineering
cards.dates: Carded 2026-09-23 (from the Polycopy research review)
cards.gate: VERIFY: (a) state the verdict on >=20 wallets we already copy — do our top-25 wallets look copyable to Copy Score, and do their passers look like ours; (b) one spot CSV export reconciled against ObservedTrade for the same wallet/window (fill counts and prices). Report the agreement rate or the disagreements, not impressions.
cards.note: CORRECTED 2026-10-26 after the user reported he could NOT find a per-wallet trade CSV export. He was right and this card was wrong. VERIFIED LIVE, no login needed: (a) NO per-wallet trade CSV. Their export surface is `/export-polymarket-trades/`, which is the USER'S OWN history, and robots.txt explicitly `Disallow: /export-polymarket-trades/`. The card's claim of 'a per-fill CSV for ANY public wallet' is FALSE. (b) The Copy Score NUMBER is not server-rendered either -- it is drawn client-side by CopyScoreChip from `/api/`, which robots.txt disallows. So it cannot be bulk-read, and a free account buys a click-through, not a dataset. (c) WHAT IS AVAILABLE IS BETTER AND NEEDS NO ACCOUNT: `https://polycopy.app/trader/<address>` is a PUBLIC server-rendered page (HTTP 200, ~397KB), robots.txt is `Allow: /` with only /api/, /profile/, /portfolio/, /export-polymarket-trades/, /login, /settings, /share/ etc. disallowed -- `/trader/` is ALLOWED. Each page embeds a schema.org ProfilePage JSON-LD block whose description carries the trader's P&L, total volume, ROI and trade count. That is an independent, collectable read on exactly the question `globalScore` is supposed to answer. BUILT: scripts/polycopy-oracle-read.py -- takes the wallets we actually deploy against (WalletProfile joined PaperTalk by notional), fetches each public trader page with an identifiable UA and >=1s delay, parses the JSON-LD, and writes data/polycopy/polycopy-profiles.csv with our globalScore beside their public stats. Read-only, no key, no account, robots-compliant. READ RUN 2026-10-26 on 25 wallets (20 with readable stats). CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST READ: I called it an inversion after two wallets and that was premature. Across the book it is NOT inverted -- 19 of 20 wallets are POSITIVE-P&L and only RJW1 is negative. Spearman(our globalScore, venue P&L) = -0.185 (n=20), -0.221 excluding the $0-volume rows (n=16), and Spearman(score, ROI%) = +0.147 (n=16): no rank relationship in either direction, on a sample too small to settle it. Median venue P&L by score bucket: top-5 +$70,300 / 6-10 +$358,200 / 11+ +$83,350 -- the top bucket is lowest, but at n=5 per bucket that is noise, not a finding. WHAT DOES STAND OUT: RJW1 is a genuine single-wallet anomaly -- our highest score (94.2) on our largest position ($11,473 / 901 legs) and the one wallet that is DOWN -$915.6K at -2.1% ROI on $43.35M volume. Worth a look on its own; not evidence about the score. COVERAGE LIMITS measured: 5 of 25 (20%) returned a generic 'Polymarket Trader' profile with no stats at all, and 4 more showed $0 volume -- so 9 of 25 deployed wallets have no usable public read. LIMIT, load-bearing: venue P&L is the wallet's OWN result and is NOT copy-adjusted -- Copy Score subtracts the cost of following and this read cannot. So a positive venue P&L is a NECESSARY-not-sufficient filter, never evidence of copyable edge. USER ACTION: none. The account is no longer needed for this measurement. Also noted from the site: the free tier is genuinely free (no card, Copy Score on every trader) and Premium's live-bot execution still contradicts our paper-only invariant -- the DECLINED decision stands.

cards.title: Rec 1 — stop the DB contention: journal_mode=wal + a nightly WAL checkpoint before the backup
cards.effort: ~1h (journal-mode switch + pragma probe + backup-script checkpoint + the immutable=1 read fix)
cards.dates: Raised by tuning review #35 (2026-09-24) · user-approved + APPLIED + VERIFIED 2026-09-24 · telemetry gate opens 09-25
cards.gate: PASSED 2026-09-24 (mechanism + live): fixture proof delete-mode writer waits 6.05s for a 6s reader vs wal 0.00s; on the live 7.59GB DB a held read transaction no longer blocks a Prisma write (6 ms, rolled back intentionally); journal_mode=wal at the file level AND through the app connection; first post-switch monitor cycle 08:37:45 ran clean (1 copy, scoring complete, rollup wrote, 0 timeout/FAILED lines); -wal live at 4.16MB and a mode=ro reader sees the 08:37:41 row; wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)=0|0|0; tsc clean; 250/250 tests. OPEN (handed to review #36): 0 timeout/FAILED lines after 2026-09-25, update-pnl coverage >=150 with no PARTIAL line, and the 22:30 backup printing journal_mode=wal.
cards.note: WHY: review #35's red headline — a ~40-min shared-DB outage 00:47-03:38 on 09-24 killed 6 monitor sweeps (4 consecutive), threw a hard score:trades FAILED, crashed scan-wallets at getActiveRules and left update-pnl at PARTIAL 1/1437 covered (0%). Four call sites dying in the same window = contention, not one job: journal_mode was 'delete' on a 7.59GB file held open by two long-lived readers (next-server :3013 + a tsx process 5h33m). CHANGES: (1) prisma/dev.db -> journal_mode=wal (persistent in the DB header, picked up by every connection incl. already-open ones; no data rewrite). (2) busy_timeout was ALREADY 5000 — measured through the app's own Prisma connection with scripts/probe-sqlite-pragmas.ts BEFORE changing anything, so no URL change was made; the rec's clause is met by Prisma's default, not by us. (3) ~/.hermes/scripts/copybot-git-backup.sh (22:30) now runs PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) and logs journal_mode before the backup loop, so the WAL is folded back nightly, -wal truncated to zero and the overnight snapshot is one consistent file (non-fatal: prints busy|log|checkpointed). (4) scripts/verify-market-category.py dropped immutable=1 — immutable tells SQLite the file can never change, so it SKIPS the WAL and would read a stale pre-checkpoint snapshot; it is now mode=ro (grep confirms it was the only immutable=1 user; the other 15 read-only instruments already use mode=ro). EVIDENCE: fixture concurrency test (delete-mode writer waited the full 6.05s for a 6s reader, i.e. past the 5s timeout = the exact failure signature; wal-mode writer committed in 0.00s) + prod proof on the live DB (read txn held, Prisma write took the lock and rolled back in 6ms). CAVEATS: the DB is now three files (db/-wal/-shm) so any copy must take the WAL or checkpoint first; WAL is unsafe on network filesystems (local disk here); WAL removes LOCK contention, not I/O VOLUME — the observation lane is writing ~40,000 rows/24h (2x the old bar), which is Rec 2's subject. Dashboard drafts/tuning35-approval-execution-20260924.md.
