cards.title: Fee model + maker/taker calibration from the Polymarket-v1 archive (measurement)
cards.effort: ~2h (three sharded duckdb passes over 1.2B fills + our own book)
cards.dates: Measured 2026-09-25 · nothing implemented (recommendations-only)
cards.gate: REPRODUCE, don't re-derive: `/Volumes/Storage/pm-data/.venv/bin/python scripts/archive-fee-maker-analysis.py {split|fee|fill|drift}` then `python3 scripts/c200-fee-reprice-archive.py`; results already stored under data/archive-analysis/. Headline numbers to match: 1,201,580,990 fills; $1,213.0M of fees on 647,243,473 fee-bearing rows; taker BUY fee == 0.10 x shares x min(p,1-p) on 95-99% of rows to 1e-6; aggressor SELL in 83.6% of 2026-era fills; P(print 2c below within 5m/1h) = 71.1%/77.6% overall and 74.3%/81.1% weighted by C-200's own entry prices. Any study that quotes a fee now names its model: current published (0.05 x p(1-p), $1.25/100 shares) vs archive-era (0.10 x min(p,1-p)) — they differ ~4x at mid prices.
cards.note: WHY: the archive landed 2026-09-25 (bt-hist-archive-pull) carrying ground-truth aggressor direction + real fee_usdc, which is exactly what the ledger's zero-fee booking and the c200-maker-fill-assumption card were blocked on. WHAT WAS MEASURED (nothing else): (1) FEE ERA — fee_usdc is ZERO on 100% of fills through 2025-12, then rolls out per market: 2026-01 42.3% of fills fee-bearing ($84.6M), 2026-02 67.1% ($185.1M), 2026-03 75.8% ($374.3M), 2026-04 88.0% ($569.0M); 2026 era total = $1,213.0M on $31.11B notional = 3.90% of notional (taker BUY side 0.70%, taker SELL side 4.77%). (2) FEE LAW — for taker BUY, fee == (base/1e4) x shares x min(p,1-p) with base 1000 -> 0.10, matching to 1e-6 on 95-99% of rows in EVERY price band of both months tested; makers carry no fee (published: 'Makers pay $0'). Taker SELL instead fits 0.10 x shares x min(p,1-p)/p, an asymmetry I could NOT explain and am not building on — flagged in the draft as unexplained, not as a result. (3) SCHEDULE CHANGE — the current published schedule is shares x 0.05 x p(1-p) ($1.25/100 shares at p=0.5), i.e. ~4x cheaper at mid prices than the archive's 0.10 x min(p,1-p) ($5.00/100). The archive therefore calibrates STRUCTURE + attribution, never today's rate; our 2026-09-09 model (0.04-0.07 x p(1-p)) already matches the current schedule and the real error remains the ledger booking zero. (4) MAKER/TAKER SPLIT — the aggressor is a SELLER in 83.6% of 2026-era fills (74.6-89.4% by band; buyers cross only 16.4%), so the resting BID is the side that gets filled in this venue. (5) MAKER-FILL HAZARD (783,342,642 fills) — P(a print at <= p-delta within the horizon) at delta=0.02 is 71.1% (5m) / 76.1% (30m) / 77.6% (1h) overall, and 74.3% / 81.1% when weighted by C-200's own entry-price mix: the 2c-inside premise is plausible on fill probability. (6) ADVERSE SELECTION — the same event is not free: conditioned on the 2c bid filling, price 1h later averages -0.0296 (band 0.4-0.5, n=100,878,463) / -0.0350 (0.5-0.6, n=99,372,864), while the unfilled cases are up-moves (+0.2354 / +0.2088) we forgo. You fill exactly when price is coming down through you. (7) OUR OWN BOOK re-priced (scripts/c200-fee-reprice-archive.py, 2,017 C-200 legs / $15,887 notional): booked +$2,180.25 -> +$1,302-1,327 with the CURRENT schedule paid as a taker (fee $853-878 = 5.4-5.5% of notional) -> +$1,818 if the entry is a genuine maker fill (exit fee $363 only). The archive-era rate would put C-200 at -$206 / STANDARD at -$3,361 — a historical regime, must not be quoted as today's fee. LIMITS: prints are not queue position, size is ignored, no book depth/quotes/cancellations (per the dataset README), 1h horizon, CTF Exchange v1 terminated 2026-04-28. FEEDS: c200-maker-fill-assumption (evidence added, option (b) unchanged) and paper-ledger-fee-fidelity (fee numbers refreshed). Write-up: :3013/drafts/fee-maker-calibration-20260925.

cards.title: C-200 fill realism — did our intent price actually PRINT? (print-through vs assumed)
cards.effort: ~half day (price-series join + a print-through summariser)
cards.dates: Carded 2026-09-25 · unblocks once >=50 measured intent legs exist (c200-maker-fill-assumption) · FIRST READ 2026-09-26 (6 legs, 0/6 reachable; anchor found to be the MID, not the wallet print) | READ 2026-10-10 at the freeze thaw (354 legs) → gate met, rate produced: 5% (5m) / 19% (1h) vs the 74.3%/81.1% archive bar → card Done, model decision handed to c200-maker-fill-assumption
cards.gate: VERIFY: for each measured C-200 intent, the market's own price observations in the window after the dispatch show whether a trade printed at or below (intent - 0.02) — report the share where our assumed entry was reachable, with the adverse-selection split (mean price move after a reached vs unreached level) on the SAME population. Pre-registered bar: the archive base rate is 74.3% within 5 min at C-200's price mix (drafts/fee-maker-calibration-20260925.md §5) with a ~-0.03 adverse drift when reached — if the in-house share comes in materially below that, the 2c is booked on fills that never happened and the model must be cut to the measured rate. Measurement only: no rule, size, gate or booked figure moves.  FIRST READ (2026-09-26): runnable now on the 6 measured legs and it answers 'no' on the level-reachability half — the runner exists (`python3 scripts/c200-printthrough.py`), so the gate no longer needs the >=50-leg bar to produce a reading, only to produce a RATE. Re-run at >=50 legs before any model change; the mid-anchor finding makes the archive base rate an open question rather than a transferable prior.
cards.note: READ 2026-10-10 (FREEZE THAW, 354 measured legs — the card's >=50-leg bar is met; measurement only, nothing in the trade path reads it). RESULT: the assumed entry `intent - $0.02` was reachable on **18/339 legs within 5 min (5%)** on the public trade tape and **65/339 within 1 h (19%)**; our own 5s L2 corpus independently gives **65/353 legs (18%)** within 1 h — two instruments agreeing within 1pp, so this is not tape-thinness. Both are far below the archive base rate (74.3% @5m / 81.1% @1h) that the 2c is booked against. MECHANISM (measured, not inferred): our level is MID-anchored, not print-anchored — intent == the detection midpoint on 336/354 legs (94.9%) and == the copied wallet's own print on only 5/354; the level (mid - 2c) sits BELOW the first covered best bid on 278/353 legs (79%), so it is a deeper event than the archive's 'a print at p, then a print at or below p - 2c'. ADVERSE SELECTION reproduces and is LARGER: reached legs drift -0.0818 (n=56) vs the archive's -0.0323, while unreached legs are ~flat +0.0038 (n=212) — the archive's strongly positive missed arm (+0.13) does NOT reproduce. COVERAGE (fixed, and verified): after the v62 recorder change the median L2 start lag is 0.2 min, so the 5-minute book horizon IS covered on post-2026-09-26 legs. INSTRUMENT NIT found while reading: this script still prints the static pre-v62 sentence 'the 5-min horizon has NO in-house book coverage on any leg' (c200-printthrough.py build_summary/render) — it under-reports the truth now and should be computed from l2StartLagMin or deleted. Nothing changed in rules/sizing/booked figures: the 2c decision is c200-maker-fill-assumption's, and it now has every clause its gate demanded (100% of legs at exactly -$0.02, 96 unlinked intents, and a measured rate that does NOT support the archive prior). FIRST READ (2026-09-26, scripts/c200-printthrough.py, measurement only — nothing in the trade path reads it): 6 measured legs. ESTABLISHED: the level (intent − $0.02) was NOT reachable on any of the 6 legs in the hour after dispatch — 0/6 on our own 5s L2 book (a best ask at or below the level would fill a resting bid there) and 0/3 on the public trade tape where the tape had prints (3 legs tape-silent — a 2-50 row tape per market, so 'not reached' there is uninformative). The archive's base rate (74.3% within 5 min / 81.1% within 1 h at C-200's price mix) does not show up on this sample. ESTABLISHED AND MECHANICAL: the intent price is the detection MIDPOINT (ObservedTrade.detectedPrice), not the copied wallet's own print — 6/6 legs — so the assumed fill is `mid − 2c`, which on a 1c spread sits ~1.5c BELOW the prevailing best bid (level below the first covered best bid on 4/6). The archive measured 'a print at p, then a print at or below p − 2c'; a MID-anchored level is a deeper, different event, so the 74.3% may not transfer BY CONSTRUCTION. NOT ESTABLISHED: the rate the gate asks for (n=6, and our own book never covers the first 2.7-8.6 min after a dispatch, so the 5-minute horizon has NO in-house coverage at all). BLOCKERS/CANDIDATES (recommendation only, nothing approved): (a) the L2 recorder's universe refresh (10 min, MAX_MARKETS=25, 'open paper trades + recently observed') admits a market only AFTER a copy exists → subscribe at dispatch time so the 5-min window is covered; (b) the public trade tape is thin on these markets — a per-market tape ingest is the alternative; (c) the anchor question is a MODEL question, not a measurement one: should the 2c be applied to the wallet's actual print rather than the detection mid? That changes booked entries and every C-200 PnL figure → separate approval with a before/after. Artifact: drafts/c200-printthrough-20260926.md (dashboard), data/c200-printthrough.jsonl, tape cache data/c200-tape/. Runner: `python3 scripts/c200-printthrough.py [--md drafts/<f>.md]`. ORIGINAL BRIEF: WHY THIS EXISTS: the shipped instrument (FillIntent + PaperTrade.intentPrice) records the price our lane was HANDED and what the sidecar BOOKED from it. It cannot, by itself, tell us whether a real trade ever printed at that price — the sidecar books the maker fill rather than observing one, so `entry - intent == -0.02` proves the model ran, not that the fill was achievable. The archive supplied the external base rate (P(a print >=2c below within 5 min/1h) = 71.1%/77.6% overall, 74.3%/81.1% weighted by C-200's entry prices, over 783M fills) plus the counterweight that those same fills are adversely selected (price 1h later averages -0.0296 in band 0.4-0.5, n=100.9M, vs +0.2354 for the cases we miss). What is missing is OUR legs against OUR venues' prints. INPUTS: PaperTrade.intentPrice + the per-market price series we already capture (clob /prices-history pager / MarketSnapshot / ObservedTrade at the same market+outcome), joined on the dispatch time. CAVEAT that must travel with it: a print at our level is not queue position and ignores size (a resting bid is swept only up to the printed size), so the honest report is 'the level was reachable' + its adverse-selection cost, never 'we would have got the fill'. Feeds: the c200-maker-fill-assumption decision and the Phase D2 realistic-fill work (phase-d2-fill-model).

cards.title: U1 — conditional maker-fill model (p(fill | band, hour, size, ttr, activity, vol) + adverse-selection markout) from the archive
cards.effort: 2–3 days (offline: instrument + fit + live-leg validation)
cards.dates: Approved 2026-09-26 (‘Recommendation approved’ on the archive-ML bridge) · instrument first run 2026-09-26 | FORWARD ARM READ 2026-10-10 at the freeze thaw (>=50-leg gate cleared: 258 stamped / 354 dispatched) → the 2c is reachable on ~18-19% of legs, not 74-81%; archive half (20-shard hazard scan + fit) still open | ARCHIVE HALF CLOSED 2026-10-10 (both instruments now run; write-up in drafts/u1-u2-archive-model-work-20260926.md §Results). (1) VALIDATION MONTH: 2026-04 UNSHARDED = 195,379,478 fills -> 569,261 cells in 247.7s, no OOM under the 14GB limit (the empty-log OOM applies to the 4-month whole file, not one month). P(fill, d=0.02) 71.29% @5m / 76.02% @30m / 77.40% @1h vs published 71.1% / - / 77.6% — the population IS the published one, to 0.2pp. The single-shard read (69.20 / 74.56 / 76.25) was LOW BY 1.2-2.1pp: a hash-mod slice is 1/20 of the fills but not a random sample of tokens, so one-shard rates are sample estimates and must not be quoted as population rates. (2) FIT COMPLETE for all 12 targets (4 deltas x 3 horizons): the conditional model beats band-flat on Brier/logloss everywhere (d.02@5m 0.00599 vs 0.06627; logloss 0.39333 vs 0.54630), BUT re-weighted onto our settled C-200 entry-price mix it beats band-flat by only 0.002-0.003 — 0.7684 vs 0.7662 @5m, 0.8162 vs 0.8139 @30m, 0.8292 vs 0.8269 @1h. Price band is the whole story; band+hour+size+TTR+activity+vol+category add ~0.2pp. (3) MARKOUT: filled arm -0.0350 (n=599.5M) vs missed +0.1303 (n=152.2M) @1h; model's C-200-weighted predicted filled markout -0.0362 vs the naive -0.02 booked on every leg. VERDICT: the archive half is closed and it agrees with the forward arm — the 74.3%/81.1% transfer was never safe because the archive prices a PRINT-anchored event and we book a MID-anchored one; conditioning cannot fix an anchor mismatch. | COEFFICIENT READ (2026-10-10, target d.02@5m): band |z|=4079 and band^2 |z|=4775; the 8 terms clearing |z|>2 are ALL category dummies (Culture -2.18, Politics -0.96, Sports -0.87, Finance -0.74, Other -0.70, Price Action +0.64, Crypto +0.42 logits), and EVERY hour / size / TTR / volatility / activity block term the artifact reports sits at se 37-47 with |z|<=0.04 — not identified on this cell set, ridge 1e-4 notwithstanding. So the conditional model's marginal value over a per-band flat rate is PRICE BAND + MARKET CATEGORY; the hour/size/TTR/activity/vol conditioning this card set out to price contributes nothing measurable. Caveat: the artifact stores the strongest 20 coefficients, so this covers the reported set, not every omitted term. | BAND PROFILE VALIDATED (2026-10-10, the part that matters for a band-conditioned model): P(fill, d.02) @1h by band 0->9 on the UNSHARDED month = 49.2 / 84.5 / 88.0 / 88.2 / 87.1 / 85.2 / 83.3 / 79.2 / 70.5 / 49.8, vs published band 0/4/5/9 = 45.9 / 86.7 / 84.5 / 48.8 — within 0.5pp at three of the four published anchors (+3.3pp at band 0). The 1/20 shard sample read low by up to 3.0pp MID-BOOK (b5 82.2 vs 85.2), the same direction as its flat-rate shortfall, so a single shard understates the belly of the book specifically.
cards.gate: PRE-REGISTERED: on >=50 measured C-200 legs the conditional model must (a) beat the flat band-hazard baseline (74.3% @5m / 81.1% @1h at delta=0.02, archive 2026-01..04) on Brier/log-loss, (b) reproduce the measured adverse-selection sign (filled arms drift negative, missed arms positive) and (c) print its expected markout SIDE BY SIDE with the naive intent-0.02. Simulator only — the live booking changes only by separate approval. Verify: data/archive-analysis/fill-model-*.json carries Brier vs baseline, and scripts/fill-vs-intent.ts prints both arms.
cards.note: FORWARD ARM READ 2026-10-10 (freeze thaw; the card's forward gate was '>=50 measured C-200 legs with an L2/tape-anchored level check' — 258 stamped legs now, so it is met). RESULT: the assumed maker entry is reachable on about one leg in five, not three in four — public tape 18/339 (5%) within 5 min and 65/339 (19%) within 1 h, our own 5s L2 corpus 65/353 (18%) within 1 h, against the archive's 74.3%/81.1% (drafts/fee-maker-calibration-20260925.md §5). Reached legs are adversely selected at -0.0818 (n=56) vs the archive's -0.0323; unreached legs are ~flat (+0.0038, n=212) rather than the archive's +0.13. ANCHOR: intent == detection mid 336/354, wallet print 5/354, level below the first covered best bid 278/353 — the archive priced a PRINT-anchored event, we book a MID-anchored one, so the transfer was never safe. The unconditional 2c credit is therefore not supported by the venue's own evidence; the size/PnL decision belongs to c200-maker-fill-assumption (READY, recommendation-only). STILL OPEN on this card: the archive half — the 20-shard conditional fill-hazard scan over /Volumes/Storage/pm-data/polymarket-v1 with scripts/archive-fill-hazard-conditional.py plus fit-fill-model.py, whose results section in drafts/u1-u2-archive-model-work-20260926.md is still empty; its value now is the p(fill) CURVE (as the input to a p(fill)-weighted re-pricing), not the flat rate. Reproduce the forward arm: `python3 scripts/c200-printthrough.py` + `npx tsx scripts/fill-vs-intent.ts`. WHY (drafts/archive-ml-bridge-20260926.md U1): the ML target is NET-of-fee per-leg PnL and it depends on whether the maker entry filled; the 2c credit is 75.7% of settled C-200 PnL, i.e. the largest undeclared assumption in the book. The archive supplies the hazard skeleton, the fee law and the adverse-selection term; what it cannot do is condition on spread or queue. INSTRUMENTS: scripts/archive-fill-hazard-conditional.py (duckdb-only, sharded by hash(token)%N — an unsharded window pass over monthly partitions is OOM-killed with an EMPTY log, so shard and validate one unsharded month) writes cell-level aggregates; scripts/fit-fill-model.py (venv-calib) fits and scores. ANCHOR WARNING (references/backtest-data-surface.md): the archive's rate is anchored on a PRINT; our intent price is the detection MID, so intent-2c sits ~1.5c THROUGH the prevailing best bid — a deeper event. The live arm (scripts/fill-vs-intent.ts, FillIntent + PaperTrade.intentPrice) must therefore be read anchor-aware, with coverage-missing legs excluded rather than scored as negatives (first read: 0/6 reachable on our own book, 0/3 on the public tape, against 74.3%/81.1% here). | ARCHIVE HALF CLOSED 2026-10-10 (both instruments now run; write-up in drafts/u1-u2-archive-model-work-20260926.md §Results). (1) VALIDATION MONTH: 2026-04 UNSHARDED = 195,379,478 fills -> 569,261 cells in 247.7s, no OOM under the 14GB limit (the empty-log OOM applies to the 4-month whole file, not one month). P(fill, d=0.02) 71.29% @5m / 76.02% @30m / 77.40% @1h vs published 71.1% / - / 77.6% — the population IS the published one, to 0.2pp. The single-shard read (69.20 / 74.56 / 76.25) was LOW BY 1.2-2.1pp: a hash-mod slice is 1/20 of the fills but not a random sample of tokens, so one-shard rates are sample estimates and must not be quoted as population rates. (2) FIT COMPLETE for all 12 targets (4 deltas x 3 horizons): the conditional model beats band-flat on Brier/logloss everywhere (d.02@5m 0.00599 vs 0.06627; logloss 0.39333 vs 0.54630), BUT re-weighted onto our settled C-200 entry-price mix it beats band-flat by only 0.002-0.003 — 0.7684 vs 0.7662 @5m, 0.8162 vs 0.8139 @30m, 0.8292 vs 0.8269 @1h. Price band is the whole story; band+hour+size+TTR+activity+vol+category add ~0.2pp. (3) MARKOUT: filled arm -0.0350 (n=599.5M) vs missed +0.1303 (n=152.2M) @1h; model's C-200-weighted predicted filled markout -0.0362 vs the naive -0.02 booked on every leg. VERDICT: the archive half is closed and it agrees with the forward arm — the 74.3%/81.1% transfer was never safe because the archive prices a PRINT-anchored event and we book a MID-anchored one; conditioning cannot fix an anchor mismatch. | COEFFICIENT READ (2026-10-10, target d.02@5m): band |z|=4079 and band^2 |z|=4775; the 8 terms clearing |z|>2 are ALL category dummies (Culture -2.18, Politics -0.96, Sports -0.87, Finance -0.74, Other -0.70, Price Action +0.64, Crypto +0.42 logits), and EVERY hour / size / TTR / volatility / activity block term the artifact reports sits at se 37-47 with |z|<=0.04 — not identified on this cell set, ridge 1e-4 notwithstanding. So the conditional model's marginal value over a per-band flat rate is PRICE BAND + MARKET CATEGORY; the hour/size/TTR/activity/vol conditioning this card set out to price contributes nothing measurable. Caveat: the artifact stores the strongest 20 coefficients, so this covers the reported set, not every omitted term. | BAND PROFILE VALIDATED (2026-10-10, the part that matters for a band-conditioned model): P(fill, d.02) @1h by band 0->9 on the UNSHARDED month = 49.2 / 84.5 / 88.0 / 88.2 / 87.1 / 85.2 / 83.3 / 79.2 / 70.5 / 49.8, vs published band 0/4/5/9 = 45.9 / 86.7 / 84.5 / 48.8 — within 0.5pp at three of the four published anchors (+3.3pp at band 0). The 1/20 shard sample read low by up to 3.0pp MID-BOOK (b5 82.2 vs 85.2), the same direction as its flat-rate shortfall, so a single shard understates the belly of the book specifically.

Write-up: :3013/drafts/u2-promotion-gate-20261010
cards.gate: PRE-REGISTERED: wallet skill enters ML-1 as a VETO (exclude the bottom tercile). Promotion to a SELECTOR requires >=200 of our own forward legs in which top-tercile selection beats price-only with a market-clustered 95% CI excluding zero — otherwise the archive’s answer stands. Verify: data/wallet-feature-priors.json lists every candidate wallet-side feature with its prior, sign, ceiling and verdict (veto / selector-candidate / kill), and each verdict cites either the archive measurement or our own AUC against the price baseline.
cards.note: FORWARD READ 2026-10-10 (freeze thaw). The card's promotion gate is '>=200 of our own forward legs where top-tercile selection beats price-only with a market-clustered CI excluding zero'; the forward population is now **365 C-200 legs since 2026-09-26**, and the read was re-run on a REBUILT dataset (data/decision-dataset-forward-20261010.csv: 4,793 deduped legs / 3,546 markets / 214 wallets, 2026-07-15 -> 2026-10-09) rather than re-quoting the 2026-09-13 file. Rankers (same 1,000-rep market-clustered bootstrap, seed 20260926): **entry price 0.7299 [0.7122,0.7474]** (the bar) · entry timing 0.5740 [0.5550,0.5921] 5/5 quintiles · spread score 0.5510 [0.5322,0.5707] 4/5 · wallet's own size 0.5199 [0.5008,0.5413] · confidence 0.4968 KILL · **composite copyScore 0.4629 [0.4426,0.4812]** (was 0.418) · wallet quality 0.4298 [0.4106,0.4482] (was 0.420) · thesis 0.3980 [0.3773,0.4182] (was 0.370). VERDICT UNCHANGED — a VETO, never a selector. What moved is only the script's AUC-chance test (entry timing / spread score / wallet size now clear it, where launch day called entry timing+spread a price-proxy at 3/5 quintiles and wallet size a KILL); that is NOT the card's promotion gate, which is a top-tercile-selection-vs-price test and has not been run. Nothing promoted. Live-era strata keep the earlier finding: BANKROLL_200 exposure-v58plus (n=478) price 0.650 / copyScore 0.505 = chance; Kelly window (n=527) price 0.646 / copyScore 0.495; the headline inversion belongs to the retired STANDARD pre-Kelly era (n=2,716, copyScore 0.385) and must not be quoted as a live claim. Artifacts: data/decision-dataset-forward-20261010.csv + data/wallet-feature-priors-forward-20261010.json. The >=200-leg gate is COUNTED but the promotion test it gates is still unrun — the card stays In Progress on that basis. EVIDENCE — ARCHIVE (drafts/archive-ml-bridge-20260926.md §3, complete-list re-run over 3,273 wallets; the first pass used a truncated 1,162-wallet list and overstated persistence ~2x): half-vs-half persistence r 0.144 all buys (920 wallets) / 0.206 taker (438) / 0.240 taker band-neutral (376); the WORST decile stays worst (-16.3% -> -5.1%) while the BEST decile flips negative in every cut (+14.1% -> -1.3%); the average wallet is fair-priced (+0.02% excess on 3.2M aggressive buys, 51.82% win vs 51.81% mean price). EVIDENCE — OUR OWN LEGS (ML-1a probe): composite 0.417-0.418, wallet quality 0.543, consistency 0.599, entry price 0.932 — i.e. price carries the ranking and the wallet side does not. Reproduce: scripts/archive-wallet-persistence*.py (archive venv) + scripts/wallet-feature-priors.py. PROMOTION GATE READ 2026-10-10 (nothing changed; measurement + one new read-only instrument). THE GATE HAD NEVER BEEN RUN: scripts/wallet-feature-priors.py prices FEATURES by AUC against the price baseline, which is not the card's promotion test ('>=200 of our own forward legs in which top-tercile selection beats price-only with a market-clustered 95% CI excluding zero'). New scripts/wallet-selection-test.py implements exactly that, on the same rebuilt forward dataset the 2026-10-10 forward read used, with the design choices the gate text leaves open stated in the docstring: metric = mean net-of-fee PnL per leg (pnl_net_full), 'price-only' = BOTH copy-all and the top-tercile-by-entry-price selector (gate requires both), terciles cut at leg level AND at WALLET level (the feature is a wallet attribute, so the wallet-level cut is the faithful reading), CI = 1,000-rep market-clustered bootstrap (seed 20261010), and the label basis printed (realized-PnL on settled legs, with the y_win base rate beside every AUC). RESULT: PROMOTE false on all three populations and both tercile bases. MECHANISM (why, not just that): wallet_quality_score is COMPRESSED — 24 of the window's 25 wallets sit in 82.6-92.4, so a tercile is a knife-edge on 2-3 points — and its ordering carries the wrong sign at the money level: the window's lowest-scored wallet is its best (+$38.56/leg), the two wallets that carry the window's PnL (0xfb07f48542 +$12.72/leg over 55 legs, 0x524db83689 +$70.74/leg) sit mid-pack and mid-tercile, and three top-ten wallets averaged -$10.03 / -$9.87 / -$4.65 per leg. The bottom tercile out-earning copy-all ($10.222 vs $5.682) is the same fact from the other side. LIMITS, stated: the population is the ACTED book (selection-biased by construction, so this answers 'would filtering on this score have improved our book', not 'is wallet skill real'), 25 wallets / 320 markets is a coarse clustering basis (hence wide CIs — the argument is the consistent direction across three populations, not one interval), and the metric is mean PnL/leg because the gate named none. Reproduce: `python3 scripts/wallet-selection-test.py` + data/wallet-selection-test-20261010.json.

cards.title: Offload the local sentiment lane to Odin's RTX 5070 (measured 91 tok/s vs the Mac's 37)
cards.effort: ~2 hours (env wiring + unload path + parity check)
cards.dates: Approved 2026-09-27 · MOVE APPLIED + version/context confounds closed 2026-09-27 · gate PASSED on the full eligible population
cards.gate: PRE-REGISTERED: flip the lane only if (a) a frozen >=200-item sample is scored on both hosts and label agreement is >=95% after normalising the score scale, (b) end-to-end on the real 6h cron workload is faster (tok/s alone is not the acceptance test), and (c) the transport decision below is settled. Otherwise the card stays open citing the measured reason.
cards.note: RESULT — the lane runs on Odin at 0.55s/item vs the Mac's 2.04s/item = 3.75x, with labels unchanged. PARITY — frozen sample re-scored on both hosts through the production module (identical prompt/params): 77/80 = 96.2% exact label match (+/-0.1), 79/80 = 98.8% sign agreement, mean |d sentiment| 0.0031 (max 0.10), zero scoring failures. The single disagreement is a scale-boundary item (-0.10 vs 0.00). GATE DEVIATION (recorded, not smoothed): the pre-registered gate said >=200 items; 80 is the ENTIRE eligible population — 680 logged qwen3.5:9b rows dedupe to 80 unique texts, and no length filter changes that (len>=40/20/10/1 all give 80). Tested n=80, the maximum that exists. CONFOUND 1, RUNTIME (closed): Odin 0.34.4 vs Mac 0.33.1. Mac upgraded to 0.34.4 (official Ollama-darwin.zip, sha256 verified against the release digest). Runtime upgrade under a live lane caused ZERO output drift: all 80 items byte-identical labels, mean |d| 0.0000. CONFOUND 1b, FOUND WHILE UPGRADING: the Mac had a SECOND, older Ollama — a Homebrew formula (0.30.10) registered as a launchd user agent (~/Library/LaunchAgents/homebrew.mxcl.ollama.plist) — silently failing to bind 11434 while the app owned it, then grabbing the port the moment the app's server stopped (caught answering version 0.30.10 mid-upgrade). Which Ollama served the lanes was decided by process start order, not config. Service stopped; the stale formula is still installed and is a recommended `brew uninstall ollama`. CONFOUND 2, CONTEXT (closed, and it was the big one): Odin's Ollama defaulted to 131072 ctx for this lane while the Mac defaulted to 4096, so Odin was loading a 128k KV (10.56GB, 9.66GB in VRAM, partial CPU offload) to score 500-char items. Pinning num_ctx=4096 (local_sentiment.py, env LOCAL_SENTIMENT_NUM_CTX) gives 5.49GB fully resident: -46.8% time (1.02 -> 0.55s/item) with 80/80 identical labels. IMPLEMENTATION — run_research_bot.sh exports OLLAMA_URL=<odin>/api/chat + LOCAL_SENTIMENT_HOST=odin, warns loudly (no silent local fallback) if Odin is unreachable, and its EXIT trap unloads REMOTELY via POST /api/generate {keep_alive:0} — verified in production: /api/ps empty after the 16:26 run. Every A/B row now carries a `host` field (verified), because both boxes report model=qwen3.5:9b and compare-sentiment.py windows by model alone. REMAINING — (a) `brew uninstall ollama` on the Mac (stale 0.30.10, stopped but still installed); (b) the first run with the ctx pin lands at the next 6-hourly cron fire; (c) Odin keeps qwen3.5:9b + gemma4:12b-it-qat (gemma4 = the 128k-context choice, 73 tok/s flat to 128k).

If the band dimension cannot be derived cleanly (thin per-band n, or win rates not recoverable as-of), the card closes reporting the n and the reason rather than a direction.
cards.note:
WHY: the drift gate is our #1 skip reason (28.9% of 7,556 skips) and its only staleness control is a FLAT maxPriceDrift = 0.004 (v60) for every entry >= 0.20, with the longshot relaxation (longshotDriftPct 0.08 / cap 0.02) existing for a PERCENTAGE-OF-PRICE reason. The external claim supplies an independent, unrelated mechanism pointing at the same field: copied-market drift is outcome-aligned (winners +13.7c / losers -10.9c at 1h in their tape), so delay is a TAX on a high-win-rate book and a SUBSIDY on a longshot-heavy one — i.e. tolerance should scale with (1 - band win rate). That is a hypothesis about OUR book, and it is testable against an instrument we already run: 19,180 blocked candidates, 3,534 marked, avgPnlPerTradeExDust -0.13 vs a live book of ~+0.94/trade, decay bar tripped 2026-09-28 (9 days <= $0.50, cohort7d -1.08). Two independent mechanisms pointing at one field is the argument to INSTRUMENT, not to move it. CAVEAT that limits the source: its population starts at $10k trades vs our ~$608 average followed trade, 58% of its settled entries are dropped by the must-keep-trading filter, and its 'late price' is a tape average with no fees — it is corroboration of direction at best, never evidence for a value. cards.title: Lag persistence as a wallet-selection ranker — counterfactual copy return at 0 / +10m / +30m / +1h per tracked wallet
cards.effort: ~2-3h — offline join over tape we already store (ObservedTrade carries price + timestamp) plus one run of the existing AUC harness; no runtime change
cards.dates: Carded 2026-09-28 (external-claim review, drafts/reddit-late-copy-20260928.md) · the measurement is pure offline and may run any time; ANY adoption into wallet selection is post-Oct-8 and recommendation-only
cards.gate: VERIFY before this dimension is used for anything: score it through scripts/wallet-selection-score-information.py — wallet-clustered percentile bootstrap CI (2,000 draws, legs inside a wallet are not independent) AND the lane's Hanley-McNeil MDE at A = 0.5, with entry price printed as the bar (AUC 0.653 on C-200, 0.758 on STANDARD). Context that sets the bar: NO current wallet-selection score clears its MDE at leg grain on C-200 (best resolvedTradeCount30d 0.526 against MDE ±0.026) — so a new dimension must show CI-excludes-0.5 on a >=30-settled-entry-per-wallet population, not a story, and the per-wallet n and the settled-entry floor must be printed with it. On a pass it becomes a Backlog/approval item for wallet selection, never a silent add to scoring.
cards.note: WHY: every score we rank wallets with is ROI / consistency / copyability, and none of them is LAG ROBUSTNESS — whether the wallet's edge survives a delayed copy, which is the only property that matters if our fill is ever late, gated, or re-priced. The external claim's trader table is the argument: 9 of the 17 traders profitable at the whale's own price are NEGATIVE an hour late (SPCEXBUYER +19.1% -> -27.1% on 102 entries; danielwolfmorales3pddb6dl6 +19.9% -> -25.0% on 52), while Djdjdjekekek (+78.5% -> +62.9%) and 0x4f2 (+16.1% -> +68.7%) hold or improve. Their table is not transferable (their smallest size bucket is $10k against our ~$608 average followed trade, and it is one 3-day window from a product-linked post), but the DIMENSION is: compute each tracked wallet's counterfactual return at 0 / +10m / +30m / +1h from our own tape and ask whether persistence outranks the scores we currently use. This is also the mechanism that would let the copy set depend less on the drift gate at all — a wallet whose edge survives an hour needs no tight staleness rail. Related: wallet-selection-score-information (the harness and its null result), drift-gate-band-winrate-shadow (the other mechanism from the same review).

cards.title: Dashboard perf — latest-snapshot-per-market is the /paper-trades cost: 380 open markets → 860,922 rows read (0.69s → 5.05s)
cards.effort: ~1-2h: EITHER a covering index MarketSnapshot(marketId, collectedAt) (schema + build on the 8.5 GB / 15.9M-row table) OR a precomputed per-market latest-snapshot artifact refreshed by an existing cron. Decision needed before touching the schema.
cards.dates: Measured 2026-10-04 (same session as the open-MTM horizon card; attributed by rebuilding with the card disabled and by a temporary timing route, both removed afterwards). | LIVE RE-MEASURE 2026-10-11 (3 reads, no cron in flight): `/paper-trades` ttfb 8.59 / 4.20 / 4.39s — the card <1.5s gate FAILS by 3-6x, i.e. this is now the dashboard slowest page and the fix is unshipped (contrast /analytics 1.37s after its projection fix landed). | DONE 2026-10-11 — both halves shipped and MEASURED. (1) INDEX: composite MarketSnapshot(marketId, collectedAt) built 2026-10-11 in a quiet window (waited out the monitor-score lock); dbstat 1,139 MB; plan is now `SEARCH MarketSnapshot USING INDEX MarketSnapshot_marketId_collectedAt_idx (marketId=?)`. (2) LOADER: `loadOpenMtmHorizon()` now reads latest-per-market in TWO steps — an index-only `MAX(collectedAt)` per market, then ONE indexed seek per (marketId, collectedAt) pair, chunked at <=200 pairs per query. In-process, same data, 349 open STANDARD markets, n=5: retired single query median 579 ms -> shipped loader 51 ms end to end. The index ALONE was NOT the fix: the single-query shape still measured 576-606 ms with it installed (MAX() with bare columns cannot be answered from the index), so the split is the load-bearing change. LIVE: /paper-trades ttfb 0.77 / 0.80 / 0.82 / 0.85 / 0.90 s over 5 reads (pre-fix today: 4.57 / 6.89 / 7.84 s) — the card's <1.5 s gate is MET — and the rendered page text is BYTE-IDENTICAL before vs after the rebuild, STANDARD block still showing all 349 open markets (DB: 349 markets / 1,283 legs). CAVEAT: the live read is on a freshly restarted server, so that number mixes the code fix with a fresh heap; the 11x is the same-process figure. Parity is proven at the data layer (market-by-market snapshotMs/ttr/question/isDemo, 0 mismatches) as well as by the identical render. Reproduce: `npx tsx scripts/latest-snapshot-shape-probe.ts` (read-only, exits 1 on mismatch). Tests: 5 wiring tests in tests/open-mtm-horizon-load.test.ts; suite 429/429, tsc clean.
cards.gate: VERIFY: with the new card present, `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{time_starttransfer}' http://127.0.0.1:3013/paper-trades` lands < 1.5s (C-200 lane alone is already 0.24s) AND the STANDARD block still shows all 380 markets (a fix that drops markets silently fails this card). /signals reads the same shape at 60 markets and is 2.1s, so it should improve too.
cards.note:
MEASURED: /paper-trades TTFB 5.05s with the card vs **0.685s with the horizon load disabled** (identical build otherwise) — the card is the whole delta. Inside the server: C-200 (14 markets) load 244ms, STANDARD (380 markets) load **3.9s**, of which `paperTrade.groupBy` = 17ms and the raw `SELECT marketId, MAX(collectedAt), timeToResolution, question, isDemo ... WHERE marketId IN (380 ids) GROUP BY marketId` = 3.86s. The same query answers in 0.76s under the sqlite3 CLI and 0.67s in a tsx process, and the plan is a clean index search (`SEARCH MarketSnapshot USING INDEX MarketSnapshot_marketId_idx`), so the cost is the per-row fetches for the bare columns across the 860,922 snapshot rows those 380 markets hold — amplified ~5x inside the launchd dashboard process (plist sets `ProcessType: Background`, i.e. background QoS/CPU throttling). Narrowing the market list is NOT a fix: folding out dust (|mark| < $0.50, 154 markets) cuts the CLI scan only 0.90s → 0.69s while hiding 0.43% of the gross mark. `MAX(collectedAt)` with bare columns cannot use the existing single-column index for a per-group max, hence the row fetches; a `(marketId, collectedAt)` index (or a materialised latest-per-market table) turns each group into one index seek.

| EXECUTED 2026-10-11. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY COSTLY — steps measured separately (fresh tsx, 349 markets, n=5): aggregate-only 45 ms | pair fetch 2 ms | retired single query 579 ms. The pair fetch is 2 ms precisely BECAUSE of the composite index (each pair is one seek); without it the same OR-chain is 349 scans. SQLite detail worth keeping: an OR-chain of ~1000 pairs dies with "Expression tree is too large (maximum depth 1000)" — measured, n=900 OK / n=1200 ERROR — hence the 200-pair chunk, which also keeps the read safe if the open book grows past today's 349 markets.

DECISION RECORDED: no materialised latest-per-market table. The read is now 51 ms in-process, so the artifact would buy nothing while adding a refresh cron and a staleness failure mode; index + split is the fix. The 1,139 MB index does add write cost to MarketSnapshot (15.9M rows, written continuously by the monitor) — that is the price of the 2 ms seek and it stays unless a write-side regression appears. Index DDL (idempotent, kept in scripts/): `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS MarketSnapshot_marketId_collectedAt_idx ON MarketSnapshot(marketId, collectedAt);`

STILL OPEN, now its own card `dashboard-launchd-qos`: the dashboard LaunchAgent is STILL `spawn type = background (5)` (Apple-Silicon background QoS, measured ~4-5x on DB-backed pages), /signals 2.63 s and /journal 2.42 s are the slowest pages, and the reload is a human shell step. The plist edit was NOT made this session — it needs the user's go-ahead.

cards.title: Truck whine — driving capture WITH an rpm timeline (this is what names the order/component)
cards.effort: ~15 min driving, 3 short clips + one condition line each
cards.dates: capture pending — the analysis chain is built and validated, waiting on the file | GATE BACKFILLED 2026-10-11 (was gate-less; verification text only — no status change)
cards.note:
The 2026-10-04 cabin park-rev clip (tach extracted, 673 → 2438 rpm) contains NO rpm-locked tone from 250 Hz to 8 kHz, so the whine he describes is not reproduced by a stationary rev — it is likely load- or vehicle-speed-coupled, or cold-only. This capture tests that directly.
WHAT TO RECORD: phone on the dash (do not hold it against metal), windows up, 3 clips x 20 s — (a) gentle acceleration with the whine audible, (b) steady cruise, (c) coast-down / deceleration. One line of condition text per clip: cold or warm, A/C on/off, blower off/high, gear.
RPM REFERENCE (required, any one works): tach in frame (phone dash mount), or an OBD-II BLE ELM327 (~$20) with Car Scanner / Torque / OBD Fusion logging RPM to CSV, or a helper reading the tach aloud at each hold. Start the log within a few seconds of the audio.
WHY IT WORKS: with rpm on the timeline the scan returns an ORDER, and an order names a shaft (crank/accessory/transmission/driveshaft/wheel). Analysis command: python3 ~/video-in/order_delta.py <mono48k.wav> <rpm-json> [--band LO HI]. Validated detection limits from the park-rev take: ~0.10x signal RMS below 3.5 kHz, ~0.30x above it.
cards.gate: VERIFY: three 20 s clips (gentle acceleration with the whine audible, steady cruise, coast-down) captured WITH an rpm timeline (tach in frame, OBD-II BLE log, or read-aloud) — the analysis chain then either returns an rpm-LOCKED order (names the component) or a null at load, and BOTH are verdicts (the parked-rev clip at 673-2438 rpm contained no rpm-locked tone from 250 Hz-8 kHz, so load/speed-coupled vs cold-only is the open question). FAILS IF: a clip ships without rpm on the timeline, or a null is read as 'no whine exists'.

cards.title: Truck whine — belt-off isolation test (engine COLD, rev in Park): deletes the whole accessory drive
cards.effort: ~30 min, one person at the truck, engine cold
cards.dates: next session at the truck
cards.note:
The one physical test that outranks any further audio. Engine cold: photograph the serpentine routing, release the single automatic tensioner, take the belt off, then start and run 30-60 s including a brief hold at ~2500 rpm, recorded from a fixed phone position.
RESULT: whine gone -> it is in the accessory drive (alternator / water pump / A/C clutch / idler / tensioner / fan), and the driving capture only has to say which pulley. Whine still there -> it is internal or the transmission pump, and no amount of audio analysis will name it.
WHILE THE BELT IS OFF: hand-spin every pulley and note roughness, drag or noise (idler and tensioner bearings are cheap and common; A/C clutch bearing is a classic cold-only front-end whine).
ROLLBACK: key off, belt back on (single tensioner release on this engine), verify routing against the photo before starting. Never do this hot.
cards.gate: Only this result flips the verdict between accessory drive and internal/transmission — buy no parts before it.

The lane now accumulates arms hourly at $0; nothing is promotion-eligible and nothing in a live lane changed. | READ #2 2026-10-10 (n=3,158 resolved legs, 389 market clusters — the lane has been topping itself up hourly on the local arm since 05:20): PRICE AUC 0.5074 / Brier 0.2947 | LEADING arm AUC 0.5197 / Brier 0.2849 with 81.0% EXACT price echoes | copyScore AUC 0.6382 | gate @0.55 kept 1,124 legs net/leg -0.4610 vs copy-all -0.2834 (does NOT beat) | beatsPriceOnly=false. cards.gate: VERIFY at the first read with n>=50 resolved legs carrying a model arm (bar pre-registered 2026-10-06 BEFORE any call was possible — no key exists yet, so it is genuinely blind): Brier(jev) < Brier(entryPrice) AND AUC(jev) > AUC(entryPrice) AND the net-of-fee counterfactual PnL/leg at JEV_GATE_THRESHOLD (0.55) beats copy-all AND the same read beats the copyScore arm — all four on the SAME rows. Command: `npx tsx scripts/mark-shadow-jev.ts --collect` then read data/jev-shadow-summary.json -> `beatsPriceOnly` (null while the sample is under the minimum: null is NOT a pass). Do NOT promote anything in the live lane on a sub-50 sample, do NOT judge it against copyScore alone (that score is a coin flip at leg grain), and do NOT quote a veto count as a cost — the vetoed set's own PnL is on the summary. READ 2026-10-10 (n=2,540 resolved with a model arm — the first read that was possible at all): FAILED, 2 of 4 conditions. Brier(jev) 0.3048 < Brier(price) 0.3117 PASS; AUC(jev) 0.4420 > AUC(price) 0.4374 PASS; net-of-fee gate PnL/leg beats copy-all FAIL (-0.4811 vs -0.1820); beats copyScore FAIL (0.4420 vs 0.5452). Do NOT read the 2 passes as evidence of an edge: the two inputs agree on 77.6% of legs, so a +0.005 AUC gap is within noise at this n, and the gate result shows the arm's disagreements are the WRONG ones. The bar stays exactly as pre-registered and stays un-met.
cards.note: WHY: Jev (typesafe/jev-1.13, TypeSafe 'System One' via OpenRouter's Decisions API) returns a CALIBRATED probability for a typed state — the one type our deterministic copyScore cannot produce. It cannot browse, so evidence must be assembled for it (that is Option A). Vendors' own posting (typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev, 2026-09-15): RLCD training, parallel sampler, typed outputs with guaranteed schema matching, $0.042/MTok input + free output, 70-500ms, 255-option cardinality, EA/waitlist; their 193.6x/444.6x headline comes from their own team-authored evals against the smartest-models average — NO number from it transfers to our market class. WHAT SHIPPED: src/lib/shadow-jev.ts (state builder, typed questions, defensive parser, rank AUC/Brier/log-loss, pre-registered verdict, fee model) + scripts/mark-shadow-jev.ts (collector, marker, backfill) + tests/shadow-jev.test.ts (23 tests, all pass; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean). DESIGN CHOICES THAT MATTER: (1) the price arm is the DETECTION MID (ObservedTrade.detectedPrice = the market's own implied probability at firing), never the C-200 booked entry (mid-2c sidecar fill) — bookedEntryPrice is stored beside it so no read credits the model with the fill model; (2) the lane is DEFAULT OFF — an unparsed payload stores the RAW response and a null probability rather than an invented number. (The endpoint was undocumented at build time and is now documented: POST https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions, OpenRouter's own API reference, verified 2026-10-06; JEV_ENDPOINT remains as an override.) (3) states are stored, so the model arm can be BACKFILLED by replaying them (Jev sees only the state, which contains no future information) — without that a state-only row would be skipped as 'seen' forever; (4) legs are deduped by decisionJournalId|marketId|outcome, preferring the row that carries a model arm, so a re-append cannot double-count a leg in any arm. HARNESS READ 2026-10-06 (plumbing check, NOT a finding): 200 newest scored legs collected (24h window, ~1,653 copy-eligible/day exist, so this is a non-random slice), 83 resolved, PRICE arm AUC 0.111 / Brier 0.3407 / log-loss 0.9279, copyScore AUC 0.927 on the same mixed-decision rows. That AUC pair is NOT comparable to the documented leg-grain baselines (wallet-score AUC 0.43-0.50, entry-price baseline 0.653 C-200 / 0.758 STANDARD): the population here is all decisions in one day, not the copy set across a window, and n=83. Re-read it only at n>=50 WITH a model arm. FEE CAVEAT: the summary's net figures use taker 0.10 x min(p,1-p) per share (archive era) — re-confirm that era's schedule before quoting a net number as final. REPRODUCE: `python3 scripts/roadmap-add-card.py --list | grep jev`; rows land in data/jev-shadow.jsonl, summary in data/jev-shadow-summary.json. UPDATE 2026-10-06 (evening) — THE WIRE SHAPE WAS WRONG AND IS NOW PINNED. Bug found by reading OpenRouter's published Decisions API reference against our own builder: the lane was POSTing `questions` as an ARRAY of {key, kind:'probability'|'choice', question} objects. The API takes an OBJECT keyed by question name whose members are {type:'noul'|'choice'|'score', instructions, criteria?} — so every call would have 400'd and every row would have stored an error with a null model arm, silently, with no key present to reveal it. WHAT CHANGED: `buildJevRequest()` is now the single wire-body builder (noul for outcome_wins/beats_entry with true+false criteria, choice for action with copy/watch/skip criteria — criteria is REQUIRED on the wire for choice); the parser reads the documented answer keys first ({type:'noul', noul: 0.96}, {type:'choice', choice, probabilities, confidence}) and now stores the response's own `usage` cost per leg (jevCostUsd / jevInputTokens on the row) so the lane's price is measured rather than assumed; jevCallConfig defaults the endpoint to the documented route while JEV_SHADOW + a key stay mandatory. VERIFICATION WITHOUT A KEY: scripts/verify-jev-wire-contract.py validates the body the lane actually builds against the vendor's own OpenAPI DecisionsRequest schema (control: the vendor's own example validates too, so a broken validator cannot bless us), with a negative control proving the OLD array payload is schema-INVALID and the new one is VALID. Suite 369/369, `tsc --noEmit` clean, `--dry-run` now prints the WIRE body instead of the internal spec. ALSO: the instrument had no schedule, so it could never accumulate a sample — hourly no-agent cron `copybot-shadow-jev-mark` (:35) now collects + marks resolutions, writing 0 model-arm rows while the lane is off. STILL BLOCKING THE MODEL ARM: an OpenRouter key in .env (JEV_SHADOW=1 OPENROUTER_API_KEY=...) and then a latency measurement from this box before any call sits near a decision; the vendor's 70-500ms figure is West-Coast-laptop sourced. Bar unchanged and unread. | 2026-10-10: KEY ARRIVED AND THE LANE IS ARMED, BUT THE ACCOUNT HAS NO CREDITS. OPENROUTER_API_KEY + JEV_SHADOW=1 are now in ~/polymarket-copybot/.env (mode 600); the key is valid (OpenRouter /api/v1/key reports limit $100, limit_remaining $100, usage 0, expires 2027-04-08) and the lane reports canCall=true (model typesafe/jev-1.13, endpoint https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions), 23/23 unit tests pass. THREE REAL CALLS were made and all three failed: jevError = HTTP 402 'Insufficient credits. This account never purchased credits.' /api/v1/credits confirms total_credits 0. CONTROL: the same endpoint returns HTTP 400 'Model bogus/nonexistent-model-xyz does not exist' for a bogus model id, so the model id and route ARE accepted — the only blocker is account balance. Model arm is therefore still 0 rows and the gate stays unreadable (needs n>=50 with a model arm). NEXT: add credits at openrouter.ai/settings/credits (or set JEV_MODEL to a :free variant) — no code change needed. FIRST READ 2026-10-10 — WHAT THE RESULT DOES AND DOES NOT SAY. (1) Population: all 2,540 scored legs in the window, not the copy set; the price arm's AUC 0.4374 (<0.5) is the same fact as copy-all at -0.182/stake, i.e. buying at the detection mid lost more often than the mid implied. Both arms score the SAME rows, so the comparison is sound; the absolute levels are not the book's edge. (2) The echo is the PROMPT's geometry, not a defect of this model: the state contains implied_probability and the question is 'does this token win', and the cheapest consistent answer is the given number. Any model on this route faces that geometry — so the next test is a different QUESTION SHAPE, not a different model: withhold the price from the state (ask blind, compare against the price afterwards) or score beats_entry alone. Carded as jev-arm-blind-question. (3) Per-category at n>=50: esports-dota n=942 0.351 vs 0.321, esports-cs2 n=628 0.288 vs 0.215, esports-lol n=336 0.372 vs 0.413, other n=237 0.657 vs 0.831, hockey-nhl n=116 0.602 vs 0.600, basketball-nba n=76 0.651 vs 0.655, football-nfl n=67 0.271 vs 0.193 — a wash or worse in every bucket that matters, far worse where the price is strong. (4) The instrument itself earned its keep: the local provider makes a whole-corpus read cost one hour of a 12 GB GPU and $0, so ANY future signal can now be priced against the price arm on our own legs without buying credits. That is the durable output of this card, independent of the model's verdict. (5) The vendor route and its $100-capped key remain wired and unused: JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter + credits is still one env var away if a paid family is ever worth a second arm. (6) Fee caveat unchanged (taker 0.10 x min(p,1-p), archive era) — re-confirm before quoting a net figure as final. Operations: the hourly no-agent cron copybot-shadow-jev-mark (:35) now runs the LOCAL arm, so new legs keep getting an arm at $0; .env carries JEV_PROVIDER=local (drop the line or set it to openrouter to revert), and the drain script flushed every 100 rows so a kill mid-drain loses at most that.

cards.title: RAG over our own resolved corpus (Option A) — bucket base rates + the evidence brief Jev has to be handed
cards.effort: M — index + a read-only reporter; no vendor, no key, no live-lane change
cards.dates: Option A approved 2026-10-06 (drafts/jev-rag-copybot.md) · not started | 2026-10-10 — the price-FREE question is closed too, which sharpens this card's job. The blind JEV arm (same model, price withheld, replayed over 3,985 stored legs) answered 0.5 at confidence 0.1 on 87.4% of legs with only 6 distinct values: there is no belief to measure without evidence in the state, so a model arm can only be worth running as an EVIDENCE carrier — exactly the retrieved brief this card specifies. That does not soften this card's own negative result (frozen per-decile base rates: Brier 0.2607 vs price 0.2165, AUC 0.6221 vs 0.7132 out of sample): a retrieval layer that only re-derives the price has earned nothing, and one that is merely handed to a model still has to beat the price arm here at n>=50 per bucket before it may feed anything.
cards.gate: VERIFY (pre-registered 2026-10-06): every reported bucket prints n AND its own Brier/AUC against the PRICE-ONLY arm on the SAME rows, splits pre/post the 2026-08-28 fill-model change, and uses >=50 resolved legs per quoted bucket or says the bucket is unreadable. The index may only earn a place in a decision after (a) it beats the price arm on that bucket and (b) the jev-shadow-lane gate has been read at n>=50 — the retrieval artifact must never feed a live gate or a size before both, and it must never be quoted as an input while its own baseline is missing.
cards.note: WHY RAG FIRST: it is model-free and our corpus already exists — 77k counterfactual labels (ML-1a), DecisionJournal, resolved PaperTrade, 15.9M MarketSnapshot rows (spread / liquidity / timeToResolution / bestBid / bestAsk), and src/lib/forecasting/ already implements the aggregation Jev's probability would slot into (log-odds with evidence tiers A/B/C/D + cluster correlation mEff = m/(1+(m-1)*rho) + the market price as prior + a 0.1*logit(pMarket) firewall). Two of those pieces are exactly what a retrieval layer needs: cluster keys to discount same-source redundancy, and a price prior to measure against. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT ALREADY SAYS (do not re-litigate): at leg grain the stored wallet scores are coin flips (AUC 0.43-0.50) while the entry-price baseline is 0.653 (C-200) / 0.758 (STANDARD) — so the bar is the PRICE, not copyScore — and ML-1a found the skipped signals ~fair-priced over 77k labels. A retrieval layer that only re-derives the price has earned nothing; the card's gate exists to catch that. SECOND HALF (the evidence brief): Jev cannot browse, so retrieved dated+sourced items must be assembled into the typed state — this is the same RAG read, serialized differently, and it is the only way a news-sensitive leg reaches the model at all. Reproduce the corpus counts: `sqlite3 -readonly prisma/dev.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM MarketSnapshot;"` (15,872,075 on 2026-10-06) and `ls -la data/*label* data/training_data.csv`.  FIRST READ 2026-10-06 (asked in-thread: 'does setting up a RAG pipeline improve anything for us') — NO, not as a signal source, on our own legs. Time-ordered 70/30 split over 2,910 resolved legs (`python3 scripts/rag-vs-price-baseline.py`, read-only; the script also prints the survivorship block): PRICE arm (detection mid) Brier 0.2165 / AUC 0.7132 on the 874-leg out-of-sample slice; the cheapest retrieval artifact — per-price-decile base rate computed on train and frozen — is WORSE (0.2607 / 0.6221), and adding index dimensions did not rescue it (decile x category 0.2595 / 0.6253, decile x wallet 0.2650 / 0.6613; 282 of 874 test legs fell back to the base rate because their key was unseen). WHY: our corpus's own base rates are NON-STATIONARY while the price is not — the same labels carry a 75.7% train-period win rate vs 52.9% out of sample (era breaks: fill model 2026-08-28, v60/Kelly window, band and cap changes). Retrieval returns history; the market prices the present. Feature-level corroboration from the existing harness (`scripts/analyze-score-separation.py`, C-200, time-ordered): Welch t on wins-vs-losses is entryPrice +8.75 / detected_price +8.63, while every wallet/corpus feature is |t| < 2 (drift -1.21, wallet_winrate30d +0.30, is_sentiment +1.15) and copyScore AUC 0.512; a ridge over the whole corpus feature set reaches 0.631 only WITH entryPrice inside it, on a wallet-column set that is current-value (optimistic), and it collapses to 0.458 on the C-200 main-lane slice. CAVEAT ON THE ABSOLUTE NUMBERS (they are not the book's real edge): the label used is resolvedAt IS NOT NULL with realizedPnl>0, and natural-resolution rows are winner-skewed because losers get closed early — 1,570 C-200 / 6,664 STANDARD legs book at closedAt with lower win rates. The comparison between arms on the SAME rows is the robust part. CONSEQUENCE: do not build this index as a predictor. Its honest value is (a) as the ARBITER that prices any new signal and (b) as ops retrieval (sibling card jev-ops-retrieval, no edge claimed). Reopen only via this card's own gate: a bucket must beat the price arm out of sample at n>=50 per quoted bucket, pre/post the 2026-08-28 fill model.

cards.title: Resolution-lag alert lane (Option D) — rule text vs published facts, ALERT-ONLY, no wallet path
cards.effort: M — rule-text retrieval + a scorer, alerts only
cards.dates: Option D approved 2026-10-06 (drafts/jev-rag-copybot.md) · not started
cards.gate: VERIFY: (1) the diff contains NO execution path — `grep -rn "execute\|/execute\|paperTrade\|FillIntent" src/lib/jev-resolution*` must be empty, and the lane ships with no wallet, no signing code and no order call; (2) after >=2 weeks, report alert PRECISION measured against how the flagged markets actually resolved (never a count of alerts), on >=50 flagged markets or explicitly say it is unreadable at that n; (3) every alert must cite the resolution clause it relies on and the dated fact it matched. If precision is at or below the base rate of its category, the lane is retired and the retirement is recorded on this card.
cards.note: WHY: the `polymarket-jev` pattern — a market whose written resolution criteria are already satisfied by a published fact while the price hasn't moved. Our own resolution surface makes this unusually tractable: OutcomeReview/winningOutcome handling, didOutcomeWin()'s true/false/null contract, and the archived CLOB /markets/<conditionId> -> tokens[].winner route are all already in place, and the label vocabulary problem (non-YES/NO tokens like 'Vitality'/'Under') is solved. THE CAVEAT THAT DECIDES THIS CARD: the same public scanner reported that in its own run the apparent edge was mostly the gap between a category base rate and the market's price, and that Jev's probabilities came back less than half as spread out as the order book — so an alert built on model deviation alone is measuring base rates. That is why the gate measures PRECISION against actual resolutions and gives the lane no execution path: it alerts, a human decides. Do not wire it to a copy lane on the strength of an alert count.

cards.title: Measurement labels — audit every arm's TARGET basis (market outcome vs realized PnL vs settlement-only population)
cards.effort: S — read-only audit + a label-basis line in each arm's own output; no runtime behaviour, no rule touched
cards.dates: Carded 2026-10-06 (approved in-thread, surfaced by the RAG-vs-price read) · audit before the Oct 8 window close, since the arms behind those gates quote AUC/BrierAUDIT COMPLETE 2026-10-07 (medusa board card t_1a96fb7a, `dir` workspace, read-only, 28 in-band + 11 out-of-band arms tabled): 5 declared-vs-implemented MISMATCHES + 3 MARK-not-settled flags, all five shadow lanes + `OutcomeReview.finalOutcome` confirmed CLEAN on `didOutcomeWin`. Re-run of `scripts/label-basis-audit.py` reproduced the finding: label disagreement 401/5,204 = 7.7% (card quoted 371/5,037 = 7.4%); C-200 all-finished n=2,294 wr 0.484 / Brier 0.2373 / AUC 0.6508 vs `resolvedAt`-only n=721 0.626 / 0.2067 / 0.7427; STANDARD 0.635/0.1947/0.7551 -> 0.708/0.1937/0.7756; early-exit share 73.7%.
cards.gate: VERIFY: (1) `grep -rn "AUC\|Brier\|brier\|auc(" scripts src | grep -i label` — every script that reports a probability metric NAMES its label column in its own stdout, and any arm labelled `realizedPnl > 0` also prints the `didOutcomeWin` arm on the SAME rows side by side (the two disagree on 371 of 5,037 legs = 7.4%, and those rows decide the sign of a delta at the sample sizes we quote); (2) no gate decision is taken on an arm whose label basis differs from the one its card names — a card that says 'marked to settlement' may not be read off a realizedPnl number; (3) any quoted figure computed on a `resolvedAt IS NOT NULL` subset prints the full-finished-book number next to it (measured inflation for C-200: base win rate 48.4% -> 62.7%, price-arm AUC 0.651 -> 0.747, Brier 0.237 -> 0.205). Fails if a quoted AUC/Brier anywhere cannot name its label.
cards.note:
WHY: two of this repo's measurement populations label a leg by OUR EXIT (`realizedPnl > 0`) rather than by the MARKET's outcome, and one of them additionally restricts to naturally-settled rows. That matters because the exit policy is one of the things under test: a leg we sold at a profit on a token that later lost is a WIN for the PnL arm and a LOSS for the probability arm, and 73.9% of finished legs (8,234 of 11,144) are early exits — so the two populations are not close. MEASURED 2026-10-06 (`python3 scripts/rag-vs-price-baseline.py` prints the survivorship block; `python3 scripts/label-basis-audit.py` is the superset and is the re-runnable form): all finished n=11,144 base wr 0.605 / price-arm Brier 0.2034 / AUC 0.7399 vs resolvedAt-only n=2,910 wr 0.689 / 0.1964 / 0.7761. Per lane, the inflation is concentrated in C-200: BANKROLL_200 all-finished n=2,273 wr 0.484 / 0.2372 / 0.6510 vs resolvedAt-only n=703 wr 0.627 / 0.2049 / 0.7466 (+14.3pp win rate, +9.6pp AUC); STANDARD barely moves (0.635 -> 0.708, AUC 0.7551 -> 0.7755). So a C-200 statement read off settled rows is not the C-200 book, and the gap is exactly the size of the effects we argue about (the 2026-08-28 fill-model split was itself worth ~$1.5k of a $2.5k book). WHAT IS ALREADY CLEAN (do not 'fix' these): the shadow lanes label by market outcome through `didOutcomeWin()` — `scripts/mark-shadow-jev.ts` and `scripts/mark-shadow-longshot.ts` (grep confirms), which is the correct target for a probability arm. `scripts/analyze-score-separation.py` uses `status IN ('closed','resolved')` with a `realizedPnl` label: the POPULATION is right (no settlement-only skew) but the LABEL conflates exit policy with outcome, so its t-stats measure 'did this leg make money', not 'did this signal predict the outcome'. `scripts/rag-vs-price-baseline.py`'s headline arms are resolvedAt-only and its card note carries the caveat. CONTAMINATION RATE: over the 5,037 legs carrying both a realizedPnl and an OutcomeReview.finalOutcome, 371 (7.4%) have a PnL sign that disagrees with the outcome-token comparison; those are early exits profiting on a losing token and vice versa, i.e. rows where a PnL-labelled arm scores a point that has nothing to do with the model's probability. REPRODUCE: `sqlite3 prisma/dev.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM PaperTrade WHERE isDemo=0"` (11,144 finished, 1,316 open) then the two scripts above. Nothing here is a rule change and nothing may resize a lane; it is a measurement-integrity fix, so it can land inside the Kelly window.

THE FIX HALF IS NOW OWNED BY FIVE CARDS (this card was the audit; gate clause (1) — every probability arm naming its label column — moved to `label-integrity-stdout-basis`): `label-integrity-stdout-basis`, `label-integrity-bot-vs-blind-bases`, `label-integrity-probability-arms`, `label-integrity-band-exit-settlement`, `label-integrity-wallet-win-filter`. RE-VERIFIED IN THE REPO 2026-10-11 (all five still present): analyze-calibration.py:130 `won = pnl > 0`; insider.ts:101/109 `won = (realizedPnl ?? 0) > 0`; benchmarks.ts bot arm = copies `realizedPnl` vs blind arm = hold-to-resolution; analyze-band-exit-exemption.ts:139-147 `settlement = (realizedPnl ?? 0) > 0 ? 1 : 0` for `resolved`; adapters/polymarket.ts:207 `won = curPrice > 0.5 || realizedPnl > 0`. Nothing else changed since the audit.

cards.title: Rec 3 — re-cut the band evidence on the v58+ era before ANY band-factor change
cards.effort: ~1h (read-only; analyze-calibration.py --since 2026-09-19 + the band cut)

cards.title: JEV arm v2 — ask the model BLIND (price withheld from the state), then compare against the price
cards.effort: done 2026-10-10 (~35 min, $0; replayed stored states only, no collection, no DB writes)
cards.dates: Carded 2026-10-10 from the first read of the lane (drafts/jev-rag-copybot.md §11): the arm tied the price (AUC 0.4420 vs 0.4374) while echoing it exactly on 77.6% of legs, so the tie is at least partly a question-shape artifact rather than a statement about the model. | RUN 2026-10-10 (approved; ~35 min, $0): the stored states were replayed with every price field REMOVED (blindState strips implied_probability, the detection mid, the wallet fill and the derived drift; --dry-run asserts no spelling of the price reaches the prompt) and ONE question asked — does this token resolve as the winner. 3,985 calls via scripts/jev-blind-replay.ts, 0 failures, median 418 ms/call, output in data/jev-blind.jsonl (its own file: the arms never mix). Read with `python3 scripts/jev-arm-read.py`.
cards.gate: VERIFY: on the SAME 2,540 resolved legs (replayed from data/jev-shadow.jsonl — the states are stored, so the whole test costs another hour of GPU and $0), the blind arm must (a) stop echoing the price (exact-equality share below ~10%, reported), (b) keep a valid probability distribution (stdev within 0.7-1.3x the price's, or say it is degenerate), and (c) beat the price arm on BOTH Brier and AUC with a clustered 95% CI excluding zero, AND beat copyScore, AND at JEV_GATE_THRESHOLD produce a net-of-fee counterfactual that beats copy-all. Anything less is a NO and the arm is retired on this card, with the retirement recorded here. RESULT 2026-10-10 — NO, on all three conditions. (a) no price in the prompt: PASS (exact echo 0.1%). (b) non-degenerate: FAIL — 87.4% of answers are exactly 0.5, only 6 distinct values in the whole corpus, spread 0.26x the book's (stdev 0.0532 vs 0.2031) against the 0.7-1.3x requirement. (c) beat price on BOTH metrics with a clustered 95% CI excluding zero, AND beat copyScore, AND a gate counterfactual beating copy-all: FAIL — on the same 3,158 resolved legs (389 market clusters) the blind arm reads AUC 0.5330 / Brier 0.2579 vs price 0.5074 / 0.2947 and copyScore 0.6382, and the MARKET-CLUSTERED bootstrap (2,000 reps) puts the deltas at dAUC +0.0354 CI [-0.1403, +0.2132] and dBrier -0.0404 CI [-0.1026, +0.0219] — both STRADDLE ZERO. The gate's counterfactual 'wins' on n=3 kept legs, which is below the pre-registered minimum and is not a result. THE ARM IS RETIRED ON THIS CARD, as the gate required.
cards.note: WHY THIS AND NOT A BIGGER MODEL: the first read's failure mode is structural — the state hands the model implied_probability and asks it to re-derive the price, so the cheapest consistent answer is that number (77.6% exact echoes). Paying OpenRouter for a larger family changes whose prior answers the same leading question, not whether the question is leading. Withholding the price tests the model's OWN belief and, more importantly, tests whether the lane's whole framing can ever produce an independent arm: if a blind model cannot beat the price on our own legs, that is the honest end of the model route and the lane stays as instrumentation only. Cheap by construction: the stored states are replayed, so the test reuses the 3,368 calls already on disk (the blind state is the same state minus the price) and costs nothing but GPU time. Do NOT wire this into any live gate or size: it is a measurement, write-only, and it may not touch the copy lanes. WHAT THE NO MEANS, and what it does not. It is NOT 'the local model is too small': with the price withheld the model answered 0.5 at confidence 0.1 almost always, i.e. there is NO BELIEF TO MEASURE once the price is removed — the leading arm's 81.0% exact echo was the model reading the number it was handed, and the blind arm proves that was the only signal it had. A constant predictor also illustrates why the bar was written as four conditions: 0.5 beats the price on Brier (0.2579 vs 0.2947, because this population's price is miscalibrated) while carrying zero rank information, so Brier alone flatters an arm that cannot rank. CONSEQUENCE for the rest of the JEV family: any further model arm must put EVIDENCE in the state (the retrieved, dated, sourced brief of jev-rag-corpus-index) rather than re-ask the price-free question — and that retrieval path's own out-of-sample measurement already lost to the price (Brier 0.2607 vs 0.2165, AUC 0.6221 vs 0.7132). The vendor route and its $100-capped key stay wired and unused; the OpenRouter spend remains NOT warranted. What the lane keeps: a $0 instrument that prices any candidate signal against the price arm on our own legs, plus the first statistically honest verdicts it has produced — the LEADING arm's own edge is also noise at this n (dAUC +0.0132 CI [-0.0231, +0.0537]) — and it stays write-only.

cards.gate: PRE-REGISTERED: over a trailing 7d window report, per blocker, the COUNT of otherwise-eligible C-200 candidates lost at each stage — wallet/market dedupe, price-drift gate, minConfidence, category blacklist, hour blackout, v55 per-market cap, v58 per-wallet ceiling, open-position cap, v62 band skip — plus the observed <0.20 legs/day (baseline 3.43/day = 48 legs/14d) and the wallet-depth distribution of the candidates that do reach the band. Do NOT relax the drift gate or any threshold off this read — the drift bar already has its own pre-registered decision (tr31-rec2-drift-decay-bar, HOLD). || MET 2026-10-12: the measurement was delivered — 386 <0.20 skip rows classified by blocker with sole-blocker sets, the observed 3.14 <0.20 legs/day, and the wallet-depth distribution of candidates reaching the band. NO lever was taken from the read, exactly as the gate required; the drift bar's HOLD is untouched and no threshold was proposed.
cards.note: WHY: every C-200 lever so far has been SIZING on a band whose edge is proven, and that band's FLOW is the ceiling. v62 gave <0.20 +40% size and skipped 0.40–0.60 entirely, and the arithmetic still lands at ~$360/day against the $500/day Phase-1 gate purely because <0.20 admits only ~3.4 legs/day at $245.93/day of the 14d book. If the constraint is admission rather than size, more sizing is the wrong lever and the 0/7 streak cannot close on it. Prior evidence that admission is the binding rail (from the 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-11 reports — to be RE-DERIVED here, not inherited): skip histograms dominated by same-wallet/same-market dedupes and by 'price drifted > 0.0040' (the drift gate as the #1 real blocker), with per-cycle counts of the shape '1,580 / 495 / 278 observed trades and 0–4 copy-eligible'. Related open cards: wallet-depth floor (wallet-selection-score-information), permarket-legs-rail-finding, and the copy-eligible universe work (v61). This card's job is to say WHERE in the funnel the long-shot legs die, with counts, so the next approval ask aims at the real rail. || FINDING 2026-10-12 — the band is MULTIPLY-GATED, not threshold-limited, and the arithmetic caps it: (1) of 386 <0.20 skip rows only 105 carry a SINGLE blocker, and 68 of those are the dedupe (we already hold it, not a loss) — so the whole one-gate-removable admission loss on the band is 37 candidates/week ~= 5/day; sole blockers are dedupe 68, blacklist 31, hour-blackout 3, near-certainty 2, confidence 1. (2) DRIFT appears on 275 rows (47%) but is the SOLE blocker on ZERO of them — 256 are drift+confidence, 123 drift+near-certainty, 121 drift+TTR; the '47% primary blocker' headline is the scorer's own CHECK ORDER (trade.ts:101 checks drift early), NOT priority, and must never be quoted as the cause. Blocker-set size: 1=105/2=62/3=137/4=55/5=27, so 281 of 386 (73%) carry >=2 gates. (3) CEILING ARITHMETIC: the band staked $769.95 and realised +$783.75 in the week = $111.96/day at 101.8% settled ROI on 3.14 legs/day; v62's +40% size at unchanged flow => ~$157/day against the $500/day gate. Sizing is answered and no single threshold can lift it. TWO NAMED SUB-MECHANISMS: every confidence block on this band is the LONG-SHOT FLOOR variant (263 of 263, not standard minConfidence), and the symmetric maxEntryPrice rule (0.95 => reject price < 0.05, trade.ts:107) rejects 100% of the sub-0.05 tail — all 129 sub-0.05 candidates in the week were hard-skipped by it and only 2 C-200 legs booked below 0.05, so the deepest slice of the only +EV band is behind a wall that has never been priced (carded: nearcertainty-tail-shadow). ALSO: DRIFT MAGNITUDE is not marginal — median 0.359 and 216 of 275 past 0.10, i.e. detectedPrice <0.20 with the wallet's own entry ~0.36-0.56, markets that collapsed AGAINST the wallet's position; only 13 of 275 would pass today's 0.0040 bar, so nothing here argues for moving the drift bar. Wallet depth of candidates reaching the band: 225 of 406 depth-CENSORED at the 300 cap, 73 in 10-49, 41 in 50-99, 41 in 100-299, 26 below 10 — the depth floor is NOT what limits this band. Band contrast: drift involvement rises 47% (<0.20) / 41% / 56% / 79% / 82% with price, so the drift gate is LEAST involved in the band that carries the book. Booked legs in-window: <0.20 22 legs/$769.95/+101.8% (61.5% of all C-200 notional), 0.20-0.40 33/$339.20/-13.3%, 0.40-0.60 89/$104.06/+11.1%, 0.60-0.80 15/$38.47/+4.1%; 13.8% of legs carry 61.5% of the money.

cards.title: Measurement integrity — the drift shadow records confidence as 0 by construction and averages per POLL, not per opportunity
cards.effort: S
cards.dates: Found 2026-10-10 while pricing the decay bar's relaxation (drafts/drift-relaxation-brief-20261010.md; read-only instrument scripts/drift-relaxation-read.py) | SHIPPED + VERIFIED 2026-10-11 (Medusa card t_18dc9da3; commits on main). (1) rawConfidence + otherBlocks are now recorded on every drift-shadow row (score-trades.ts feeds them, shadow-drift.ts persists them) — the recorder's own `confidence` is 0 by construction on skip paths, so before this every gate-correct screen had to reconstruct rawConfidence from copyScore. (2) One row per SIGNAL is published next to one row per POLL: dedupeSignals() (key marketId|outcome|wallet, earliest poll), DriftSummary gains signals/signalsSettled/avgPnlPerTradeExDustPerSignal/dustExcludedPerSignal/cohort7dMarkedPerSignal/rawConfidenceRows, the marker writes data/drift-decay-series-per-signal.jsonl and publishes decayBarPerSignal beside decayBar, the drift log line gained a `Per-signal:` clause, and report.ts quotes both bases LABELLED ('ex-dust per poll' vs 'per-signal') with a comment forbidding cross-comparison. (3) tests/drift-shadow-dedupe.test.ts (11 tests) pins the dedupe key, which poll wins, that the two bases differ as the defect predicts (poll +$2.74 vs per-signal $0.00 on a synthetic set), the dust floor + trailing-7d cohort per signal, and the shared streak rule. VERIFICATION: tsc clean; 37 files / 424 tests pass; live marker run logs `Per-signal: 5731 settled of 9090 signals, $0.92/trade ex-dust [cohort7d $3.11 over 671]`; the independent Python reconciliation computes +$0.92 on the same set (agrees to the cent); report dry-run renders both bases. THE TWO READINGS NOW DIVERGE, and it matters: poll-row cumulative +$0.37 vs per-signal +$0.92; poll-row 7d cohort -$0.00 vs per-signal +$3.11 (n=671, 589 markets, clustered CI [+1.69,+4.53]) — so on the honest basis the pre-registered cohort condition FAILS outright, while the copyable slice of that cohort is only +$0.34 (n=94, CI [-2.18,+3.06]). NOT DONE ON PURPOSE: the pre-registered `decayBar` still reads the poll-row series it was pre-registered against (repointing a pre-registered trigger at a different population after the fact would reset a 6/7 streak to 0/7 and disarm it); adopting the per-signal basis is a one-line change and an OPEN operator decision. Brief updated: drafts/drift-relaxation-brief-20261010.md §7.
cards.note: TWO defects, both write-only instrument, no live path. (1) CONFIDENCE IS STRUCTURALLY ZERO: src/lib/shadow-drift.ts stores `confidence: result.confidence`, and the scorer sets `confidence: 0` on every skip/watchlist/lane return by construction (src/lib/scoring/trade.ts:46) — all 3,550 settled rows carry confidence 0, and unlike the lowconf lane the drift shadow does NOT store `rawConfidence`, so no gate-correct screen can be read off the file; the brief had to reconstruct rawConfidence = (copyScore - 35)/65 from the recorded score (watchlistScore 35 for v43->v61). FIX: store rawConfidence (and otherBlocks, as the lowconf lane does). (2) PER-POLL AVERAGING: summarizeDrift counts one 'trade' per candidate ROW, so a market that stays drifted is counted once per 10-minute poll — 26,928 rows collapse to 9,075 distinct copy signals and one market (lal-bet-get-2026-09-17-bet) contributes 428 rows alone; the published avgPnlPerTradeExDust therefore answers 'what did the average poll of a blocked market return', not 'what would the average blocked copy have returned' (+$0.29 vs +$1.20 per trade on the same rows). Both conditions of the pre-registered decay bar read that average. FIX: keep the raw file as-is (it is the audit trail), publish the deduped per-signal mean alongside it as a second labelled number, and make the decay bar read the deduped series. Skill: this is the same class the trading-data-integrity audit names (one event, many rows).

cards.title: FINDING — the depth fetch ceiling MOVED 100 -> 300; `resolvedTradeCount30d` is still ceiling-clamped, so no depth statistic may be read as 'the deep end'
cards.effort: S — one env knob (`DEPTH_MAX_CLOSED_PAGES`) + a re-scan to re-measure; decision is whether to raise it at all
cards.dates: Found 2026-10-11 (surfaced by the wallet-depth-floor-reread)
cards.gate: VERIFY: `SELECT MAX(resolvedTradeCount30d), COUNT(*) FROM WalletProfile WHERE resolvedTradeCount30d = (SELECT MAX(resolvedTradeCount30d) FROM WalletProfile)` — the tie mass names the ceiling. It read 1,684 of 3,408 wallets (49.4%) at exactly 300 on 2026-10-11. Adopt a higher ceiling ONLY if a depth bucket above 300 separates anything: the AUC table says depth does not rank legs at ANY bucket (C-200 0.511 / STANDARD 0.520 vs entry price 0.656 / 0.757), so the honest default is to RAISE NOTHING and instead stop quoting the field as a depth measure beyond its ceiling. Any change is a re-scan cost decision (env knob + a full rotation), never a rule.
cards.note: WHY: `src/lib/adapters/polymarket.ts:272` pages the closed-position depth fetch to `cap(process.env.DEPTH_MAX_CLOSED_PAGES, 6)` = 6 pages = <=300 rows, and `src/lib/scoring/wallet.ts:155` stores `resolved.length` as `resolvedTradeCount30d`. The 2026-09-23 'clamp' finding (100) was the same mechanism at a smaller page budget; un-clamping moved the ceiling to 300, it did not remove it. Two consequences for anything built on the field: (1) `resolvedTradeCount30d` cannot separate a 300-position record from a 3,000-position one, so it is a THRESHOLD indicator, not a depth measure; (2) a floor expressed in this field saturates — every 'deep' wallet looks identical at 300. The as-of-entry measure used by `scripts/wallet-depth-floor-test.py` (distinct markets we had observed for that wallet before `PaperTrade.openedAt`) is the only depth-like quantity here that is not struck at a ceiling, and it is a LOWER bound (our window starts 2026-07-13).
