cards.gate: VERIFY: the two arms of the comparison carry the SAME label basis, printed with each arm. Either (a) the bot arm is re-scored hold-to-resolution on the same rows as the blind arm, or (b) both bases are printed side by side and the '✅ bot beat blind copying' line names which basis it used. Fails if `beatBlind` can be computed from two different populations. Any move in the published line is a measurement change: before/after table, dry run first (`scripts/benchmarks*.ts --dry-run` style), approval before the number lands in the EOD.
cards.note: WHY: `src/lib/benchmarks.ts` builds the bot arm from copies' `realizedPnl` (EXIT — our exit policy) and the blind arm from `computePnl(finalOutcome === outcome)` (OUTCOME — hold to resolution), then `src/lib/report.ts` prints the comparison as one verdict. The two labels disagree on 7.7% of legs, so the headline can flip on label choice rather than on the bot's merit — exactly the class `measurement-label-integrity` exists to catch. cards.title: Wallet scoring reads a MARK as a resolved win: `won = curPrice > 0.5 || realizedPnl > 0` feeds `winRate30d`/`roi30d` → `copyScore`
cards.effort: M — measure the delta on stored rows first (shadow); switching the flag changes wallet scores and therefore SELECTION, so it never ships on the audit alone
cards.dates: Carded 2026-10-11 (audit t_1a96fb7a, out-of-band table) · re-verified at src/lib/adapters/polymarket.ts:207 on 2026-10-11
cards.gate: VERIFY (pre-registered, measure-first): first re-derive `winRate30d`/`roi30d`/`copyScore` for the tracked wallet set twice — as shipped, and with the resolved-win flag read from the venue's own settlement only — and price the SELECTION delta (how many wallets change status/rank, how many legs that would have changed, with the counterfactual on stored rows). The fix ships only after that delta is approved as its own measurement change. Fails if the flag is switched without the delta table, because a wallet-score input is a selection input.
cards.note: WHY: `src/lib/adapters/polymarket.ts:207` sets `won: (curPrice > 0.5) || realizedPnl > 0` for closed-position rows; that flag flows into `winRate30d`/`roi30d`, which `src/lib/scoring/wallet.ts` blends into `globalScore` and the copy decision. Two defects in one expression: a MARK (last price > 0.5) decides a settled win/loss, and a position we exited early is credited as a win regardless of how the market ended. This is the only audit item that reaches SELECTION, which is why it is shadow-first rather than a labelling fix. Depth of the wallet-score surface and the fields that lie: `references/outcome-resolution-and-labels.md` + the wallet-depth findings on `wallet-depth-ceiling-300-finding`.

cards.title: FINDING - the ML-1 promotion bar's absolute AUC/Brier are population-specific; price-only fails its own bar on the re-pointed book

cards.gate: VERIFY (the restatement, for approval - do NOT apply unasked): (a) the bar reads as 'beats ITS OWN population's price-only baseline on a frozen time-ordered holdout, with a market-clustered CI on the difference excluding 0', with the absolute AUC/Brier named as belonging to the artifact they were measured on; (b) any candidate read prints the per-era price-only AUC beside the pooled one (criterion (d) shape); (c) the measured pair is preserved as the evidence: decision-dataset test n=1,060 base 0.535 -> price-only AUC 0.7292 / Brier 0.2110 vs training_data.csv test n=2,302 base 0.492 -> AUC 0.7096 / Brier 0.2184, i.e. the BASELINE fails the 0.729/0.212 thresholds on the file the model is now fitted on.

Taken literally, the restated gate is UNREACHABLE on the new file - not because models got worse but because the comparator moved. Second, measured half: price's ranking power DECAYS by era and both artifacts agree on the direction - pre-kelly 0.7582 (old file 0.7592), kelly-window 0.6727 (old 0.6265), exposure-v58plus 0.6542 - so 'beats price' is a different amount of work in each era and a pooled number hides it. cards.title: ML-1 fit arm — a pre-registered fitted family does NOT beat price-only (measured, nothing promoted)

cards.title: Kalshi venue tape capture — LIVE at 93% duty, artifacts TRACKED in git (the only irreversible asset in the complementary-Kalshi workstream)
cards.effort: built + live in ~1 h
cards.dates: Started 2026-10-12 17:1x CDT · policy OVERRIDDEN same day by Xman ('override both') to cron 15 min / 14-min window (~93% duty, was 5 min / 4 min / 80%) · artifacts tracked in git with time rotation · overlap-safety proven 2026-10-12 18:53 (two back-to-back overlapping windows: 45+0 bars written, 27+42 deduped, bars.jsonl 3647 rows / 3647 distinct pairs)
cards.gate: VERIFY one week after the 2026-10-12 override (i.e. 2026-10-19): (1) overlap integrity — `python3 -c "import json;b=[(r['ticker'],r['minute']) for r in map(json.loads,open('data/kalshi-tape/bars.jsonl'))];print(len(b),len(set(b)))"` must print the SAME number twice. This is now structurally guaranteed by the capture script's dedupe guard, so a failure means the guard regressed, not that the schedule drifted — check `bars_deduped` in the newest coverage row (>0 is EXPECTED and healthy now that windows can meet at the minute boundary); (2) coverage health — of the last 300 coverage rows, `cap_hit` false and `stop_reason=window_complete` in >=99%, median `hole_minutes_before_window` <= 1.5 min (a hole >20 min means a tick's lock was skipped: a 14-min window is at the practical ceiling because a run takes about as long in wall time as the span it captures); (3) freshness of the ARTIFACT (not the job status) — newest coverage row <20 min old at read time, and each day has a non-empty prints-<date>T<hh>.jsonl.gz plus a rotated bars-<date>.jsonl.gz; (4) the tracked tree stays under the backup's guard — `git ls-files -z data/kalshi-tape | xargs -0 du -k | sort -rn | head -3` shows no file near 95 MB (per-hour prints ~1 MB, daily bars ~3 MB by design; a single file that big means the rotation stopped working). Then hand the accrued tape to kalshi-maker-read-prereg.
cards.note: User-approved in-thread 2026-10-12 ('Do a, b, and c'). Kalshi's public trade tape is keyless but ROLLING: on 2026-10-12 it reaches 2026-08-15 and nothing at 2026-07-25 (~8 weeks; it was ~10 weeks on 2026-09-25), so every day not captured is microstructure history that cannot be recovered. USER OVERRIDE 2026-10-12 ('override both'), replacing the first cut's 5-min/4-min/80%-duty plus gitignored artifacts: (1) the artifacts ARE tracked in git now — the captured history is the un-recoverable asset and a local-only copy is one disk failure from gone — made safe by TIME ROTATION rather than by luck (prints gzipped PER HOUR ~1 MB, bars rolled to bars-<date>.jsonl.gz ~3 MB on the date change, coverage one ~1 KB row per tick), with only the volatile ~0.9 MB state.json cursor ignored; (2) coverage maximised to ~93% duty (15-min interval / 14-min window, ~4-5 GB/day of transfer) to eliminate most of the hole the 80% design accepted, ~1 min of slack per tick left so the next tick's lock is never skipped. Because near-continuous windows can now MEET at the minute boundary, the script gained a DEDUPE GUARD (a (ticker,minute) bar already written for a ticker is never written again; counted per run as `bars_deduped`), and `last_minute` tracks EMITTED closed minutes only so the guard cannot swallow the bar of a minute that was still partial at the previous run's end. Shape: scripts/kalshi-tape-capture.py walks /markets/trades newest-first and filters LOCALLY to the families in data/kalshi-tape-families.json (10 seeded: the volume families KXBTC15M/KXBTCD/KXETH15M/KXNFLGAME/KXMLBGAME/KXNBAGAME plus KXHIGHNY/KXWTI/KXCPI/KXFED), writing per-minute BARS per ticker, every print >=100 contracts verbatim (gz per day), and ONE coverage row per run (pages/bytes, prints scanned vs kept, window captured, cap_hit, and the hole before the window). MEASURED firehose: 183-188 prints/s venue-wide, and a real 4-minute window costs 45 pages / 13.8 MB / 45,000 prints scanned -> **~4 GB/day of transfer at 80% duty**, i.e. the window design buys headroom proportional to the duty cycle rather than a large saving (no 429s observed; the docstring's own continuous-capture estimate was the same ~4 GB/day). The job captures COMPLETE 4-minute windows every 5 minutes and records every hole — coverage is measured, never assumed, and no bar total may be quoted as venue volume without its coverage row. Wrapper ~/.hermes/scripts/copybot-kalshi-tape.sh is a silent-when-healthy watchdog (one line to Discord only on a failed run, a cap hit, an incomplete window, or a hole >20 min). OVERLAP: card bt-data-capture (Backlog) already listed 'Kalshi forward tape' as its first acquisition step — the Kalshi half now has a running source; its PM-side pager + Parquet step is still open. Zero trading risk: read-only public endpoints, no API key, no order surface, nothing touches the PM book.

cards.title: Pre-registered Kalshi maker read — resting-order fill simulation net of adverse selection (option A, second half)
cards.effort: read ~2 h once the sample exists
cards.dates: Pre-registered 2026-10-12 (BEFORE the data existed) · run when >=30 captured hours of tape exist (~1 week at 80% duty)
cards.gate: PROMOTE ONLY IF: net-of-adverse-selection maker EV is positive with a 95% CI excluding zero at the pre-registered sample size (per family, no pooling). Otherwise the lane CLOSES and the negative result is recorded — that is the expected outcome, since our moat is wallet-copy + measurement, not microstructure. Rules fixed in advance: universe = allowlisted families with >=500 captured bars; a fill requires a print AT the resting price with the taker OPPOSING us (a print below your bid is NOT a fill — measured error: that proxy said 390 fills at 0.90 where the correct count is 2); because queue position and unfilled remainder are unobservable on a keyless tape, credit min(1, our_size / print_size) of each qualifying print and print the unfiltered count beside it; maker fee $0 on standard series; every simulated fill marked to the market's settlement via Kalshi /markets/{ticker}, reported as fill-time-to-settlement PnL. THIS is the test — a lane that only fills when the market is about to move against it shows a healthy fill count and negative PnL.
cards.note: User-approved in-thread 2026-10-12. WHY A MAKER STUDY AT ALL: Kalshi's published schedule (effective 2026-07-07) charges taker 0.07*C*P*(1-P) — $0.0131/contract at P=0.25 (525 bps of price) — while the maker multiplier is 0 by default, i.e. resting orders pay $0 on standard series. On KXBTC15M the top-of-book spread was 1c at 0.25/0.26 (4% of price) against a 5.3% taker fee, so any taker strategy there is dead on arrival and a maker earns instead of pays. NEGATIVE RESULT ALREADY BANKED (do not re-propose the naive version): scripts/kalshi-btc15m-calibration.py over 6,438 settled markets (2026-08-06 -> 2026-10-12) shows the last print is calibrated to the cent in both tails (<0.02: n=3,211 realized YES 0.0000; >0.98: n=3,222 realized 1.0000) and 99.9% of the sample lives in those tails — so 'buy the cheap tail at settlement' has no sample, and the question is intra-window, which is exactly what the tape captures. Fill flow measured on the first 4.6 minutes of tape is sparse and tail-concentrated (bid 0.25 -> 7 fills / 1,268 contracts; 0.50 -> 0; 0.80 -> 1; 0.90 -> 2; 0.95 -> 15), which is the sample-size problem, not an edge either way. NO KALSHI API KEY EXISTS: this is paper/shadow only and cannot execute.

cards.effort: ~1 h decision + wiring
cards.dates: Carded 2026-10-12, immediately after the user override that moved the tape artifacts INTO git
cards.gate: Decide and implement ONE of: (a) keep tracking (current) and add a monthly `git count-objects -vH` + per-file size check to the backup log so growth is visible before it bites; (b) move data/kalshi-tape to a SEPARATE data repo (keeps the code repo small; the nightly backup already supports multi-repo scope); (c) external volume + manifest. cards.note: Arithmetic measured 2026-10-12 so the decision is not a vibe: at ~93% duty the tape writes ~22 MB/day of prints (gz) + ~11 MB/day of bars (raw, ~3 MB gz daily) + ~1 MB/day of coverage, i.e. roughly 25-35 MB/day of TRACKED growth (~1 GB/month in .git), on top of a repo whose .git was already 707 MB. GitHub's hard limit is 100 MB per FILE (satisfied by the per-hour / per-day rotation) but the practical constraint is total size and clone/push time; git-lfs is not installed and its free tier (1 GB) would be consumed in ~1 month at this rate. Today's override was correct for durability; this card is the follow-up that stops 'tracked' quietly becoming a 10 GB repo. Also relevant: bt-data-capture (Backlog) wants the same tape for backtesting, so whatever policy wins should be the one that serves both.

cards.title: BTC outside the copy path — what actually runs on BTC, and what the skipped BTC copies were worth (MEASURED)
cards.effort: ~1 evening
cards.dates: Read 2026-10-13 01:0x UTC (question asked 2026-10-12)
cards.note: Answers 'are we doing anything outside copy trading around bitcoin'. (1) WHAT RUNS: the venue tape (live, 15-min, ~94% duty) captures KXBTC15M/KXBTCD/KXETH15M — 215k/210k prints per window, 761/750 bars, no cap hits; the hourly macro lane is the same instrument pattern on the same venue; the btc15m calibration read (6,438 settled markets) shows 99.9% of the sample in the price tails, so 'buy the cheap tail' has no sample and intra-window pricing is the open question the tape feeds. (2) SKIPPED BTC COPIES: all 1,469 of 1,469 btc-updown decisions are skips across 602 markets and NOT ONE PaperTrade exists; counterfactual held to resolution with the venue's own resolution as ground truth = snapshot entry (n=543, 191 mkts) win 45.9%, mean edge -0.0522/$1, clustered 95% CI [-0.0939,-0.0096] (excludes 0 ON THE LOSS SIDE); detected entry (n=1,466, 599 mkts) win 47.8%, mean -0.0419/$1, CI [-0.0835,+0.0012]. The gates walked away from a losing trade, not from edge. (3) THE BLACKLIST IS NOT THE CAUSE: category token is `btc`, the C-200 blacklist names `bitcoin`, and score-trades.ts does an exact token compare — the skips come from the generic gates (drift 'too late', 'resolves in 0.0h < min 2h', liquidity $0 < min $750, price near certainty). (4) CROSS-VENUE PAIR: Kalshi KXBTC15M x PM btc-updown-15m is the ONLY exactly-aligned pair in either venue family, but the oracles differ (CF Benchmarks BRTI 60s vs Chainlink BTC/USD 60s TWAP): 282/287 windows agree over 3 days = 1.74% disagreement, 95% CI [0.75%,4.01%] — and a paired position pays 1.00 on agreement and 0.00 on disagreement, so that rate IS the risk. A single-snapshot ~6-7c 'gap' did NOT survive simultaneity: four back-to-back paired reads gave net -0.1122, -0.0182, -0.0554, -0.0017 (all <= 0). Also: never read PM quotes from Gamma bestBid/bestAsk (stale by ~0.6 vs the live CLOB book). No live-path change; no rule edit recommended. Artifacts: data/pm-btc-skip-probe-20261013.json, scripts/pm-btc-intraday-skip-probe.py, scripts/kalshi-pm-btc-updown-read.py, drafts/btc-outside-copy-20261013.md

cards.title: APPROVED + IMPLEMENTED (2026-10-13) — pre-registered Kalshi x Polymarket BTC up/down paired read, true-simultaneity
cards.effort: ~half day + 3 days of samples
cards.dates: Approved in-thread 2026-10-13 ('I approve the btc pair prereg') · sampler LIVE on cron faa5df74ddf3 (every 15 min) · gate frozen before the first sample row existed · read due once >=288 windows accumulate (~72h)
cards.gate: FROZEN 2026-10-13, BEFORE any sample existed. Per direction (A = PM Up + Kalshi No, B = PM Down + Kalshi Yes), take the per-window BEST net available at an executable size of >=50 pairs, charge the direction's MEASURED fatal-oracle rate as a Wilson 95% UPPER bound (A: P(PM=down & Kalshi=up), B: P(PM=up & Kalshi=down)), clustered bootstrap over windows. PASS <=> CI lower bound > 0 on at least one direction. Sample floor 288 windows (72h); below it the verdict is INSUFFICIENT SAMPLE and no claim is made. If it fails, the honest close is 'both venues price the same 15 minutes correctly' and nothing gets built.
cards.note: (1) WHY THIS PAIR: KXBTC15M x btc-updown-15m-* is the only cross-venue pair in either family that aligns exactly (temperature/oil die on ontology: one-degree bucket-grid offset, 'above 84.99' vs integer strikes). But the oracles differ — Kalshi settles on the CF Benchmarks BRTI 60s simple average, Polymarket on the Chainlink BTC/USD 60s TWAP — so the pair is a BASIS trade, and the basis is the risk. (2) FEE SCHEDULE PINNED from the venue's own structured fields, not a constant: Gamma publishes feeType=crypto_fees_v2 and feeSchedule={rate:0.07, exponent:1, takerOnly:true, rebateRate:0.2} for this market, and the archive-measured law (bt-fee-maker-calibration, $1.21B of fees) is taker fee = rate x shares x min(p,1-p) with makers at $0 — so 0.07*min(p,1-p) per PM share is exactly right. TRAP avoided: takerBaseFee/makerBaseFee and CLOB /fee-rate are a legacy constant 1000 on ~85% of markets regardless of schedule; pricing base/1e4 would have charged 0.10/share here. Kalshi taker 0.07*P*(1-P), maker 0. (3) ORACLE MATRIX MEASURED (287 windows / 72h, scripts/kalshi-pm-btc-updown-read.py --json data/kalshi-pm-btc-oracle.json): 282 agree / 5 disagree = 1.74% (95% CI 0.75-4.01%); the 2x2 splits it PER DIRECTION, which the aggregate cannot do — fatal to A = 4/287 = 1.39% (CI upper 3.53%), fatal to B = 2/287 = 0.70% (CI upper 2.50%). Near-symmetric, so the pair's A/B price asymmetry is NOT explained by oracle basis. (4) SAMPLER (scripts/kalshi-pm-btc-pair-sampler.py, wrapper ~/.hermes/scripts/copybot-kalshi-pm-pair.sh): both venue books read back-to-back with measured venue-to-venue touch skew as its own field venue_skew_ms (the first version measured the WHOLE sampling call incl. the Kalshi depth query, which is not the card's <1000ms spec — corrected before the field accumulated); the mirror sum is computed WITHIN each sample (median 2.20, p10 2.027 over the first 27 samples = 2.00 + both venues' own ~10c two-sided spreads), because pairing the best A with the best B across different samples is meaningless and initially read 2.25, REAL depth on both legs (Kalshi orderbook?depth=10 orderbook_fp ladder; PM clob.polymarket.com/book for BOTH tokens — NEVER Gamma's bestBid/bestAsk, which is stale by up to ~0.6 on these markets), per-leg fees at the pinned schedules, both directions' cost/fee/net and executable size, plus one coverage row per invocation. Kalshi's touch exists TWICE and they disagree by ~1c on the live market, so every row carries both and the canonical `net` is priced at the WORSE ask (`net_optimistic` keeps the better one) — a pass cannot be a snapshot-choice artefact. (5) ANALYZER (scripts/kalshi-pm-btc-pair-read.py) prints the identity checks BEFORE any verdict: the mirror sum (median best A_cost + best B_cost ~= 2.00 + both spreads, so one direction being cheap MEANS the other is expensive) and the cross-venue side spread (PM Up bid - Kalshi Yes ask) at the first vs last sample of each window, because a gap that collapses inside the window is a latency artefact. FIRST WINDOW (n=1, 2026-10-13 01:2x-01:4xZ — observation only, floor is 288): the opening samples looked like an edge and the instrument refuted them INSIDE the same window. First ~2 min: direction B net +0.020/+0.052/+0.063, direction A net -0.139..-0.176, cross-venue side spread (PM Up bid - Kalshi Yes ask) +0.07 -> +0.11. By 6-8.5 min into that SAME window: B net -0.025..-0.120 (only 7/8 samples still qualify at >=50 executable pairs), A net -0.119..-0.181, side spread collapsed to +0.02..-0.01. So the apparent edge was a REPRICING LAG at the window open — the venues pick up the new window at different speeds — not a persistent dislocation. That is precisely the artefact the analyzer's first-vs-last-sample check exists to catch, and why the gate is 'per-window BEST net after the direction's fatal-rate haircut' rather than 'the net visible right now'. Rotation note: samples rotate per UTC day (~7 MB/day) so no tracked file approaches the backup's 95 MB guard; coverage lives in data/kalshi-pm-pair-coverage.jsonl (different prefix ON PURPOSE so it cannot be globbed as a sample). (6) NOTHING in the live path changes: read-only, keyless, no order surface, no rule edit. Any trade would need a separate approval with its own before/after.

cards.title: Weather data feasibility (executed 2026-10-12, read-only) — both venues' settlement oracles reproduced from keyless public data
cards.effort: ~1 session (read-only)
cards.dates: Asked in-thread 2026-10-12 21:4x ('can we pull historical weather data for predictive use in PM and Kalshi weather bets') · executed same session · draft drafts/weather-data-feasibility-2026-10-12.md · harness scripts/weather-oracle-reconcile.py · awaiting read + option pick (B recommended)
cards.gate: No gate — read-only reconnaissance, nothing wired to the live path. The decision this card waits on is the user's pick between option B (pre-registered nowcast-vs-price study, RECOMMENDED), option C (breadth to the other 96 PM city/side families and 422 Kalshi weather series), or none. Verification that the read is real, not a claim: run `python3 scripts/weather-oracle-reconcile.py` (keyless, 12 s) and confirm it still prints Kalshi 396/396 verdicts / 66/66 days and PM 22/22 days against hourly METAR @ LaGuardia, with the wrong-product controls at 1/9-6/11.
cards.note: (1) THE ANSWER: yes, and the oracles are reproducible exactly, not approximately. Kalshi KXHIGHNY: 408 settled markets / 68 days (2026-08-05->09-30, first listing of the series) — GHCN-Daily Central Park TMAX (tenths of degC -> F, nearest int) + TYPE-AWARE strike semantics reproduces 396/396 bracket verdicts across 66/66 days with observations; the same data under one uniform convention scores 384/396 (inclusive) or 379/396 (cap-exclusive), which is how this reads as a data bug instead of a semantics bug. Polymarket 'highest temperature in NYC': 22/22 days across BOTH slug eras (11/11 in the Oct-2025 Wunderground era, 11/11 in the Oct-2026 NOAA era) reproduce from the daily MAX of routine hourly METAR @ KLGA (IEM ASOS, report_type=3) — i.e. the displayed 'Temp' column, which is what the 2026 rule text names. Two days of the Kalshi window lack GHCN observations and are excluded, never counted as matches. (2) KEY INSIGHT — THE ORACLE PRODUCT MATTERS MORE THAN THE STATION. Same station (LaGuardia), same publisher (NOAA): GHCN's DAILY SUMMARY scores 4/9 against PM's 2026 verdicts while the HOURLY displayed readings score 11/11; Central Park hourly scores 4/11, and per-day differences reach 2-3F (2026-10-01: LGA hourly 78 = PM bracket '78-79'; Central Park daily 76). A generic 'NYC temperature' series would have run off by 2-3F on most days. Kalshi's oracle is a DIFFERENT NYC station (CLINYC = Central Park, via The Weather Company, per the market's own rules_primary text) — never share an observation series across the two venues. (3) TRAPS THAT EACH COST A MEASUREMENT: (a) PM REUSES YEAR-LESS SLUGS — 'highest-temperature-in-nyc-on-october-1' is the 2025 market (event.endDate 2025-10-01); 2026 markets carry '-2026'; key joins on endDate, never the slug (a slug-keyed probe read 1/9); (b) GHCN raw TMAX is TENTHS OF DEGC, reading 206.0 as F gave 0/66 days; (c) Kalshi T-tickers read floor+1 ('floor 87' = '88 or above'), less reads cap-1, B is inclusive; (d) PM's venue endDate (12:00Z = 08:00 ET on the target day) is NOT a trading cutoff — acceptingOrders stays true and prints were observed to 22:59 ET that evening, so BOTH venues have an intraday window (this corrects an in-flight assumption that PM stops at 8am); (e) the PM publisher changed between eras at the same station (Wunderground 2025 -> NOAA 2026), so per-era re-validation is mandatory. (4) DATA INVENTORY (all keyless, all verified): GHCN-Daily Central Park 57,618 TMAX rows 1869-01-01->2026-10-09 (17 MB CSV/station); IEM ASOS hourly METAR (379 days in one request, decades available); Open-Meteo forecast + 31-member GFS ensemble; Open-Meteo HISTORICAL-FORECAST api = ARCHIVED FORECAST RUNS back to >=2022 (the backtest enabler — reconstructs what was knowable at hour H on day D); NWS api.weather.gov; Kalshi settled markets + hourly CANDLESTICKS (~40 candles per settled market); PM Gamma events + CLOB prices-history (68 hourly points on a live market). Our own tape already carries the family: data/kalshi-tape/ has 187 KXHIGHNY bars / 44 prints since 2026-10-12 — do NOT build a second Kalshi weather instrument. (5) SIGNAL SIDE, measured: intraday certainty curve (hourly METAR LGA, 103 days Jul-Oct 2026) — the day's high is already final at 10:00 ET 8%, 12:00 18%, 14:00 57%, 16:00 91%, 18:00 100% (within 1F: 11/30/80/99/100%). Market side, event day, median last-trade price of the eventual WINNING bracket over 14 settled days: 08:00 0.51 | 12:00 0.60 | 14:00 0.76 | 15:00 0.81 | 16:00 0.93 | 17:00 0.98 | 18:00+ 0.99 (days >=0.90: 0/1/4/6/9/13/14). Coarse read is EFFICIENCY, not lag — by the hour the outcome is determined it is priced; the winner's last hours carry 4-11k contracts, so those are real quotes. Any edge must live in the DISTRIBUTION (bracket mass vs ensemble spread / max-so-far), which is what option B measures. (6) DEPTH ASYMMETRY: station + forecast history is deep (1869 / >=2022), VENUE history is shallow and perishable (Kalshi KXHIGHNY first listing 2026-08-05 = 68 days; public trade tape rolls ~8 weeks) — an argument to start the clock now, not to wait. (7) NOTHING in the live path changes: read-only, keyless, no rule edit, no size, no order surface, no venue keep/cancel.

cards.title: APPROVED + IMPLEMENTED (2026-10-12) — pre-registered weather nowcast-vs-price calibration (NYC, both venues): sampler LIVE hourly, gate frozen before the first in-window sample
cards.effort: ~1 day instrumented (done) + 3-4 weeks of forward samples
cards.dates: Approved in-thread 2026-10-12 ('B, then card and schedule C and D') · gate FROZEN and committed as 78d3050 at 22:52 CDT, BEFORE the sampler wrote anything · instrument + read committed · sampler LIVE on cron 0598c4000662 (every 60m) · read due once >=20 distinct settled days per venue accumulate
cards.gate: FROZEN 2026-10-12 in drafts/weather-nowcast-prereg-20261012.md (do not move it now that data exists). Q1: at 16:00+ ET (and the 18:00+ variant) — hours at which the day's high is already final in 91%/100% of 103 measured days — is there EXECUTABLE residual mass in physically dead brackets (bracket_high < max-so-far on that venue's OWN settlement station, so P(YES)=0 by monotonicity)? Edge per dead bracket = max( (1 - no_ask) - fee_taker(no_ask) [buy NO], yes_bid - fee_taker(yes_bid) [sell YES] ), only routes with size >= 50 contracts; PASS requires >=20 distinct settled days with a day-clustered bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 0, per venue, never pooled. Q2: every sample with ET hour < 14:00, market-implied bracket distribution (mids normalized) vs ensemble-implied (31 GFS members rounded to whole F into the venue's own grid), scored by log-loss and Brier of the REALIZED bracket, paired by day; reported as a signed delta with a day-clustered CI — a claim needs the CI to exclude 0, and no direction is assumed. FLOOR: >=20 distinct settled days per venue or the verdict is INSUFFICIENT SAMPLE and nothing is built. Drop rule: >2% of a day's samples dropped excludes that day and prints the exclusion. Fee laws pinned (Kalshi taker 0.07*P*(1-P), maker 0; PM weather_fees rate 0.05, exponent 1, takerOnly, maker 0) — a schedule change voids the sample.
cards.note: (1) WHY: the feasibility read (wx1) settled the OUTCOME side — both venues' verdicts reconcile 100% from keyless public data — so the only open question is whether PRICE lags the observation/forecast structure. The coarse evidence said it mostly does not (winner's median price 0.93 at 16:00 ET when the outcome is 91% final; 0.99 at 18:00 when it is 100%), which is why this tests the DISTRIBUTION and the DEAD-BRACKET RESIDUAL rather than the winner, and why it is pre-registered. (2) SHIPPED: scripts/weather-nowcast-sampler.py (keyless, read-only, ~14 s/run: Kalshi open KXHIGHNY cycles + orderbook_fp bid ladders, PM events + CLOB per-token books, each venue's own station's hourly METAR via IEM ASOS report_type=3, 31-member ensemble, raw fee fields) -> data/weather-nowcast-samples.jsonl (one bracket row + one context row per cycle + one coverage row per run); analyzer scripts/weather-nowcast-read.py (census -> Q1 -> Q2 -> verdict, writes nothing); wrapper ~/.hermes/scripts/copybot-weather-nowcast.sh (lock, log, silent-on-success, artifact-freshness watchdog: the newest row must be from THIS tick); cron 0598c4000662 hourly, deliver origin. First verified runs: 3 manual ticks, 111 rows, 0 errors. (3) THE FIRST RUN CAUGHT A REAL FLAW IN MY OWN INSTRUMENT: v1 measured 'max so far' on the LGA series for BOTH venues, so Kalshi bracket 69-70 was flagged dead at 23:52 ET while its own book carried a 0.99 YES bid — because Kalshi settles on Central Park, not LaGuardia. Under v1 basis Q1 would have 'measured' a ~0.99 edge on a bracket that could still win: a fabricated result. Fixed to a per-venue station basis (PM: KLGA; Kalshi: CP/NYC) with the change recorded as an amendment in the prereg file, and the single v1 row DELETED so the artifact starts clean under v2 semantics (documented; there were no in-window samples to void). (4) FIRST-READ STATE (2026-10-12, after the day's high was final — not a finding): dead brackets are visible on both venues (6 in the first run) but the harvestable side is NOT offered — PM dead brackets showed YES asks at 0.001 with ~9 k size and no YES bids; Kalshi showed a NO bid ladder to 0.99 with an empty YES ladder. Under the gate's mirror test neither the buy-NO nor the sell-YES route exists at >=50 contracts, so Q1's census reads 'dead_brackets_seen=N but NO qualifying leg'. This is the pre-registered no-op shape (see the prereg's closing section) and it has to be measured over >=20 days, not one evening. (5) NOTHING in the live path changes: no rule, size, gate or venue decision; Kalshi stays paper regardless (no key). A pass here only earns the right to write wx4-live-lane with its own before/after. Read command: python3 scripts/weather-nowcast-read.py [--json /tmp/wx2.json].

cards.title: Weather breadth expansion — the other 96 PM city/side temp families and 422 Kalshi weather series (SCHEDULED behind wx2's result)
cards.effort: ~2-3 days (per-city oracle identification dominates; the instrument generalizes)
cards.dates: Scheduled in-thread 2026-10-12 ('then card and schedule C and D'). NOT STARTED — starts only after wx2-nowcast-vs-price-calibration reports (>=20 settled days, ~3-4 weeks).
cards.gate: Do NOT start on faith in the input data. Entry condition: wx2 returns a signed, CI-backed edge for NYC on at least one venue (or an explicit 'NYC is efficient' close, in which case this card is re-scoped or dropped rather than executed). Then, per city, the gating question is the wx1 procedure repeated: identify that city's settlement STATION and PRODUCT from the market's own resolution text, then reconcile the venue's own settled verdicts against free public data to >=99% before any city is studied. A city that cannot be reconciled to that standard is excluded and named, not approximated — the NYC result showed the same station under the wrong product scoring 4/9 while the right product scored 11/11, and per-day station gaps of 2-3 F.
cards.note: SCOPE measured 2026-10-12: Polymarket carries ~300 open weather-tagged events of which 224 are daily temperature markets across 96 distinct city/side families (highest- and lowest-temperature, ~$1.58 M 24 h volume); Kalshi carries 422 series in 'Climate and Weather' out of 14,981, including daily families (KXHIGHNY/KXHIGHLAX/KXHIGHMIA/KXHIGHOU/KXLOWTDAL/KXLOWTYSSY/KXLOWTVABB ...) plus monthly/one-off climate contracts. Why this is a card and not an afternoon: every city needs its own oracle identification (which station, which publisher, which product granularity — hourly display vs daily summary), and the PM side has to survive the year-less-slug reuse (key on event.endDate) and the per-era publisher changes. WHAT GENERALIZES FOR FREE: scripts/weather-oracle-reconcile.py (the reconciliation harness: type-aware Kalshi strike semantics, GHCN tenths-degC handling, the wrong-product/wrong-station controls) and scripts/weather-nowcast-sampler.py's bracket/context/coverage row shape. WHAT DOES NOT: the station map (one row per city, with the resolution-text quote that pins it), and the observation-source latency/coverage per city (some stations are not in GHCN or IEM's ASOS set — those cities are out). PRECONDITION WORTH CHECKING FIRST: venue history is shallow (Kalshi's KXHIGHNY series only lists since 2026-08-05, and other cities may list later than that), so for a new city the retrospective arm may be near-empty and the forward sampler has to start the clock — the same perishability argument as wx1.

cards.title: Weather live lane (Polymarket; Kalshi paper-only) — SCHEDULED behind wx2, needs its own before/after approval
cards.effort: ~1-2 days once (and only once) an edge is signed
cards.dates: Scheduled in-thread 2026-10-12 ('then card and schedule C and D'). NOT STARTED — deliberately parked on wx2-nowcast-vs-price-calibration.
cards.gate: Two conjuncts, both required, neither satisfiable by this card alone: (1) wx2 PASSES its frozen gate on a venue with a day-clustered CI lower bound above 0 at the pre-registered size (>=50 contracts) after that venue's own taker fee; (2) a SEPARATE approval is given for the implementation, presented as a before/after with a dry run that writes nothing — because anything that touches realized PnL or a risk gate is recommendations-only until then (standing rule). The approval package must name: the entry rule (which hour bucket, which side, which price limit), the size rule and its interaction with the exposure cap (base $1,000 v50 + 50% x max(0, netWorth - principal)), the fee model actually used (PM weather taker = 0.05*min(p,1-p) from the market's own feeSchedule; maker free), the fill model (maker rest vs taker cross, and what the observed book depth supports at that size), the exit/resolution path, and the kill switch with the number that trips it.
cards.note: WHY PARKED: the honest prior after wx1 + the first instrument runs is that the market prices the NYC daily high correctly once the observation is knowable (winner's median price 0.93 at 16:00 ET when the outcome is 91% final, 0.99 at 18:00 when it is 100%), and that the harvestable side of a dead bracket is not even offered at size on either venue. So the expected value of building a live lane today is negative work; the only thing that changes the picture is wx2's measured residual. KALSHI IS PAPER-ONLY PERMANENTLY HERE: we hold no Kalshi key, and Kalshi publishes no wallet attribution, so this lane can only ever be Polymarket-real / Kalshi-shadow. KNOWN STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCES TO CARRY INTO ANY DESIGN: the two venues settle on DIFFERENT NYC stations (PM = LaGuardia via NOAA's hourly Temp column; Kalshi = Central Park/CLINYC via The Weather Company), so the same physical day is two different settlement events — never hedge one against the other as if they were identical; and PM's venue endDate (08:00 ET on the target day) is not a trading cutoff (orders stay accepted and prints run to ~23:00 ET). NOTE ON SCOPE DISCIPLINE: the C-200 copy lane's gate stack (category blacklist, per-slug cap, hour gates, exposure cap) is not to be touched by this lane; weather would enter as its own lane with its own kill switch, or not at all.

cards.title: Binance data feasibility for PM + Kalshi BTC (executed 2026-10-13, read-only) — the oracle map, measured
cards.effort: ~1 session
cards.dates: Read-only, shipped 2026-10-13 | nothing on the live path
cards.note:
scripts/btc-oracle-reconcile.py (keyless, /tmp only) + drafts/btc-binance-data-2026-10-13.md. MEASURED: (1) hosts - api.binance.com and fapi.binance.com are HTTP 451 geo-blocked here, so NO funding/OI/perp basis from this host; the working keyless hosts are data-api.binance.vision (REST + WebSocket, live trade frames verified) and api.binance.us. (2) Depth: 1m klines from 2017-08-17, 1s from 2022-06-01, keyless bulk ZIPs (1m 2.1MB/mo, 1s 70.3MB/mo, aggTrades 395.7MB/mo), 6000 request-weight/min. (3) THE DECIDING FACT: Binance is the pinned SETTLEMENT ORACLE for Polymarket's crypto price/threshold families - 1,617/1,617 settled markets reproduced exactly (100%) - and Binance-settled events carry $2,177,175 of $2,358,540 24h volume = 92.3% of the crypto book. (5) Decision curve measured: 1 min before the boundary a $50-clear call is right 99.9%, but at min 8 only 88.5% and at min 4 only 79.6%. Traps recorded in the write-up (archive CSV is MICROSECONDS vs API milliseconds - produced a false 50.95% result; look prices up by timestamp not list position; up-arrow reads High / down-arrow reads Low; a 1h up-or-down candle BEGINS at the stated hour).

APPROVED FLAG CHANGES (executed 2026-10-13 after 'proceed with asset universe, venue scope, futures, and history cap'): (1) ASSET UNIVERSE extended from BTC to seven assets (bitcoin, ethereum, solana, xrp, dogecoin, bnb, hyperliquid -> BTCUSDT..HYPEUSDT, all verified keyless; HYPEUSDT does trade on Binance spot). (2) VENUE SCOPE resolved as PM-Binance-settled ONLY: Kalshi (CF BRTI) and PM Chainlink families are excluded from any 'deterministic' claim because there Binance is a proxy and the proxy error rate is the risk; the Kalshi 15-min measurement stays where it belongs (the running pair lane). cards.title: APPROVED + IMPLEMENTED (2026-10-13) - pre-registered 'deterministic convergence' on the Binance-settled PM families: 7-asset universe, 4 families, 2 cadences, gate frozen before the first sample
cards.effort: instrumented 2026-10-13 (~1 day) + 2-4 weeks of forward samples to the pre-registered floor (measured cadence, ~0.2 MB/day)
cards.dates: Approved in-thread 2026-10-13 16:26 CDT ('B, and then proceed with asset universe, venue scope, futures, and history cap') | gate FROZEN + committed BEFORE the first scheduled sample (no sample file existed at freeze time) | instrument: scripts/btc-convergence-sampler.py code sha256[:12]=b06650b8c215 (stamped on every row so rows from any other revision are excluded), reader scripts/btc-convergence-read.py | floor reached in ~2-4 weeks of forward samples | LIVE 2026-10-13: cron copybot-btc-convergence (ad0280a9fa73, every 30m), copybot-btc-convergence-window (f786d4c16939, minutes 1 and 7 hourly — the measured ~11-12 min post-determination window), copybot-btc-convergence-read (869b4fb02872, daily 09:50, MONITOR-GATED on ~/.hermes/scripts/copybot-btc-convergence-gate.py: BELOW / PREMISE / MET / STALE / NOCLAIM / PASS + :E on errors)
cards.note: CORE QUESTION (Q1, primary): on a leg whose outcome is ALREADY DETERMINED from the Binance tape, is the determined side buyable below 1.00 - fee at >= 50 executable shares? Q2 (secondary): is the distance-to-strike on an UNDETERMINED ladder priced consistently with the physical remaining-horizon distribution (vol-normalised empirical estimator, spec frozen in the pre-registration). WHY IT IS DIFFERENT FROM EVERY OTHER BTC LANE: Polymarket's crypto price/threshold families name Binance in their own rule text and our keyless pull reproduces their recorded verdicts 1,617/1,617 = 100%, so oracle risk is IDENTICALLY ZERO here - 'determined' is a computable object, not an opinion. That property does NOT transfer to Kalshi (CF BRTI) or PM's Chainlink families, which is why both are EXCLUDED by decision: there Binance is a proxy and the measured proxy error rate IS the risk (97.795% vs BRTI; 93.06% at best vs Chainlink, every miss within $19.60 of the knife edge). MEASURED CONSTRAINTS THAT SHAPED THE INSTRUMENT: (1) the post-determination trading window is ~11-12 minutes (3pm ladder closedTime 19:11:33Z for a 19:00Z anchor; 4pm 20:11:33Z; noon 16:12:42Z for a 16:00Z anchor) so a 15-minute grid CANNOT observe it - hence a second frozen cadence at minutes 1,4,7,10; one ladder was still accepting 45 min after its anchor, so the close is NOT on a fixed schedule and every row carries accepting_orders. (2) FIRST LIVE TICK (20/20 decided rows, replayed before the gate was committed): 100% of decided legs had NO ASK on the determined side - the winner's book is bid-only (20 levels <= 0.999, zero asks) and only the LOSER is offered (~0.001); verified per token against the CLOB including the outcomes/clobTokenIds mapping. If that survives the window cadence, Q1 is answered STRUCTURALLY (unbuyable at any price, not mispriced) and the gate reports that finding instead of a statistic. (3) FUTURES: api/fapi are 451 here so there is no live funding/OI, but the ARCHIVE is reachable at T+1 (UM 1m klines 1,441 rows/day, UM aggTrades 452,085, CM klines 1,441, metrics/OI 289/day, fundingRate 91 rows MONTHLY, one month behind - the current month 404s until it closes) and nothing in this gate may rest on it. Read-only, keyless, no orders, no sizing, no venue decision; Kalshi stays paper (no key). FIRST COVERAGE TICK (2026-10-13 21:50Z, committed 762ca9de3047): 36 rows, ALL decided, ALL no_ask; only bitcoin (20 brackets) and ethereum (16) had a live ladder at that minute. STORAGE: sizing the series AFTER designing it found raw capture would have been ~47 MB/day (912 B/row x every strike of every ladder), which breaks the nightly backup's 95 MB guard in one day; both jobs were PAUSED before either wrote a row and the fix landed first (undetermined rows only in the first 5 min of each hour + gzip each finished day, rotation not deletion). Measured after the fix: ~33 KB/tick -> ~1.6 MB/day raw -> ~0.2 MB/day compressed, so the 4-week series costs ~5 MB, not 55.
cards.gate: FROZEN 2026-10-13 in drafts/btc-convergence-prereg-20261013.md (do not move it now that the series exists). Q1 PASS <=> pooled median edge > 0 AND day-clustered bootstrap (cluster = UTC DAY, 10,000 draws) CI lower bound > 0 in BOTH the market's-own-fee arm and a 0.07 sensitivity arm applied to every no_schedule_zero row, at >= 1,500 executable decided rows over >= 14 UTC days including >= 200 rows with determined-side ask < 0.99; below the floor the reader prints the SHORTFALL and no claim. Q2 is analysis-eligible only under an estimator revision whose hash is pinned in the pre-registration - pre-estimator rows can never be scored. Taxonomy counted separately: no_ask (structurally unbuyable) / thin (<50 shares) / priced. Identity checks print BEFORE the verdict.

Flip conditions: λ̂(<0.20) rising toward 0 (which shrinks f* at the sizer, no rule change needed), OR per-copy realized edge in <0.20 turning negative at $100.

DECIDED 2026-10-13, USER-APPROVED in-thread ('Approved' on drafts/kelly-final-read-2026-10-13.md; clarified in-thread as continue-Kelly, trim declined). Kelly CONTINUES; the offered cap trim $100→$60 is DECLINED — no RuleSet version created, active set stays v62, exactly zero fields changed.

MEASURED COST OF THE DECLINED OPTION (read-only replay, nothing written): paper trading has no size-dependent slippage and PnL is linear in size for a fixed entry/exit path, so each resolved main-lane copy is rescaled by min(60,s)/s — first-order-exact, same method as scripts/kelly-window-counterfactual.ts. Population: 118 resolved main-lane C-200 copies under journal v>=49 (vs 1,009 lane copies, Kelly-exempt).
  cap $100 (actual): window main-lane realized $3,580 — <0.20 n=53 $3,615 · 0.20–0.40 n=65 −$36
  cap $60 (declined): $2,095 — <0.20 n=53 $2,112 · 0.20–0.40 n=65 −$17

45 of 118 positions sat above $60 and were repriced (39 long-shot, 6 in 0.20–0.40). The overshoot the trim targeted (long-shot <0.20 share 7.8x baseline vs the pre-registered 3–6x) is a size overshoot from cap $20→$100 plus variance, not a mis-calibration — so cutting the cap shrinks the profit driver rather than fixing a defect.

cards.title: Incident — 16h C-200 booking outage: TDZ ReferenceError in fill-intent.ts module initializer (FIXED + VERIFIED)
cards.effort: one-line code move (hoist) + ~2h detect/fix/verify; detection was the hard part
cards.dates: Broke 2026-10-13 18:16:38 CDT (file mtime; sibling-session edit swept into the 22:30 auto-backup as ef566f1) · detected by the 07:00 tuning review (#55, 2026-10-14) — NOT by monitoring · fixed + verified 2026-10-14 11:13–11:16 CDT · fix commit 1b33bd5
cards.gate: VERIFY 7d (no code): (a) ~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json shows NO job with failure_streak >= 3 (the new hermes-cron-health-watch alerts on that threshold, so a silent watcher is the check); (b) the monitor-score 10-minute grid is unbroken after 11:13 CDT 10-14; (c) the 10-14 EOD completes its whole chain to the 'Outcome review complete' line; (d) after ANY edit touching a module-level initializer, `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -E "TS2448|TS2454"` is empty — this bug CLASS is a compile error tsc already reports, so (d) is the actual prevention, not a post-hoc check.
cards.note:
ROOT CAUSE: the 2026-10-13 18:16 edit read `NO_IMPROVEMENT_TOL` (declared at line 122) inside the MODULE-LEVEL `GAP_BUCKETS` initializer (lines 96–98), so src/lib/fill-intent.ts threw `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'NO_IMPROVEMENT_TOL' before initialization` (TDZ) AT IMPORT. src/lib/paper.ts:11 imports it, so every booking path died with it. Reproduced live before the fix.

IMPACT (measured, not estimated): journal frozen 18:10:39 → 11:13 CDT (16h 56m); 92 consecutive monitor-score crashes (10-minute grid), 17 update-pnl crashes, the 22:00 10-13 EOD crashed (no 10-13 daily report, no outcome review, no training export); the book sat unmarked ~16h. scan-wallets was unaffected — it never imports paper.ts. 0 alerts fired for any of it: all three jobs are `deliver: local`, and nothing in the system read `failure_streak` (which jobs.json tracks per job) — hence the sibling card hermes-cron-health-watch.

FIX (1b33bd5): hoisted the const above GAP_BUCKETS — a one-line move that PRESERVES the 14-line sub-cent 'measured credit' band the broken edit was adding (that band fixes a real report/header contradiction), plus a 'DECLARED BEFORE GAP_BUCKETS — do not move it below' comment so the next edit cannot re-break it. The tuning review's alternative (`git checkout efeb2a0 -- src/lib/fill-intent.ts`) was REJECTED: it would have discarded that work. ROLLBACK: `git checkout efeb2a0 -- src/lib/fill-intent.ts`.

VERIFICATION: (1) import fails before / `IMPORT OK — 6 buckets, tol 5e-4` after; (2) `npx vitest run tests/fill-intent.test.ts tests/paper-sizing.test.ts` = 36/36 pass; (3) monitor-score 11:12:43 run = ok, `failure_streak 92 → 0`, booked 3 copies (1 short-TTR lane), rollup wrote 6 hour-rows; (4) update-pnl re-marked 1,288/1,288 open trades (361 markets, 82s), 17 resolved, last PnlSnapshot 11:15:44 CDT; (5) `tsc --noEmit` project-wide = ZERO other used-before-declaration errors, so this was the only instance.

BOOK EFFECT: C-200 realized $5,697.69 → $5,786.43 (+$88.74 from the resolution catch-up); open 18/$147.88 → 5/$44.13 (13 of those legs resolved during the catch-up mark). The first post-fix scoring pass consumed the whole backlog in one run: 400 decisions, of which only 3 became copies — i.e. the freeze did not hide a pile of missed entries.

LESSON: this failure mode is invisible to the lanes' own health checks (the DB is fine, the venue data is fine, the process simply cannot LOAD), and it was found 12h late by a once-a-day LLM review. Two controls came out of it: the cron-health-watch above, and (d) in the gate — tsc already reports this bug class at compile time.

cards.title: Research agent — daily brief (07:15) + weekly deep-dive (Mon 08:30) · fact-sheet fed · recommendations-only
cards.effort: scripts/research-collect.py + wrapper ~/.hermes/scripts/copybot-research-collect.sh + skill copybot-research-agent + 2 cron jobs (88da82871963 daily, 78f0f313c43c weekly)
cards.dates: Built 2026-10-15 · first scheduled fire 2026-10-16 07:15 CDT · weekly 2026-10-19 08:30 CDT · test fire 2026-10-15 09:12 (labelled DRY RUN)
cards.gate: Re-read at two weeks (2026-10-29): (1) did EVERY daily brief contain either a cited material item or an explicit [SILENT] — i.e. is it signal or noise? (2) did the weekly produce at least one recommendation WITH a decision rule, and did its retro name a deciding number for each prior recommendation? If the daily turns out to be noise, cut to weekly-only; if recommendations are never adopted, the pre-registration shape is too vague — tighten it rather than adding more recommendations.
cards.note:
WHY IT EXISTS: the tuning review finds breakage, not opportunity — nothing in the stack looked outside our own book. There was a vendor-catalogue watcher (polycopy-research-watch) and a political-sentiment feed (copybot-research-bot), but no strategy/platform research with recommendations.

HOW IT IS WIRED (three parts, deliberately separated):
1. DETERMINISTIC COLLECTOR — scripts/research-collect.py reads our book read-only from prisma/dev.db (active RuleSet knobs, settled/realized by window, open exposure, per-lane split, 24h decision funnel, leading skip tags, recent daily reports) plus best-effort keyless venue snapshots (Polymarket gamma top-60 by 24h volume, Kalshi open markets). Sources that fail print `SOURCE FAILED` with the reason and the script's exit contract stays 0/1 — a dead source must be VISIBLE, never silently omitted (per the keep-previous-exit-0 trap). Cross-checked: its C-200 realized ($5,781.41) matched the tuning review's figure exactly.
2. AGENT SKILL — copybot-research-agent carries the identity (prediction-market bot designer), the hard rules (every book number from the fact sheet; every external claim cited with URL+date; recommendations only; caps of 1 recommendation/day and 4/week; each pre-registered with a decision rule), and the DO-NOT-RE-LITIGATE list (Kalshi copy-routing retirement, the Kelly regime v49+ / C-200 band policy, the ladder/goal policy, already-measured copy-cost economics, the sidecar maker-fill convention; carded lanes in flight are extended by measurement, not re-proposed).
3. TWO CRON JOBS — daily 07:15 (<=15 Discord lines, one recommendation max, [SILENT] allowed) and weekly Mon 08:30 (drafts/research-weekly-YYYYMMDD.md + <=20-line summary, up to 4 ranked pre-registered recommendations, plus a retro that names the number deciding each prior recommendation, plus roadmap cards for keep-but-not-now items). Both attach the collector wrapper, run with workdir=repo, continuity ON (dedupe against their own previous run), deliver=origin so the user can reply/approve in-thread, and are pinned to deepseek-v4-flash.

KNOWN SHARP EDGES: schema drift in dev.db fails loudly by design (three columns were wrong on the first run and were fixed against the real schema — simulatedPositionSize, decision, Kalshi's deprecated `volume` -> *_fp fields); the dashboard serves drafts WITHOUT the .md suffix (the .md URL 404s), which the weekly prompt states explicitly; and `pinned: true` freezes the model deliberately, consistent with the other LLM copybot jobs.

cards.title: Research agent recon — GitHub asset radar + Reddit Atom feeds added to the fact sheet
cards.effort: scripts/research-collect.py (+8 GH search queries via `gh api`, 4 Reddit Atom feeds, 6h TTL cache) · skill copybot-research-agent v1.1.0 (source tier 6 + asset-evaluation rules + Tooling radar slot + weekly 'Reusable assets' section) · both cron prompts updated
cards.dates: Built 2026-10-15 · first dedicated run 2026-10-16 07:15 CDT (daily) · full asset section Mon 2026-10-19 08:30 CDT (weekly)
cards.gate: Re-read at two weeks (2026-10-29), same review as the parent card, plus: (1) did ANY asset from the radar survive to `audit` or `adopt-now` — i.e. is the radar producing usable candidates or just noise? (2) did a Reddit entry ever lead to a primary source we acted on, or is the block decorative? If the radar is all zero-star spam, raise the stars floor / add topic: qualifiers; if Reddit never pays off, drop the block.
cards.note:
WHY: user asked for the agent to research Reddit and GitHub for strategies and for reusable code, agents, scripts, bots, datasets, MCPs and APIs. Done as COLLECTOR sections rather than as prompt guidance, so repo facts arrive verified instead of recalled — the same fail-loud contract as the venue snapshots.

ROUTES (hard-won, both were wrong on the first attempt):
* Reddit .json endpoints return HTTP 403 from this host, and old.reddit/api.reddit also 403/302. The **Atom feeds work**: `www.reddit.com/r/<sub>/top/.rss?t=day` and `search.rss?q=...`. RSS carries title/date/link but no score. A 6-request burst triggers HTTP 429 on the FIRST feed, so the collector now (a) caches each feed to data/cache/research-recon/ with a 6h TTL, (b) paces requests 2.5s apart, and (c) stops issuing feeds after the first 429 instead of making it worse. A stale cache beats an error and is labelled `STALE cache (Xh old) after HTTP 429`.
* GitHub: `gh` is authenticated as BladeRunner28 (keyring) → 5000 req/h, so the collector uses `gh api` with a keyless-REST fallback (60 req/h). Queries use `in:name,description` ONLY — including `readme` matched 449k repos (`awesome-go` came back as a 'dataset'). The `(a OR b) mcp` grouping was still too loose, so MCP is split into two single-term queries.

WHAT IT SURFACES (first real run): `Jon-Becker/prediction-market-analysis` ★3876 MIT (markets data/analysis framework), `pmxt-dev/pmxt` ★2169 MIT ('CCXT for prediction markets' — unified Polymarket/Kalshi API), `alsk1992/CloddsBot` ★2971 MIT, `warproxxx/poly-maker` ★1512 MIT (Polymarket market-making bot), `LLMQuant/awesome-trading-agents` ★896 CC0, `ccxt/ccxt` ★44k (now covers prediction markets), plus a live Kalshi×Polymarket crypto-barrier arb scanner and a Polymarket weather-market toolkit that overlap our carded lanes.

GUARDRAILS WRITTEN INTO THE SKILL: a repo is a candidate, never an endorsement (licence / last push / does the code match the claim / dependency risk / untrusted-code hygiene; `github-repo-audit` for the verdict); datasets need look-ahead-free licensing; Reddit is CHANGE DETECTION ONLY — never evidence for a strategy or return claim, and never the sole basis for a recommendation.

SELF-INFLICTED BUG WORTH REMEMBERING: the collector died at import with `NameError: name 'time' is not defined` (I dropped an import while rewriting the import block) and earlier with `NameError: name 'REPO' is not defined` — a module-level constant referencing a symbol that only exists inside main(). Same class as the 2026-10-13 fill-intent TDZ outage: a load-time NameError kills the whole script rather than degrading one feature. The cache dir is now derived from `Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent`, so the collector works from any cwd.

WHY: user asked that GitHub leads trigger audits automatically and that the recommendations come back to him FOR APPROVAL IN THE DAILY AND WEEKLY REPORTS (not as a separate ping stream he has to reconcile against the briefs).

ARCHITECTURE (three separated concerns):
1. NOTICE — the daily/weekly research agent enqueues candidates (`asset-queue.py add`), never audits inline: a 15-line brief cannot read five repos, and an audit must survive a brief failing.
2. READ — the audit worker job runs copybot-asset-audit.sh, which (a) seeds the queue deterministically from the newest fact sheet's radar block, (b) claims ≤2 leads, (c) prints a read-only anatomy per repo. `asset-inspect.py` never clones, installs or executes candidate code and never touches a key — it is built entirely from `gh api` (stars/forks/issues, licence, archived, created/last-push, languages, file+byte counts by type, tests/CI/lockfile/env-example presence, manifests, entrypoints, recent commits, releases, README length and its key/telemetry/hype/stub markers). The 'claims vs substance' problem is therefore structural: claim size sits next to code size.
3. DECIDE — the audit records `complete --verdict ... --recommend ... --decision-rule ... --effort ... --reversibility ...`, which opens an approval entry (state=pending). The daily brief runs `asset-queue.py approvals --limit 2` and the weekly runs `approvals` + `status`, so every pending item appears in a report with the exact answer to give (`approve <owner/repo>` / `decline <owner/repo>`) until the user decides it. The worker itself never asks for approval — that is deliberate, per the user's instruction. A `--recommend` without a `--decision-rule` is refused by the prompt (measured, not asserted).

SEEDER BAR (deterministic, un-fudgeable): licence ≠ no-licence AND ★≥5 AND pushed ≤90 days AND not already queued AND not mentioned in drafts/. First run: 4 of 35 radar slots cleared it, 31 skipped (nearly all 'no licence') — which is itself the answer to 'is the radar junk?': mostly yes, and now measurably so.

SHARP EDGES: a run that dies mid-audit leaves items in 'auditing' — `status` flags them and `pending` auto-reclaims claims older than 90 min (added after my own test stranded two); `add --force` re-queues manually. The queue is committed at data/research-asset-queue.json so the ledger survives sessions and is visible in the daily GitHub backup. Audit drafts are served at :3013/drafts/asset-audit-<slug>-<date> WITHOUT the .md suffix.

cards.title: TTR-scaled admission margin — MEASURED, rule did not fire (DROP)
cards.effort: scripts/horizon-margin-replay.py (~1 h, read-only; artifact data/horizon-margin-replay.json)
cards.dates: Proposed by the DRADIS audit 2026-10-15 · approved by user 2026-10-15 · measured 2026-10-15
cards.gate: CLOSED — do not re-propose on the frozen 2026-09-13 basis. Re-open ONLY with (a) a larger basis (e.g. the 2026-09-23 1,962-leg / 102-wallet read) preceded by a power calculation, or (b) an anchor derived from our own realized-vol-per-horizon data instead of borrowed from a donor whose scale is not transferable. A second pass at the same frozen data is the thin-window error our rules forbid.
cards.note:
Idea from mbordash/DRADIS (AGPL-3.0, keys-required => concept source only, never adopted): a time-to-resolution-scaled admission margin (base*sqrt(secs_left/taper), floored, capped) replacing our flat 0.05 shadow margin in src/lib/scoring/price-edge.ts.

RESULT (read-only replay, 662 settled C-200 legs, 132 admitted flat): flip set (flat-admit, scaled-reject) n=62 across 23 wallets, mean -$0.3307/leg, median -$0.8947, win 35.5%, wallet-clustered 95% CI [-5.5543, +3.7130] -> INCLUDES 0, so the pre-registered rule does not fire. Kept set n=70, mean +$2.7552, CI [-3.2956, +8.4363]. Sensitivity grid across taper 6/24/72/168 h: flip mean +1.60 / -0.33 / +0.47 / +0.32 -- the sign is an artefact of our arbitrary anchor, not of the data (the donor's absolute scale is not transferable; the cap never binds). Means and medians disagree wildly in both sets => heavy tails over few wallets.

WHY IT WAS WORTH THE HOUR: a change with no supporting evidence was stopped before it entered the shadow path, the donor's curve was confirmed byte-equivalent to ours (so the fee CURVE was never the gap), and this is the first closed loop through the new asset-audit pipeline (notice -> queue -> audit -> approval -> measurement -> recorded outcome).

cards.title: C-200 sub-$0.05 entry floor — pre-registered read (gate 2026-10-24)
cards.effort: ~1-2h read-only (instrument built; readings auto-append)
cards.dates: Pre-registered 2026-10-17 · gate 2026-10-24
cards.note:
PRE-REGISTERED, rule fixed before first run. Hypothesis: C-200 legs entered <$0.05 are loss-making (lifetime ROI <= -20%) while 0.05-0.15 stay strongly positive, so the missing sub-0.20 flow is saved cost and the variable is an entry FLOOR, not the x3.5 longshot factor. Decision rule: by 2026-10-24, (a) <0.05 ROI <= -20% at n >= 60 settled C-200 legs AND (b) trailing-7d sub-0.20 skip counterfactual nets >= +$25 across >= 30 resolved markets => propose c200MinEntryPrice = 0.05 (needs owner approval + 7-day verify). Else record null and drop. Read #1 (2026-10-17): PENDING_DATE — <0.05 n=31 pnl -$828.20 ROI -55.2% win 19.4%, resolved-only 0/6 wins; 0.05-0.10 +149.0%; 0.10-0.15 +90.0%; 0.15-0.20 +51.6% (resolution-only +3.5% — early exits carry it); >=0.20 -0.4%. Counterfactual: 62 deduped skip signals, 52 resolved, net +$1,483.66 dust-inclusive / +$596.20 ex-dust. FINDINGS: (1) gate (b) is NOT discriminating — it passes on both bases and one 21x winner is 14% of the net; decision rests entirely on (a) n reaching 60; (2) the rule's own n gate may force NULL by default (needs 29 more settled legs in the thinnest band in a week); (3) the brief's '404 skips @ 3.6c' basis does NOT reproduce — DB gives 206 rows @ 7.35c / 62 signals @ 9.16c. Instrument: scripts/entry-floor-replay.py (series data/entry-floor-read.jsonl, appends a line per run). DRAFT: drafts/entry-floor-prereg-20261017.md READ #2 (2026-10-26, gate date +2d — THE FIRST READ ON OR AFTER THE GATE): the gate date passed UNREAD. Nothing ran the instrument: the series held exactly one line, the 2026-10-17 registration-day PENDING_DATE read, until 2026-10-26 (fixed — the read is now taken by scripts/research-collect.py on the daily fact sheet, and every record carries gateDate/daysSinceGate/priorReadAt; a read taken after the gate date prints 'GATE WAS UNREAD' when no prior read exists on or after it). VERDICT: INSUFFICIENT_N — gate (a) n=31/60 (ROI -55.18% passes the -20% bar), gate (b) resolved 55/30 and net +$5,250.66 both pass. GATE (a) CANNOT REACH 60 BY WAITING: the <0.05 cell holds 31 settled C-200 legs, ALL settled, 0 open, newest sub-0.05 opening 2026-10-09T01:17Z, and since the 2026-10-17 registration the lane opened 5 legs at 0.05-0.10, 16 at 0.10-0.20, 42 at >=0.20 and ZERO below 0.05. Per the registered rule that is a NULL — recording it (and dropping the card) is the owner's call, not an instrument one, so the card is left where it is. Read #2 counterfactual: 66 signals, 55 resolved, +$5,250.66 dust-inclusive but +$279.14 ex-dust on 37, with the single best win $3,323.33 = 63.3% of the net — gate (b) passes on one dust ticket, as finding (1) predicted.

--- DECIDED 2026-10-26 (user-approved): RECORD THE NULL, CLOSE AS SUPERSEDED. Column -> Done.

THE NULL, measured: the <0.05 cell holds 31 settled legs against a registered n of 60, 0 open, and the
newest sub-0.05 opening is 2026-10-09. Since registration the lane opened 5 / 16 / 42 legs in the three
bands ABOVE it and ZERO below. n=60 is therefore not reachable by waiting -- the population stopped being
produced. Per the pre-registered rule this is a recorded NULL, not a pending read: "INSUFFICIENT_N" is the
answer, and it is an answer about FLOW, not about the rule's truth.

WHY CLOSED RATHER THAN LEFT SCHEDULED: v67 shipped 2026-10-24 (`c200LongshotBandFloor = 0.05`) and removed
the 3.5x long-shot multiplier below 0.05. That multiplier was the mechanism that made sub-0.05 entries
dangerous -- the book was putting its LARGEST clip ($100 max, $25.66 blended across lanes) on its longest
odds. With the boost gone, an ADMISSION floor at 0.05 would bind on zero legs while the economic harm it
targeted is already addressed by a size rule. Keeping this Scheduled would mean a dated gate that can only
ever record the same NULL again.

WHAT THIS CARD DOES NOT CLAIM: that a sub-0.05 admission floor is wrong. It is untested and now unmeasurable,
because nothing opens there. That is the honest state.

REOPEN CONDITION: the first sub-0.05 opening after 2026-10-26 (any lane). That single row restarts the
count and makes the question measurable again -- at which point the registered rule applies unchanged.
NOTE the reopen is a FLOOR question, not a size question: v67 already governs size there, so a future
reading must not re-litigate the multiplier that is now floored.

cards.title: Split the ML bot into its own lane and bot, separate from copybot
cards.dates: opened 2026-10-19 (operator directive: 'card out making the ML bot its own separate lane and bot from the copybot')
cards.note:
DESIGN v1 WRITTEN 2026-10-20: drafts/ml-bot-design-20261020.md http://localhost:3013/drafts/ml-bot-design-20261020 -- architecture, taker-fill decision with measured premium table, self-learning guardrails, reporting spec, pre-registered promotion bar, build phases 0-5. NOTHING IMPLEMENTED; phases 2-4 are Lane A and each need approval.

KEY DESIGN CALL: the ML lane books TAKER fills behind a 35%-of-mid premium cap. Measured from 8.99M cheap-band quotes: median taker premium is 33.3% of mid (vs 1.1% in 0.40-0.60), which consumes 70% of the band's gross edge; break-even premium is 47.8% and 44.0% of cheap-band quotes sit ABOVE it, i.e. unprofitable by construction. Creator fills reach only ~19% in 1h (ml-u1) so a maker lane both loses 81% of its sample and pays -8.2% adverse selection on the rest.

ORIGINAL NOTE: Today the ML work is a shadow/measurement arm INSIDE copybot: it trains on copybot's own copy decisions (export-training-data.ts), is judged against copybot's price-only baseline, and has no bot_id, no ledger, no sizing and no exposure of its own. The operator's target state is an ML bot that makes its OWN entry decisions - with sentiment as one of its decision lanes - as a first-class bot alongside copybot, not a model bolted onto copybot's decisions. That inverts a core property of the current lane: ML-1 learns 'was copying this wallet's trade profitable', which requires copybot to act first. An independent-entry ML bot must generate candidates itself (from observed flow) and cannot use copybot's acted-only label set without inheriting its selection bias (open card ml1-declined-arm-coverage). Separation work spans: own bot_id + RuleSet namespace, own PaperTrade/DecisionJournal scoping, own exposure cap and daily-loss rail, own dashboard lane and EOD/PnL attribution, and a decision path that does not read copybot's copyScore. Pre-requisite measurement: the declined-arm label coverage must exist before an independent-entry model can be trained without bias.
cards.gate: Done when an ML bot exists as a separate bot_id with its own rule set, ledger rows, exposure accounting and PnL attribution, and every ML bot decision is journaled with the features it consumed (incl. sentiment delta) such that its PnL can be reported WITHOUT copybot's ledger - verified by an EOD report that shows the two bots' books side by side and sums to the same total as the combined account. Shadow-only until the pre-registered promotion gate is cleared and the operator approves going live.

cards.title: Convex-hull gap over events we already hold — does the 2.2% combinatorial-arb magnitude touch our book?
cards.effort: ~2-3h offline replay, keyless, read-only
cards.dates: Carded 2026-10-19 from arXiv:2610.23517 (2026-10-19) + the weekly research deep-dive
cards.gate: PRE-REGISTERED (rule fixed before the first run): group the open legacy legs by event via gamma metadata, keep every multi-outcome (neg-risk) event where we hold >=1 leg, compute sum-of-asks and sum-of-bids vs 1 net of each market's published fee class, and report the gap distribution plus how many of OUR legs sit on the rich side. If >=10 held events show a hull gap > 2x the round-trip fee AGAINST us, card a pre-registered hedge read; if <10, record the null and keep phase-c parked — the paper's magnitude does not transfer to our book. FAILS IF: a gap is quoted without the fee class it was netted against, or the read is reported as 'promising' on fewer than 10 events.
cards.note: WHY: arXiv:2610.23517v1 (Seo et al., 2026-10-19) proves prices outside the convex hull of admissible payoff vectors admit arbitrage, recovers 1.9M logical relations over 255,000+ contracts from venue metadata + semantic resolution analysis, and replays FULL-DEPTH Polymarket books: guaranteed profit after spreads and fees = 2.2% of committed capital, 3.2% at resolution, with opportunities persisting where relation discovery and execution are costlier. That is the first published magnitude for the intra-venue half of `phase-c` — and it is earned at 255k-contract scale with full-depth execution, neither of which we have. So the question is not 'build phase-c' but 'at OUR scale, are the relations we already sit inside mispriced against us'. Our own record says we hold legs across marketIds inside one family (tuning #59/#60: swe-org-gais Org YES + Gais NO; ucl-mnc-aek1 twice) and the per-market rail's live clause is legs <= 2, so the grouping is small and cheap to audit. Read-only: no live-path change, no writes outside drafts/. NOT a phase-c build and NOT a cross-venue (Kalshi) proposal — that lane's retirement is untouched.

cards.title: STANDARD exit rule — scope the 168h replay before any change
cards.effort: ~3h replay + decision
cards.dates: Carded 2026-10-20 (profit review 2026-10-20, user-approved 'yes to both')
cards.note:
FINDING (profit review 2026-10-20, reproduced): the ENTIRE stale-exit / capital-recycling block is scoped `botId === "BANKROLL_200"` (scripts/update-pnl.ts:240). STANDARD exits only on market resolution or a dead-slug 404 older than 24h (update-pnl.ts:148-156, lane-agnostic). It has no time exit and no adverse exit, so its hold time is set by market TERM, not by information decay.

CONSEQUENCE: 1,269 open legs = only 357 distinct bets, $13,623 notional, weighted age 76.3 days. Stranded capital-days 1,033,886 vs 566,915 for the ENTIRE finished history — the live book holds 1.8x more capital-days than every trade ever completed. Edge per capital-day over 30d: C-200 $0.3818 (1.70d hold) vs STANDARD $0.0114 (13.89d hold) = 33x. Hold time is INVERTED against edge: cheap band recycles in 4.4d, 0.6-0.8 in 11.2d, 0.8-1.0 in 34.4d. The >=0.8 stock is $5,661 notional holding ~$469 of remaining upside against $5,661 of downside (~12:1 against) at 82 days old.

THIS IS THE SAME SCOPING CLASS AS v63: every band/exit/concentration rail written since v41 was guarded `botId === "BANKROLL_200"`, so the lane carrying 99% of the open book never got one. v63 (2026-10-20) closed the band-skip half; this card is the exit half.

SCOPE FIRST — DO NOT IMPLEMENT OFF THIS CARD. Step 1 is a read-only replay: run `staleExitDecision` at `staleExitHardHours=168` over deduped STANDARD legs, marking each leg at its first `MarketSnapshot` with `collectedAt >= openedAt + 168h` (15.9M snapshot rows available). Output booked PnL and capital-days versus hold-to-settlement, PER BAND. No RuleSet row is touched by the replay.

DECISION RULE (pre-registered): adopt the exit when capital-days fall >=50% while booked PnL falls <$150 over 90d.

REFUTATION (pre-registered): if a 168h exit turns the >=0.8 band from -1.23% to worse than -8%, it is monetising noise on near-certainty tokens and paying fees to do it — the exit is wrong and hold-to-settlement stands.

FRAMING, so this is not sold as profit: the review's own read is that the exit is bought for SOLVENCY, not profit — PnL is ambiguous at +/-$100/90d. At live scale the current book would be ~1.7x gross against cash, i.e. unexecutable. This is a capital-efficiency and risk-shape fix.

LANE A: implementation needs its own approval after the replay. Replay itself is read-only and Lane B-safe.

*** PREMISE PARTLY FALSIFIED 2026-10-20 (measurement, same day as carding) ***
Measured the OPEN STANDARD book (339 distinct markets): latest-snapshot timeToResolution median = 2,766.8h = 115.3 DAYS (p25 2,133h / p75 4,179h), and only 12 of 330 markets (3.6%) have an implied resolution already in the past. Universe baseline over the same 90d is median 64.25h = 2.68d.
WHAT THIS MEANS: the 76-day weighted age is NOT stale capital stranded by a missing exit rule -- it is capital committed to LONG-DATED markets. STANDARD is systematically selecting ~4-month-dated positions and holding them to resolution, which is a strategy signature, not negligence. So the '1,033,886 stranded capital-days' framing overstates the defect: that capital is committed, not stranded, and only ~3.6% of it is in markets that should already have resolved.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS CARD: a 168h exit would liquidate roughly 96% of the open book BEFORE its markets resolve -- that is a deliberate strategy change (sell the 1-week markout instead of the resolution payoff), not a bug fix. The real lever is therefore INSTRUMENT SELECTION (prefer short-TTR markets) rather than an exit rule. The replay below is still worth running because it prices the trade directly, but the pre-registered refutation now looks like the LIKELY outcome: for near-certain tokens the 168h markout forfeits most of the remaining upside that hold-to-resolution captures, so the >=0.8 band should turn sharply worse. Expect this card to close as a recorded NULL, and treat the surviving finding as 'STANDARD should prefer short-TTR markets' -- which is what the ML lane's BTC/short-TTR cohort sequencing is already designed around.

cards.title: FINDING — the 0.8–1.0 band does not survive realistic size; the ML market-only lane is CLOSED
cards.effort: done (measurement, ~1h)
cards.dates: Measured and closed 2026-10-20
cards.note:
This closes the ML bot's market-only thesis on measurement, and it closes it against my own recommendation — I had proposed testing 0.8–1.0 as the one region worth rescuing, and the test says no.

CONTEXT: scripts/ml-market-candidates.py measured 120,884 market-only candidates (both sides, T-24h and T-6h before resolution, labels at ask + fee). Every band lost money except 0.8–1.0, which returned +0.77% with a tight market-clustered CI [+0.5, +1.1] on 38,925 candidates. That was the only statistically solid positive in unselected market entry, so it got a proper test: scripts/ml-near-certainty-read.py.

SUB-BANDS (only two cells clear zero):
  0.80-0.85  2,764   +1.27%  [-0.63, 3.12]   <- spans zero
  0.85-0.90  3,821   +0.47%  [-0.88, 1.81]   <- spans zero
  0.90-0.95  7,368   +1.28%  [+0.62, +1.89]  <- CLEARS
  0.95-1.00 24,972   +0.62%  [+0.36, +1.00]  <- CLEARS, barely

IT DIES ON FILL QUALITY. Premium + fee cost 1.660pp of a 2.434% gross:
  premium x1.0 -> +0.774% | x1.5 -> +0.053% | x2.0 -> -1.645%
A fill 50% worse than the quoted ask erases the edge. No margin for estimation error.

THE ARITHMETIC MEAN IS NOT A RETURN. 97.2% of trades win +3.7%; the 2.8% that lose return -100.0%. Breakeven win rate 96.4%, realised 97.2% => margin +0.7pp. GEOMETRIC mean per trade = -20.4% against arithmetic +0.774%. At full size this compounds to ruin; sized small enough to survive, the absolute return is nil. Classic pennies-in-front-of-a-steamroller distribution.

CAPITAL PRODUCTIVITY IS WORSE THAN THE LANE WE JUST CAPPED. Return per capital-day = mean ROI / mean hold = 0.774% / 28.05d = 0.028%/day = $0.0055 per $20 leg:
  C-200    $0.3818/capital-day  -> this lane is 69x worse
  STANDARD $0.0114/capital-day  -> this lane is 2x worse than the lane v64 is freezing for lack of edge

CAPACITY DOES NOT RESCUE IT: median market liquidity $2,380, median LIFETIME volume $607, p10 volume $59. 404 candidates/day at a $20 leg is $62.57/day gross against ~$14.4K of tied-up capital.

VERDICT: the edge is statistically real, economically immaterial, and destroyed by any fill worse than quoted. The ML lane as a market-only market prediction business is CLOSED.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE -- and it is the important part: WALLET-CONDITIONED SELECTION. The copy book's +47.75% in <0.20 comes from WHICH WALLETS were copied, and that signal demonstrably exists. The lesson is not that prediction is worthless; it is that the edge in this system lives in wallet selection, and a price-only model cannot manufacture it. See the counterfactual contrast: identical <0.20 band, +47.75% with wallet selection vs -50.64% without.

SAMPLING CAVEAT recorded honestly: decision points are the snapshot NEAREST T-24h/T-6h, which for thin markets can land far from target (mean hold 28.05d vs median 1.55d). Tightening the window would sharpen the capital-day figure but would not move the payoff geometry or the x1.5 premium result, neither of which depends on hold time.

cards.title: FINDING — the ML model as a VETO on copy legs is NOT established (non-monotone, CIs span zero)

cards.note:
With market-only prediction closed (card ml-near-certainty-does-not-survive), the ML model's remaining useful job is a VETO on copy legs -- it is wallet-conditioned, and the +47.75% vs -50.64% contrast says the alpha is in WHICH WALLETS get copied. scripts/ml-veto-calibration.py tests that on the time-ordered holdout.

THE RIGHT QUANTITY IS EDGE, NOT PROBABILITY: a high modelled p on a near-certain market is fairly priced, not an opportunity. So the veto fires on EV = p_model - (entry + feePerShare), not on low p.

SAMPLE: 13,776 held-out predictions -> 826 legs joined to finished PaperTrade rows ($8,298 notional). Baseline: PnL $43.38, ROI 0.52%.

THE SWEEP LOOKS GREAT AT ONE POINT AND IS NOISE. PnL by threshold:
  EV>-0.05  $25.84  |  EV>-0.02  -$21.28  |  EV>0.00  $138.12  |  EV>0.02  $313.81  |  EV>0.05  -$165.38
The argmax (EV>0.02) reads +$313.81 against a $43.38 baseline, a +$270 'improvement'. But the curve ZIGZAGS: it falls, rises, rises, then COLLAPSES from +$314 to -$165 as the threshold gets stricter. A real ordering must be monotone -- raising the threshold keeps a strictly better subset. 2 direction changes across 5 thresholds. Picking the peak is curve-fitting to 826 legs.

CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY BY EV QUARTILES (all CIs span zero, and NOT in EV order):
  Q1 [-0.077,+0.005] n=207  +3.93%  [-11.9, +21.6]
  Q2 [+0.005,+0.029] n=206  -4.42%  [-17.9,  +9.8]
  Q3 [+0.029,+0.051] n=206  -5.16%  [-19.4,  +8.9]
  Q4 [+0.051,+0.227] n=207 +11.61%  [ -5.8, +30.5]
Q1 beats Q2 and Q3. EV does not order realised ROI on this sample.

PER-BAND: EV>0 barely moves anything (<0.20 spreads -4.83pp on n=37; 0.4-0.6 -0.35pp on n=385). The only large spread, 0.8-1.0 +17.69pp, rests on n=7.

VERDICT: NO justified veto. I wrote the script's own verdict logic to test monotonicity and refuse the argmax, because the naive reading of this table is exactly the trap I have been avoiding all session.

VALUABLE SIDE FINDING -- INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION OF v63: the held-out 0.4-0.6 band returns -8.97% on 385 legs, with no knowledge of the rule. v63 skips exactly that band in the live lane. Two independent roads to the same conclusion, which is the strongest evidence v63 is right that exists so far.

BLOCKER: n=826 is too small to settle this, and the model's p is refit each run so there is no frozen artifact to rescore history with. Revisit only when the scored-and-settled leg count is far larger; the ml-daily cron accumulates them. Do NOT propose a RuleSet change on the current sample.
