  BANKROLL_200      7 legs      $80.90 open notional  principal 1,900 -> 0.3x under
Portfolio: $13,646.90 open notional vs $7,763.70 cash = 1.76x cash. Realized $15,440.13 on 11,466 finished legs; open unrealized $1,542.32.

REALITY CHECK — IT TAKES C-200 DOWN TOO: isPortfolioGate() matches /drawdown gate|gross exposure cap/, and portfolio gates fire BEFORE the per-bot leg loop. On block the cycle produces no copies, no leg-block reasons and no signal. That is exactly the Sep 16-18 freeze that ran 39.7h undetected and is why isPortfolioGate exists. A C-200-calibrated absolute dollar ceiling extended to a lane holding 168x more notional recreates that failure on purpose.

SECOND FINDING — THE CAP IS NOT WHAT CONSTRAINS C-200 EITHER: C-200 has $7,763.70 cash and $80.90 open notional (1.0% deployed) against a derived cap of roughly $6K (~70x headroom). It has 7 legs because its GATES ARE REJECTING CANDIDATES, not because a ceiling binds. Idle cash there is a FUNNEL problem, not a RAIL problem.

VERDICT: do not port. Either reason alone is sufficient — a 13.6x immediate halt on a 115-day book, or a silent portfolio-gate freeze with a 39.7h precedent.

THE UNPRICED PREREQUISITE: set STANDARD's BotBankroll principal and cashBalance. Until that row is populated every ratio-based rail is undefined for the lane carrying 87% of the book's notional — the cap, any notional-per-cash limit, and any per-lane return-on-capital figure. The lane has no accounting identity, so it cannot be risk-managed by ratio at all. Candidate values (each Lane A, since each sets a ceiling): measured contribution; deposited capital recoverable from scripts/capital-deposits-report.ts history; or a portfolio split by measured edge per capital-day (C-200 $0.3818 vs STANDARD $0.0114) — the third is the only one that makes the rail and the strategy agree, and it is also the largest change so it must not be chosen by default.

cards.title: Re-price archived-market fees off CLOB clob-markets fd: does it move >=$25 or flip a leg's sign? (agent-next approved 10-21)
cards.note:
APPROVED by user 2026-10-21 ('I approve of all 4'). Source: agent-next/polymarket-paper-trader [watch], concept only. HYPOTHESIS: archived markets are fee-priced off a flat/default schedule, and the CLOB `fd` field resolves the real fee for enough of them to change net figures. MEASUREMENT: fetch `clob-markets/{conditionId}` for the archived-market population, read `fd`, re-price fees on those legs, diff against the stored fee. DECISION RULE: `fd` resolves >=90% of conditionIds AND re-pricing moves aggregate fee >=$25 OR flips at least one leg's net PnL sign => adopt as the fee input. REFUTATION: if fd coverage <90% the field is not a usable source and the card closes with that null; if coverage is high but the delta is <$25 and no sign flips, the existing fee model stands. COST ~1-2h. CHEAPEST of the 4 - do this first. All fee numbers ship with the era they apply to (schedule changed ~4x since 2026-01). || PROGRESS 2026-10-21 (scripts/archived-fee-fd-probe.py): THE FIELD THE REC NAMED DOES NOT EXIST. CLOB /markets/<conditionId> carries 30 keys and no `fd`; the real fee fields are `maker_base_fee` and `taker_base_fee`. Coverage gate PASSES on the real fields: 60/60 fetched (0 errors), taker_base_fee non-zero on 59/60 = 98.3% (one market 0), value 1000 on every fee-bearing archived market. A probe keyed on `fd` returns 0/60 and would have CLOSED this card on a FALSE null. || SECOND TRAP, fixed: PaperTrade.marketId is a LOCAL SLUG (demo rows are literally 'demo-market-4-30'), not a conditionId -- feeding it to CLOB 404s 57/60. The real key is ObservedTrade.conditionId via DecisionJournal. || NEXT MEASUREMENT (the >=$25 / sign-flip half of the rule, still open): our fee model is feePerShare = rate*price*(1-price) (peaks 0.50, symmetric); the venue base-fee convention is rate*min(p,1-p) (also peaks 0.50 but LINEAR in min(p,1-p)). At p=0.10 those agree to ~0.1c; at p=0.50 ours is half the venue's. Verify the venue formula against the primary source BEFORE re-pricing, then diff aggregate fee and count sign flips. Do not quote the 1000 value as '10%' -- it is the base-rate numerator, not a per-trade percentage.

--- FEE LAW CONFIRMED FROM IN-REPO DATA 2026-10-22 (was an unverified suspicion): kalshi-pm-btc-pair writes a per-row fee_model = {pm_rate 0.07, pm_law 'rate*min(p,1-p) taker, maker 0', kalshi_rate 0.07, kalshi_law 'rate*p*(1-p) taker, maker 0', pm_feeType crypto_fees_v2}. So SAME rate (7%), DIFFERENT law, and the Polymarket lane's reprice model uses rate*p*(1-p) - i.e. the KALSHI law applied to a POLYMARKET fee. The open question is therefore no longer 'which law' but 'how much this moves', i.e. the existing >=$25 / sign-flip-half test.

--- RESOLVED 2026-10-22 AGAINST THE PRIMARY SOURCE. scripts/fee-sign-flip-test.py, artefact data/fee-sign-flip-report.json. PRIMARY SOURCE (fetched): https://docs.polymarket.com/trading/fees.md -> fee = C x feeRate x p x (1 - p), takers only, makers never charged. Verified against the docs' own 100-share Crypto table: p=0.50 -> $1.75, and 100 x 0.07 x 0.50 x 0.50 = $1.75 exactly. The min(p,1-p) law would give $3.50 for that same trade. Sports table agrees independently (100 x 0.05 x 0.25 = $1.25). Rates: crypto 0.07, sports 0.05, politics/finance/tech/mentions 0.04, economics/culture/weather/other 0.05, geopolitics 0. SO OUR MODEL WAS CORRECT ALL ALONG. The 'venue base-fee convention is rate*min(p,1-p)' belief on this card came from scripts/kalshi-pm-btc-pair-sampler.py, whose header cited an archive calibration; that header, its pm_fee() and the pm_law string it writes into every tape row were all WRONG and have been corrected (Lane B). Quoting that tape's fee_model block as a venue fact was circular -- our own encoding read back as evidence. MEASURED (12,710 legs, $135,290 notional, coverage 99.7%): ours $5,024.02 vs documented $4,996.97 -> DELTA -$27.05, i.e. we OVERCHARGE by $27 (0.02% of notional). 2 net sign flips, both dust: net +$0.0126 -> -$0.0467 and +$0.0004 -> -$0.0120. A FIRST RUN SEEMED TO SAY OTHERWISE (+$9,907 delta, 142 flips) and it was an ARTIFACT: it priced the 'venue' leg as shares x (taker_base_fee/1e4) x min(p,1-p) = 0.10 x min(p,1-p), i.e. 11% of notional. That field is a legacy constant 1000 on ~85% of markets, exactly the trap this card already warned about -- and the live book's +$15.5k realized on 12,676 legs is arithmetically impossible under 5%/side fees. Caught by (a) the card's own warning, (b) a fan-out check (12,750 = 12,750 = 12,750, clean), (c) fetching the primary source. RESIDUAL, NOT A LAW ISSUE: the $27 comes from category assignment only -- Tech is charged 0.05 where docs say 0.04 (-$14.39 on 263 legs), and the slug-keyword fallback sometimes disagrees with the ObservedTrade class taxonomy (politics -$20.38, other +$11.44). VERDICT: the >=$25/sign-flip bar is tripped mechanically (-$27.05, 2 flips), but the substance is the OPPOSITE of the card's hypothesis: there is no fee-schedule mispricing to adopt. RECOMMEND: do NOT change the fee law (already correct); optional micro-cleanup is Tech 0.05->0.04 and preferring the class taxonomy over slug keywords, worth ~$27 on $135k. Nothing applied -- any fee-input change is Lane A.

cards.title: Track 0.20-0.40 Kelly band as UNRESOLVED over a 30-day extension (kelly rec 2, approved 10-21)
cards.note:
APPROVED 2026-10-21 (user 'approved' on copybot-kelly-window-report recs 1-4). Band 0.20-0.40 read n=77, realized -$76, lambda-hat -0.21/-0.158 vs a NEGATIVE realized -> sign flip against the model. At n=77 that is noise-level, NOT a loss. RULE: it is tracked as unresolved for 30 days from 2026-10-21 (to 2026-11-20); do NOT reclassify it as a loss, do not propose a band rule for it, and do not cite it as evidence either way until then. CLOSE CONDITION: at the 30-day read, if the sign flip persists with a CI excluding zero -> the lambda-hat line for that band needs a refit review (Lane A, proposal only). If it resolves toward the model's sign -> retire the flag. REFUTATION: if the band produces n<40 over 30 days there is insufficient data to call it anything and the extension repeats once, then closes as INSUFFICIENT_DATA. Do not re-derive this from the Oct-21 snapshot; it was already read.

--- λ̂↔realized ALIGNMENT PASS RUN 2026-10-24 (read-only, user-approved). This was the 'highest-information lever' the 10-24 kelly report offered INSTEAD of touching kellyFraction; the report's own §6 caveat flagged it as never checked. METHOD: scripts/analyze-calibration.py (own finished trades; excess = win_rate - mean entry price, two-sided z) against data/premium-calibration.json (calibratedAt 2026-10-15, wang-mle). RESULT — the table RANK-ALIGNS with realized outcomes in 5/5 bands once the documented sign convention is applied. λ̂ is the OPPOSITE sign to economic edge BY DESIGN, because the consumer computes q = Φ(Φ⁻¹(p) − λ̂): a negative λ̂ RAISES the fair probability and therefore the edge.   band        λ̂        realized excess   z       realized PnL   agrees   0.00-0.20   -0.7431   +0.1757           +6.28   +$5,959.26     yes   0.20-0.40   -0.1580   +0.0503           +2.41   +$82.59        yes   0.40-0.60   +0.0596   -0.0235           -1.49   -$162.22       yes   0.60-0.80   +0.1969   -0.0688           -3.13   +$10.61        yes   0.80-1.01   +0.2906   -0.0664           -2.14   +$0.12         yes premiumRiskTag() encodes the same convention (lambda <= -0.15 = 'info edge (underpriced)', >= +0.15 = 'overpriced entry'), so the label and the arithmetic agree. The first pass looked like a 5/5 SIGN INVERSION until the convention was read; recording that so the next reader does not file it as a defect. THE TENSION THIS EXPOSES, and why the report's 'do not touch kellyFraction' holds: 0.20-0.40 carries a STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT +5.03pp per-contract edge (z=+2.41) and yet only +$82.59 across 524 legs, because v57 change B caps size in [0.20,0.60) at legacy-equivalent. That cap was itself measured (clip-size split: <=$15 +$149 on 84 legs, $15-30 -$116 on 17, >=$30 -$331 on 8). So the edge is real per CONTRACT while scaling it per DOLLAR was measured harmful — 'add size to 0.20-0.40' is NOT the lever, and pulling it would repeat a measured loss. Nothing proposed. APPROVED STATUS QUO: Kelly fraction 0.5, all caps unchanged. A falsifiable target missed by 15% on n=23 is thin grounds to move caps; concentration 138/138 in <0.40 and drawdown 2.6% vs a 20% gate both cleared with room. Minor label defect noted, not fixed: the report's caveat says 'at the Sep 15 refit' but the artefact is calibratedAt 2026-10-15. Artifact side effect: data/calibration-analysis.json was regenerated; only analyzedAt changed, every number identical (verified by diff). NOT PROPOSED, deliberately: hour-of-day shows 3 of 24 cells at |z|>=2 (08:00 -0.1812 z=-2.26, 20:00 -0.2365 z=-2.82, 14:00 +0.0957 z=+2.21) against ~1.1 expected under the null — noise-consistent, and the band axis has already been retired as an axis. Recorded as an observation, not a lead.

cards.title: Pre-register the single-loss concentration test: per-position cap or concurrent-long-shot limit (kelly rec 4, approved 10-21)
cards.note: APPROVED 2026-10-21 as the TEST only - its own wording gates the rule change on separate approval ('per-position cap or concurrent-long-shot limit is the next test, with your approval'). HYPOTHESIS: the $100 cap binds on every long-shot Kelly position (= 1.3% of net worth per full loss at 7,831 NW), so a cluster of concurrent long-shots can produce a correlated drawdown the current 20% drawdown gate is too coarse to catch. MEASUREMENT: distribution of concurrent open long-shot positions and of per-position loss as a share of net worth; count days where simulated concurrent full-loss exposure exceeded 5/10/15% of net worth; replay against realized outcomes. DECISION RULE: propose a per-position cap or a concurrent-long-shot limit ONLY if the measured concurrent-full-loss exposure exceeded 10% of net worth on >=1 day in the read window, or a single leg lost >1.3% of net worth twice in 30 days. REFUTATION: if concurrent full-loss exposure never exceeded 10% of net worth, the concentration concern is arithmetically unreachable and the card closes with that null - state it and drop it. DO NOT implement any cap without a second approval; this card authorises measurement only.

cards.title: ML observe lane: settle from venue truth (CLOB tokens[].winner), not the last-snapshot price band
cards.note:
PROPOSED 2026-10-22, Lane A (feeds the promotion gate) - NOT applied. Write-up: drafts/ml-settlement-source-20261022.md. DEFECT: ml-observe-read.py derives outcomes from our own last MarketSnapshot with yesPrice>=0.90 / <=0.10, but collection stops while markets are still mid-priced - measured 201/234 (85.9%) of near-resolution markets have a mid last price, so ~1 in 7 ever settles. LIVE PROOF: 6/6 of the soonest observed markets are closed at the venue with a decisive winner (CLOB 200 OK), while observe-report.json reports settled_observations=0. OutcomeReview CANNOT fix this: it has no marketId/conditionId and keys on paperTradeId, so it only covers acted markets. FIX: observe.market_id -> MarketSnapshot.conditionId (46,227 populated) -> GET clob.polymarket.com/markets/{conditionId} -> tokens[].winner; keep --settlement-source=snapshot and compute both for a week. DECISION RULE: adopt only if conditionId+CLOB coverage >=90% of observed markets AND agreement with the proxy >=95% on the decisive overlap. REFUTATION: proxy stands if coverage <70%, or disagreement >5%, or >20% of observed markets lack a conditionId. EFFECT: n>=400 settled moves from ~early December to ~2026-11-01. Does NOT change the §8 bar and opens no positions. Cost ~2h read-only.

--- APPLIED AND VERIFIED 2026-10-22 (approved by user). ml-observe-read.py settles from CLOB tokens[].winner by default; --settlement-source=snapshot and --no-venue-fetch are both tested rollbacks. Result: venue settles 224 observations across 72 markets, the old proxy settles 0, coverage 100% (85/85 conditionId, 85/85 CLOB record), 13 markets not_closed_yet. Every run still computes BOTH sources and reports them side by side; observe-report.json now carries a settlement block and /ml renders the source plus both counts. BUG SHIPPED AND CAUGHT SAME DAY: y was 1 if outcome=='Yes', which marks every named-outcome market (Over/Under, team names) as NO regardless of the winner -- cache gave it away at 63 NO/9 YES, corrected to tokens[0].winner, now 36/36. Two published figures corrected: baseline net ROI +7.982% -> -3.390% (the positive was live on /ml about 2 minutes) and direction agreement 45.8% -> 55.6% (the 'below a coin flip' claim is retracted). Unchanged finding: the last snapshot sits a median 0.075 from 0.50 where the band rule needs 0.40, so it carries almost no resolution information. Cache carries a CACHE_MAPPING tag so a future mapping change is refetched, never trusted. Also split the zero-test path out of NOT_ESTABLISHED: 224 settled but <60/bucket is ACCUMULATING, not a failed test.

cards.title: Step 0 for any Kalshi build: explain Kalshi PnL $0.00 across 721 resolved venue-shadow pairs
cards.note:
OPEN 2026-10-22, read-only, ~1h. kalshi-venue-shadow.jsonl holds 1,281 paired rows, 721 resolved. Across those, Kalshi PnL sums to $0.00 while the Polymarket side sums to $3,216.44, and raw kalshiResolved-vs-won agreement is 335/721 (46.5%). NOT YET CALLED A DEFECT: kalshiResolved and won may encode different things (venue resolved vs our side won), which would make the agreement arithmetic meaningless, and $0.00 may be by design if that arm books quotes rather than positions. But a paired arm producing zero PnL over 721 resolutions is the shape of a silent instrument. RULE: no Kalshi lane may be built until one of those two readings is confirmed, because K2's entire premise is that those pairs measure cross-venue edge. Closes as EITHER 'by design, arm books quotes only' OR 'silent instrument, fixed + re-measured'; if the latter, every pair-derived number published so far gets a caveat.

--- RESOLVED 2026-10-22 (read-only, ~1h). TWO OF MY OWN NUMBERS WERE WRONG, RETRACTED: (1) 'Kalshi PnL $0.00 across 721 resolved pairs' was MY arithmetic - I summed kalshiPnl over 721 rows coercing nulls to 0, but only 2 rows have non-null kalshiPnl; the instrument correctly books only verified pairs and there are two. (2) 'kalshiResolved vs won 46.5% agreement' was meaningless - 'won' is a trade outcome (realizedPnl>0) while 'kalshiResolved' means WE OBTAINED A KALSHI QUOTE (row.kalshiResolved=true; row.kalshiEntry=q.price), not a market resolution; the comparison never meant anything. THE REAL FINDING IS WORSE THAN A BUG: cross-list coverage is 0.2% (withKalshiQuote=2 of 1,281 copies). Failure buckets: 'no open Kalshi event matched question (scored 0.00 over 25 pages)' 657, 'kalshi orderbook empty for event' 59, 'stale_first_sighting >6h' 35; summary reports quoteFailures 790, staleSkips 395, unverifiedMatches 94 (low match score 0.60-0.67 = matcher guessing). The job's own NOTE already said it: the binding constraint is matcher coverage, not the delta. CONCLUSION: the venue-shadow book cannot support a cross-venue study at n=2, and its 94 'matches' are low-confidence guesses. CLOSED as 'by design + coverage-blocked', not 'silent instrument'. Reproduce: data/kalshi-venue-shadow-summary.json + kalshi-venue-shadow.ts semantics.

cards.title: Kalshi ML lane: scope done, awaiting K1-vs-K2 decision (K2 = cross-venue mispricing recommended)
cards.note:
SCOPED 2026-10-22, no code written. Doc: drafts/kalshi-ml-lane-scope-20261022.md. CORRECTION OF RECORD: earlier briefs said Kalshi had no lane; the accurate statement is that no ml-* script READS Kalshi. Six Kalshi cron jobs run (shadow 15m, shadow-report 18:30, venue-shadow 15m, tape 15m, macro 60m, pm-pair 15m) with 195MB tape since 2026-10-12, kalshi-macro-quotes 75,278 quotes / 336 markets / 9.7d across 6 macro families, macro-settled 14 rows carrying venue truth (result + expiration_value), venue-shadow 721 resolved pairs, and 92 Kalshi PaperTrade legs (+$27.82). 'No wallets' was never a blocker - the ML lane is market-only by construction. OPTIONS: K1 Kalshi-only model = blocked on CALENDAR not code (tape 10d vs Polymarket's 99,561 rows/29,686 markets; comparable ~2027-01), do not build now. K2 cross-venue mispricing PM-vs-Kalshi = recommended, ~3.5 dev-days, uses data on disk, and is the only lane where Kalshi adds information rather than another book to lose on. K3 macro calibration already runs with its own pre-registered bar (n>=20 settled/family at >=24h and <=6h) at 14 settled - a wait, not a build. K2 PRE-REGISTRATION: median executable edge must exceed round-trip fees AND >=30% of pairs clear fees AND survive ex-top-10 AND survive excluding pairs above median venue_skew_ms. REFUTATION: if median edge is inside the fee band, <30% clear, edge is carried by <10 pairs, the skew control kills it, or the Step 0 zero-PnL question shows the pairs never measured what they appear to, the lane closes. Kalshi fee model must be verified against the venue, not reused from the Polymarket adapter. NEXT: K1 vs K2 decision + Step 0 authorisation.

--- K2 MEASURED 2026-10-22 AND REFUTED ON BOTH FORMS (user authorised 'Step 0, then K2'). (A) ARB FORM, on the structurally-paired source data/kalshi-pm-btc-pair-*.jsonl (17,937 rows / 801 windows, BTC 15m up-down, both venues, per-venue fee laws, venue_skew_ms): median net cost of a COMPLETE pair = A -0.1222 (n=15,834; mean -0.1072; p90 -0.0127; net-positive 0.59%) and B -0.1232 (n=16,185; p90 -0.0108; net-positive 0.78%). Skew control: medians identical either side of median skew (-0.1217 vs -0.1223; -0.1242 vs -0.1216), so latency does not create it. Fails the pre-registered rule twice: median edge far outside the fee band, net-positive share ~0.6% vs a >=30% bar. Absolute AUCs are optimistic (mid-window features vs last-observation labels) but the comparison is fair and is the finding. cards.title: STANDARD minTimeToResolutionHours 2 -> 24 (APPROVED 2026-10-23; shadow 14 d, then flip unless shadow >= +3% on >=150 blocked legs)
cards.note:
APPROVED 2026-10-23 as proposed by profit-recs (commit 656017b, scripts/profit-velocity.py). PRE-REGISTERED RULE, unchanged: build the shadow, run 14 days, then flip live UNLESS the shadow shows >= +3% on >=150 blocked legs. Founding measurement: STANDARD buys 38% of legs (40% of finished notional) in markets resolving within 24 h and that block returns -13.0% on 3,395 legs CI [-21.8,-4.0]; >24 h earns +24.7% on $60,519. Marginal, on the bands v63 still leaves open: -$1,303 all-time (-6.0%) and -$1,528 over 90d (-9.1%) — only the marginal number is a decision. Expected: book +27.43 -> +30.99 $/1k-capital-day; implied capital for $5k/day $182k -> $161k. REFUTATION: shadow >= +3%; OR the flat 0.6-1.0 cells widen to >= +10% on 150 forward legs; OR 3-7d ex-top-10 falls below 0% on 60d. C-200's short-TTR lane self-rescues at src/lib/scoring/trade.ts:239-247 and is untouched. NOTE the code default is already 12 (src/lib/rules.ts:286); the live RuleSet is the outlier at 2. STATUS: shadow not yet built — next build in this lane.

--- SHADOW BUILT 2026-10-23, AND IT EXPOSED A DEFECT IN THE APPROVED RULE. scripts/ttr-floor-shadow.py (read-only) + data/ttr-floor-shadow.json + cron e4dd4573fefe (daily 07:20, no_agent, silent while ACCUMULATING, speaks only on an actionable verdict). INSTRUMENT CALIBRATED FIRST, because a shadow that cannot reproduce the study it is shadowing is an instrument defect: replaying the band over all history returns 3,396 legs at -12.95% and a kept band of +24.67% on $60,518.80, against the study's -13.0% on 3,395 legs and +24.7% on $60,519. Match to the digit. THE DEFECT: the approved rule says 'shadow 14 days, flip unless >= +3% on >=150 blocked legs', but the two halves are incompatible. Measured properly over the last 14 days, STANDARD opened 76 legs, 60 of them in the 2-24h band = 4.29 openings/day. Fourteen days therefore yields ~60 band legs, NOT 150. Reaching n=150 needs ~35 days, before settlement lag. So the day-14 trigger cannot fire, and a shadow that quietly runs for 14 days would produce a NULL rather than the decision it was approved to produce. (A first version of this script reported 0.9 legs/day and a 167-day ETA -- that was MY arithmetic error: it divided SETTLED legs by elapsed days on a cohort one day old, which has barely begun to settle. Fixed to use openings as the denominator, hoisted above the decision block it feeds. Report it as an instrument bug, not a throughput finding.) THE THREE WAYS OUT, none applied: (A) n-driven window, RECOMMENDED -- run until n>=150 settled (~35-45 days with settlement lag), then apply the identical rule. Preserves the pre-registered n; costs calendar, no risk. (B) Flip now on the historical 3,396-leg read with a forward kill-switch -- revert if the band reaches >= +3% at n=150. Banks +$1,303 all-time / +$1,528 (90d) immediately, but the risk is symmetric with the gain by the proposal's own arithmetic (marginal CI upper +6.7% ~= -$1,462 if wrong), which is precisely why a shadow was proposed in the first place. (C) Lower n to ~60 to keep the 14-day window -- POST-HOC weakening; at n=60 the CI cannot separate -13% from zero, so it would launder a weak result into a pass. Not recommended. The live floor is STILL 2. Nothing has changed what the bot decides.

--- OPTION A ADOPTED (user, 2026-10-23): n-driven window, commit 8b58687. The day-14 clause is RETIRED, not reinterpreted — at 4.29 band openings/day it could only ever have yielded ~60 legs, so the approved rule's two halves could never both be satisfied. The trigger is now n >= 150 settled band legs with no calendar deadline. Projection fixed in the same commit: the ETA divided by days-since-approval, a 2-leg sample on a one-day cohort, projecting ~84 days against a true ~35. Rate now comes from a fixed trailing 14-day window (4.29 band openings/day => ~35 days to n=150, before settlement lag). Cron e4dd4573fefe (daily 07:20, no_agent) stays silent while ACCUMULATING and speaks only when the verdict becomes FLIP / REFUTED / INSUFFICIENT. Calibration re-verified unchanged after every edit: 3,396 legs at -12.95%, kept band +24.67% on $60,518.80. LIVE FLOOR STILL 2 — no rule, threshold or size changed by any of this.

--- IMPLEMENTED AND ACTIVATED 2026-10-23 as RuleSet v66. FIRST: the premise had to be checked, and it changed the job. 'Carry' implied an existing STANDARD stale exit to rescope, but there was none — the v33 hard max-age is gated `botId === "BANKROLL_200"` in scripts/update-pnl.ts and no STANDARD rule field existed. So this was a BUILD, not a scope edit. WHAT SHIPPED: roles.ts fields standardStaleExitHours (0 = disabled) + standardStaleExitBandMin (0.60); src/lib/paper.ts standardStaleExitFires() as a SEPARATE function from staleExitDecision (the C-200 rail is unconditional with a tier-1 adverse cut; folding STANDARD into it would let a future C-200 edit silently change what STANDARD exits on); a STANDARD branch in update-pnl.ts; scripts/apply-v66.ts. The band floor is an ENTRY-price test, not a live-mark test — a mark-based scope would let a winner drift into scope after the fact, which is the lookahead the scope exists to avoid. SCOPE AMBIGUITY RESOLVED BY THE DATA, NOT BY CHOICE: 10-22 said '>=0.60' and also 'exempt <0.40', which leaves 0.40-0.60 undefined. v63 already skips 0.40-0.60 on STANDARD, so no leg can reach the exit there — the scope is >=0.60 and nothing else. Do not widen downward: 0.20-0.40 destroys $1,064 on 135 legs. POPULATION CHECK BEFORE ACTIVATION: the dry run found 701 open legs / $7,321.20 notional, which is the same 701 / $7,321 the 10-22 study measured at >=0.60 — the predicate reproduces the measurement. These clear on the next update-pnl cron run (a STOCK clearing, not a flow change). TESTS: tests/standard-stale-exit.test.ts, 13 cases (disabled-by-default, 0/-5 never close, 167.9 vs 168 inclusive, floor 0.60 inclusive, 0.5999 out, the whole cheap band out, NaN out, C-200 untouched). 517/517 pass, tsc clean. cards.title: Floor the C-200 long-shot band multiplier at 0.05 (v67)
cards.note:
IMPLEMENTED AND ACTIVATED 2026-10-24 as RuleSet v67 (profit-recs #1, user-approved). THE DEFECT: mapBankroll200Size applied the long-shot multiplier to `entryPrice < 0.20` with NO lower bound, and applyKellyBandRails then did Math.max below 0.20 so Kelly could not shrink a long-shot back down — the code was written to protect the ruleset's largest factor (3.5x). Biggest factor, smallest prices: the book put its biggest clip on its longest odds. WHAT SHIPPED: rules.ts c200LongshotBandFloor (0 = no floor, so landing the code changes nothing); paper.ts mapBankroll200Size gates the multiplier on `entryPrice >= longshotFloor`; both score-trades.ts call sites pass it, INCLUDING the Kelly rail's legacy-equivalent — without that second pass, applyKellyBandRails' Math.max would rail a sub-0.05 leg right back up to the 3.5x size it was just exempted from. scripts/apply-v67.ts. tests/longshot-floor.test.ts, 9 cases (526/526 pass, tsc clean). SCOPE CORRECTION — the proposal said 'both lanes' and that is wrong. mapBankroll200Size is reached only under `botId === "BANKROLL_200"` in openPaperTrade, so STANDARD's sub-0.05 legs never received the 3.5x. Measured decomposition below 0.05 (settled, isDemo=0): C-200 31 legs / $1,500.92 / MAX CLIP $100.00 / avgP 0.0396 vs STANDARD 37 legs / $312.60 / max clip $10.60. So the '$25.66 clip, largest in the book' is a BLENDED average across lanes; the real exposure is C-200's $100 clips at ~4%, and STANDARD's 46 open legs at 0.0029 are $375 total with a $9.40 max clip — not the problem and never boosted. There is nothing for this floor to do on STANDARD; an admission floor there would be a different, unmeasured rule and was NOT implemented. CURRENT HOLDINGS: C-200 has 0 open legs below 0.05, so this is PREVENTIVE — no stock clearing, no PnL booked by activating. The proposal's 'removes the $100-at-0.002 exposure' is a capability removal, not a release of existing positions. REVERT: c200LongshotBandFloor -> 0. Refutation stays binding: blocked sub-0.05 candidates win >=3 of 60 forward (>=5%), or 0.05-0.20 truth ROI <0% on a 60d read. NOT DONE (not approved): #2, moving the cell to 0.15-0.20 at 4.5x.
